paragraphs.text: "The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah:" [1].

This statement is regarded as an introduction to the whole book, which contains a collection of visions and prophecies revealed to Isaiah in various circumstances: in the days of Uzziah the Great, Jotham the good king, Ahaz with his dark reign, Hezekiah and Manasseh, and so on... Yet he calls them all a "vision," because although they are different visions, they represent one unity, with one goal: God's declaration of His thought, His will and His plan of salvation, for the building up of the holy congregation, or for the sanctification of mankind who believe in Him.

The visions here are not dreams that the prophet enjoyed during his sleep, but divine revelations presented to the prophet while he was awake, while his senses were still because of their limitation and inability, so that the prophet may say with St. John the Seer: "I was in the Spirit" (Rev 1:10). Perhaps by "vision" is meant the divine inspiration proper to prophecy.

These visions are "concerning Judah and Jerusalem," that is, they concern the kingdom of Judah or the southern kingdom (Judah and Benjamin), and they focus on the capital, Jerusalem, as the city of God in which is His holy temple; but they also included prophecies about the northern kingdom (the rest of the tribes) and about the neighboring kingdoms that had a relationship with the people.

These visions are the word of God, which does not touch Judah in the eighth century B.C. alone, but touches the life of every person who longs for the salvation of his soul and for enjoying fellowship with God, as it is written in the Book of Deuteronomy: "The LORD our God made a covenant with us in Horeb. The LORD made not this covenant with our fathers, but with us, even us, who are all of us here alive this day" (Deut 5:2-3)... It is God's word and His declarations to every human soul!
"Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: for the LORD hath spoken, I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me" [2].
The book begins with a great trial whose two parties are God and man, in which lifeless nature, heaven and earth, is summoned to witness this trial.

Perhaps the prophet Isaiah summoned nature as the prophet Moses had done before: "Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth" (Deut 32:1). It is as though Isaiah were assuring his people that what he utters is an extension of the words of the prophet Moses, in whom every Jew takes pride. Perhaps he wanted to stress how hard man's heart is and how blind his insight, and therefore he summons lifeless nature to bear witness against him, a matter that his contemporary, the prophet Micah, made clear: "Hear ye, O mountains, the LORD'S controversy, and ye strong foundations of the earth: for the LORD hath a controversy with his people" (Mic 6:2).

Perhaps this summons was made by an angel on behalf of the Lord, to bear witness against man in the hardness of his heart. Or perhaps the Lord Himself made this summons, since He did not summon His holy temple or His Law to testify against them, but asked for lifeless nature, which fulfilled God's purposes and accomplished its mission by submitting to Him, while man became utterly corrupt because of his disobedience.
St. John Chrysostom says: [It is now fitting to summon heaven (as witness), since there is no man who hears and bears witness to these things.]

St. Clement of Alexandria sees that God summons the Gnostics, that is, the believers who possess heavenly divine knowledge (heaven), just as He summons those whose hearts are occupied with temporal and earthly things.
"I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me" [2].

God does not bear human feelings, yet He is not a lifeless being; rather, He is "Love" itself, unique in His love for His heavenly and earthly creation, especially His love toward man. Therefore, when He speaks with us human beings, He speaks to us in our human language, expressing His love as though with human feelings, so that we may touch Him and experience union and fellowship with Him.

God knows that nothing can grieve a man and make him lose the taste of life like the feeling that he has failed in raising his children, especially if they rise up against him declaring rebellion against him. With the vast difference, God reveals His feelings toward fallen man: he is a beloved son, to whom his heavenly Father offers every possibility of a transcendent life, but he meets love with rebellion.
He called His people "My firstborn son" (Ex 4:22), and so He calls us His children, for we did not receive the spirit of bondage but the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father (Rom 8:15).

God expects us to bear the spirit of sonship that responds to God's unique, tender fatherhood, which cost Him much, offering His only-begotten Son as a sacrifice to acquire us for Himself as children in the waters of Baptism. St. Gregory the Theologian says: [Like a good shepherd You sought after the lost one; like a true father You labored with me who had fallen.]

St. Cyprian speaks to us about our duty as children of God toward their Father, saying: [If we are children of God, if we have indeed begun to be His temples, if we receive His Holy Spirit, we must live in holiness and spirituality.]

God reproaches His children for their rebellion, for the rebellion of sons is more bitter than the rebellion of hired servants and slaves, and the wounds of loved ones, especially sons, are harsher than those caused by enemies.

St. Irenaeus sees that God created man as His son who imitates Him and fulfills His divine will toward him, but when he glorifies God and accepts the counsel of the enemy of good, he becomes a son of the devil. For this reason the Lord Christ called those who opposed Him "sons of the devil" (Jn 8:44), and denied that they had a spiritual descent from Abraham (Jn 8:39).

* According to nature, that is, by creation, we are said to be sons of God, since we are all His creation. But as regards obedience and teaching, we are not all sons of God; only those who believe in Him and fulfill His will are (sons). Those who do not believe and do not obey His will are the sons of Satan and his angels, because they do the works of Satan.

St. Irenaeus * When the Pharisees persecuted our Lord and Savior, He wept because of their coming destruction. They mistreated Him, but He did not repay them in kind, nor even with a threat; even when they treated Him with contempt and killed Him, He on the contrary grieved over their audacity... All these things were before their eyes in the Holy Scriptures, for the Psalmist prophesied, saying: "Strange children have worked vanity against me" (Ps 18:45). And Isaiah said: "I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me" (Isa 1:2). They were no longer the people of God or a holy nation, but became the rulers of Sodom and the people of Gomorrah (Isa 1:10). They exceeded the sin of the people of Sodom, as the prophet prophesied: [Sodom shall be justified before you] (cf. Ezek 16:48; Lam 4:6). For the people of Sodom resisted angels, but this people attacked the Lord of all, the God of all and their King; they dared to kill the King of angels, and did not know that the Christ whom they killed lives to this day.
Pope Athanasius the Apostolic
"The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider" [3].

If God called Israel His firstborn son (Ex 4:22), it was fitting for the son to know his Father, to perceive His mysteries, and to respond to His purposes and will; but through his disobedience man sank down to something lower than the dumb animals. As St. John Chrysostom says, man sank to something lower than the animal, so the Lord Christ took our nature and ascended into the heavens to raise our nature to what is heavenly.
Man has sunk so low that it is said in the Book of Proverbs: "Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise" (Prov 6:6).

The ox and the ass are known for their stupidity when compared with the rest of the animals, and yet, when they are hungry, they go by instinct to their master at the place of food, as though asking him to let them eat. But Israel, whose life was embittered by captivity, became hungry and naked, and yet did not return to God, its Father, who cares for it and attends to it. What the animals practice by instinct surpassed the conduct of rational man in his wickedness!

If man has sunk so low, below the animal, then the Word of God incarnate was born in a manger, so that when man draws near, as to the manger, he finds the Lord Christ as food for him. He eats, and his insight is opened to perceive the mysteries of God through his union with the only-begotten Son, who knows the mysteries of His Father, for He says: "neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him" (Mt 11:27).

Here is a divine call addressed to us, whom the Lord Christ acquired by His blood, and whose souls He fed with His Body and Blood; therefore it is fitting for us to listen to His words and respond to His call.

St. John Chrysostom compares the Jews in the Old Testament with the believers in the New Testament with regard to the knowledge of God, saying that the former knew God in their thought but not in their life, experience and works (Tit 1:16).
* Their error is not in their (mental) ignorance but in their wickedness, in their evil will, for even when they knew it, they chose to be ignorant.
* Before the Cross even the Jews did not know (the Father), for it was said: "Israel doth not know," but after the Cross the whole world ran to Him.

St. John Chrysostom * Without doubt the mystery of the Kingdom of Heaven was hidden in the Old Testament, and it had to be revealed in the fullness of time in the New Testament. The Apostle says: "for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ" (1 Cor 10:4)... Christ Himself was symbolized to them by the rock, but to us He was declared in the flesh.

St. Augustine * How can you not consider it a terrifying thing, if those who know God (in the mind) did not recognize the Lord (at His coming), while the two stupid animals, the ox and the ass, know who feeds them, and Israel was found to be more stupid than they?!
St. Clement of Alexandria * They crowned Jesus and lifted Him up, bearing witness to their ignorance.
St. Clement of Alexandria

entries.section: 4. A description of the people's condition:

paragraphs.text: 4 Woe to the sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters! They have forsaken the LORD, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backward. 5 Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. 6 From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment. 7 Your country is desolate, your cities are burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers. 8 And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city. 9 Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.
After summoning lifeless nature and the irrational animals to witness God's trial with man, He disclosed the condition to which the people had come, like a bill of indictment, which said:

First: He described them with seven traits in [4], as though He were saying with the prophet Amos: "For three transgressions of Judah, and for four... For three transgressions of Israel, and for four" (Amos 2:4, 6). The three signify the inner sins of the soul, which is in the image of the Trinity, and the four signify the outward sins of the body, which was taken from the earth (the four quarters of the world). It is as though the people had been defiled within and without, by hidden and visible sins, in body and spirit.

The first four traits here signify the visible bodily sins: "Woe to the sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters"; and the last three traits represent the inner sins: "They have forsaken the LORD, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backward."
In any case, the number 7 signifies "Completeness," as though their sins had reached the full measure.
It is observed that Isaiah is fond of the number 7, for he often presents 7 traits in setting out different matters.
The bill of indictment came declaring these sins, which are summarized as follows:

A. Collective sins: "Woe to the sinful nation" [4]. If the sin of Achan the son of Carmi caused destruction to the people (Josh 7:11), how much more if the whole nation turns aside to evil?! Corruption had crept into the priests as into the people, into the nobles as into the common folk, so there was need of a collective return to God, as the people of Nineveh did. This people was called "the holy nation," but it isolated itself from the Holy One and bore the trait "sinful nation," using the Hebrew word goi, an expression particular to the Gentiles because of their not clinging to God. It is as though this nation had turned aside from its purpose to enter the ranks of the nations foreign to God.

B. The weight of their iniquity: "a people laden with iniquity" [4]. Since the prophet Isaiah prophesies about the Savior and salvation, he had to bring out the weight of the sin under whose burden souls are bowed down... God alone knows the weight of this iniquity, for the Word of God came incarnate, the Lamb of God who taketh away the sin of the world (Jn 1:29, 36).

Under the weight of sin the soul is bowed down until it sinks as in the waters of the world, and so it bears the nature of the world, not of heaven. Therefore it is said of Pharaoh and his army: "they sank as lead in the mighty waters" (Ex 15:10), and it is said of wickedness: "and he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof" (Zech 5:8).

St. Gregory of Nyssa sees that the man who walks in the virtuous life is light in weight spiritually, while the wicked man is heavy and sinks in the waters. Virtue is light and makes man like a cloud rising upward, and like a dove that flies on its small wings (Isa 9:8). Origen spoke at length about this, showing how Peter nearly drowned because of sin (doubt), and when the Lord gave him faith he walked on the waters.

C. Rooted in evil: "a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters" [4]. Sin crept into the life of their forefathers, so the generations came rooted in evil from their fathers and grandfathers. As the Lord said to the scribes and Pharisees: "Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers. Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers" (Mt 23:32-33).

D. Their forsaking of the Lord, the source of holiness: "They have forsaken the LORD, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backward" [4]. There is nothing worse than for a man to forsake his God, the source of his life and the secret of his holiness. The Lord says through Jeremiah: "For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water" (Jer 2:13).

If Isaiah saw the holy God (Isa 6), He is the "Holy One of Israel," the source of the sanctification of His believers, granting us His traits working in us! The prophet repeated this expression 20 times.

entries.section: 4. A description of the people's condition:

paragraphs.text: E. An incurable disease: "Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wound and bruise, and a fresh stroke that has not been pressed nor softened with oil" [5-6].

By saying: "Why should ye be stricken any more?!" God declares that this people had rejected sonship to God, and therefore was no longer worthy to be the object of God's concern and discipline. He had already disciplined them as His sons, but they revolted more and more, so He wishes to stop the fatherly disciplines, leaving them to receive the fruit of their natural corruption, for He says: "My people would not hearken to my voice; and Israel would none of me. So I gave them up unto the hardness of their hearts, and they walked in their own counsels" (Ps 18:11-12). And it is written in Jeremiah: "Wherefore will ye plead with me?... In vain have I smitten your children; they received no correction" (Jer 2:30), "I have stricken them, but they have not grieved; I have consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction" (Jer 5:3).

Now God leaves them to their corruption, which they chose by their own will, so that disease creeps into their body from the head to the heart to the foot. It creeps into the mind so that they become unable to manage, and also into the heart so that their inner affections and feelings are defiled, and down to the feet from below so that they become unable to move toward God on the royal way of His Kingdom. Corruption crept into the leaders and great men (the head), as into the servants and priests (the heart), and into the common people (the body), even into the despised among them (the sole of the foot).
The wounds became deadly and the bleeding does not stop... There is no one who moves to rescue and save, and no one who offers the oil of love to soften the harsh stroke!
Corruption struck human nature itself, as St. Cyril of Jerusalem says:
[Great is the wound of human nature; from the foot to the head there is no soundness in it.]

entries.section: 4. A description of the people's condition:

paragraphs.text: F. Complete desolation: "Your country is desolate; your cities are burned with fire, your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers. And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city" [7-8].

The prophet speaks here of what would befall Judah after the invasion of Sennacherib the Assyrian, counting what would befall them in the future as though it were present, because it was bound to happen.

St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [Isaiah lived about 1000 years ago, and he saw Zion as a shelter (for cattle); the city at that time was standing and beautiful in its public benefits and clothed with greatness... But he says: "And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage (a shelter for cattle) in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers." Now we find the place full of cucumber planting. See how the Holy Spirit enlightens the saints.]

The land that flows with milk and honey, the Promised Land that God gave to His people, for whose sake the people endured walking in the wilderness for forty years, became desolate. Sennacherib seized 46 fortified cities, so Jerusalem was under direct threat of danger, "as a besieged city" and "as a lodge" or "cottage" that is easy to occupy... Its inhabitants saw what the strangers (the Assyrians) did to their cities, setting fire to them, and the fire consumed their produce before their eyes while they were unable to move. Their cities became desolate, as overthrown by strangers, that is, as Sodom and Gomorrah were overthrown before, or as if a violent flood of water had flooded over them and shattered them.

This desolation that came is a sign of the iniquities Judah had committed, and a natural necessity of their forsaking God their Sanctifier, their turning back from Him, and their not obeying His voice, for it was said: "But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God, to observe to do all his commandments... that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee: Cursed shalt thou be in the city, and cursed shalt thou be in the field" (Deut 28:15-16).

So every soul that does not cling to God its Sanctifier, desolation comes upon all its cities: upon body, soul, mind and heart with all the feelings and emotions, and so on... Every fortification is taken away from it, and it becomes like a cottage or a tent in the open, an easy prey in the hands of sin.

* These are those who defile themselves and turn them from being the house of the heavenly Father, the holy Jerusalem, the house of prayer, into a den of thieves... They take from it what is precious, and plunder from it the best it has so that it becomes as nothing.

Origen The expression "is left" of the daughter of Zion here points to the position of the people of God, whom He counted as His own people, the virgin daughter and the pampered bride, who has become forsaken, "left alone"; she feels isolation (Loneliness) and abandonment, and this is the harshest punishment upon a human soul! The daughter of Zion brought this punishment upon herself. She was a pampered bride and became abandoned and divorced. Origen says: [I think that the Husband (God) wrote a bill of divorce for His former bride, and gave it into her hand, and sent her out of His house.]

entries.section: 4. A description of the people's condition:

paragraphs.text: In the midst of this complete desolation God finds a small faithful remnant that bears witness to Him, for whose sake He did not destroy His corrupted people, for it was said: "Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah" [9]. The Apostle Paul quoted this statement in (Rom 9:29). It is as though what happened in the days of Isaiah is repeated in all generations, even in the apostolic age, when a faithful few of the Jews accepted faith in the Lord Christ.

God does not care for great numbers but for the small remnant that is sanctified to Him in the midst of the corruption that overtakes the many. This remnant is the "little flock" to whom it is the Father's good pleasure to give the Kingdom (Lk 12:1); this remnant the Lord of hosts left for Himself as His own work, granting it His Holy Spirit to sanctify it to Him, so that it becomes a holy leaven that leavens the whole lump.

* See that you belong to the chosen few, and do not walk in coldness imitating the slackness of many; live as the few, so that you may be made worthy with them to enjoy God, because many are called, but few are chosen (Mt 20:16).

St. John Cassian For the sake of this small remnant God shortens the days of tribulation, especially in the last times, for it is said: "but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened" (Mt 24:22).
"Hear the word of the LORD, ye judges of Sodom! Give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah:" [10].

With courage, without fear or flattery, Isaiah calls the judges of the people "judges of Sodom" and gives the people themselves the title "people of Gomorrah," because of the injustice and corruption that marked both the rulers and the ruled.
In the whole book we find not one situation in which the prophet feels fear or weakness except at his seeing the Lord Christ in His glory (Isa 6), for Isaiah fears God, not men.
He sees that the only cure for the judges, as for the people, is the word of the Lord and His Law.

11 To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the LORD: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats. 12 When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this at your hand, to tread my courts? 13 Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; the new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with; it is iniquity, even the solemn meeting. 14 Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth: they are a trouble unto me; I am weary to bear them. 15 And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.

The accusation directed at them here is extremely serious; for He did not ascribe to them atheism or the practice of idol worship, but ascribed to them hypocrisy; they practice the worship of God with great precision and with a deadly literalism; they offer many sacrifices and offerings and keep the feasts, while their hearts are far from God and their lives are corrupt.

This accusation is directed against those who profess faith throughout all generations, who keep the letter while ignoring the inner spirit, as it was said to the angel of the Church of the Laodiceans: "Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked" (Rev 3:17), because he imitated the Pharisee who said: "God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess" (Lk 18:11-12).

This accusation moved the Fathers of the Church to disclose the purpose of worship in the life of the Church, whether in the New Testament or the Old, and the obligation not to deviate from this divine purpose:
A. St. Irenaeus says: [God shows that He has no need of anything (Isa 1:11); He only urges them and counsels them to practice these things so that man may be justified and draw near to God.]

God wants us, through our worship, to draw near to Him and be united with Him so that we bear His nature in us, the nature of love and mercy. For He desires mercy, and not sacrifice (Hos 6:6; Mt 9:13). Therefore He rebukes the Jews, saying that they spread forth their hands for prayer with importunity but are not heard, because their hands are full of blood through committing murders (Isa 1:15); instead of love they bore hatred and the killing of souls and bodies, especially the killing of the prophets and those who spoke the word of truth.

* Why these divisions? Because we keep the feast but with the leaven of malice and wickedness, and so we divide the Church of God into parts, keeping what concerns its outward matters while excluding the better things: faith and love. We have heard from the prophetic words that such feasts and fasts do not please the Lord.

St. Irenaeus * It is clear to everyone that the piety that leads to worship and honor is the oldest and greatest of causes, and that the Law itself urges justice and teaches wisdom... by calling to the Creator of the world and its Father.

St. Clement of Alexandria B. They offered many sacrifices and burnt offerings in the temple of the Lord, and chose the fatlings, but God is not pleased with them, for He did not ask for the sacrifices in themselves, because He has no need of them, but asked for them as a symbol of the unique sacrifice of the Lord Christ, for the reconciliation of man with God and his enjoyment of fellowship with Him. But the goal was lost to them, for when Christ the Sacrifice came they rejected Him; they offered animal sacrifices and celebrated the feast of the Passover and denied the true Passover, the Lamb of God who taketh away the sin of the world.

* In the days of the Lord the Jews thought that they were celebrating the Passover, but they did this in vain because they persecuted the Lord. By their own testimony the Passover no longer bore the name of the Lord, for it was called the Passover of the Jews (Jn 6:4), not the Passover of the Lord... because they denied the Lord of the Passover.

Pope Athanasius the Apostolic * All these (sacrifices) were abolished so that the new Law of our Lord Jesus Christ might be fulfilled, which He fulfills not under the yoke of obligation (but by His will, since He offered Himself as a ransom).

Epistle of Barnabas C. They used to gather to celebrate the weekly feasts (the sabbaths), the monthly and the yearly feasts, which the Lord counted as His own feasts, in which He was pleased because He gathers with His people and fills them with His divine joy.
These assemblies became a burden to God, and His soul hated them (Isa 1:14), so He no longer counts them as His assemblies.

* The Lord did not ascribe (these practices that they kept) to Himself but counted them as the works of sinners (since they are hateful to Him), whether the new moons or the sabbaths or the great day or the fasts or the feasts.

In the Law concerning the sabbath we read in the Book of Exodus: "... To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the LORD"... "Eat that to day; for to day is a sabbath unto the LORD" (Ex 16:23, 28).

Origen D. In more than one place God assures His people that when He brought them out of the land of bondage He did not give them laws concerning sacrifices (Isa 1:12), lest they think that He brought them out out of a need for their worship or their offerings; rather, that they themselves might enjoy Him... Pope Athanasius the Apostolic says that God wanted to draw them away from the idols and attract them to Himself, giving them the laws at the proper time (after their exodus); and yet they forgot God, who had worked wonders with them in Egypt, and went back to worshiping the calf (Ex 16:3). The laws concerning sacrifices came after they received the Law, so that they would not offer them to idols but to the true God. What was required of them was to learn first to abandon the idols and to care for God's commandments, and after that to offer sacrifices (Jer 7:22).
* He does not accept sacrifices from you, nor did He command you first to offer them out of need for them, but because of your sins.

St. Justin Martyr E. He says: "who hath required this at your hand, to tread my courts?!" [12]. They multiplied their entering into the temple to offer sacrifices without number, and God saw them, in their lack of repentance, as like the animals that trample His house and defile it! The offering of sacrifices turned from reconciliation with God into the pouring out of God's wrath.

They came with offerings like incense, which symbolizes prayer, but since they gave the Lord the back and not the face (Jer 2:27), their incense became an abomination to the Lord, because it carried the smell of their hypocrisy and their lack of repentance.

* Works that are done in a way contrary to the will of God, or that are offered without fitting reverence, profit nothing... God has no need of anything, since nothing makes Him unclean! He has reached the end because of their conduct, full of hypocrisy [11].

Pope Athanasius the Apostolic * The Lord our God is not pleased with the keeping of such things; if there is found among you a man who breaks his oath, or a thief, let him cease from this; and if there is found an adulterer, let him repent; and then he keeps the sweet and true sabbaths of God. If anyone has unclean hands, let him wash and be purified.
The Martyr Justin

16 Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil; 17 Learn to do well; seek the truth, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow. 18 Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool. 19 If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: 20 But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it.

God exposed them before themselves, showing the ugliness of the corruption that had come upon them, without crushing them with despair or wounding their souls; rather, with heavenly fatherly love He offered them the cure, to cover them and restore them to the good nature in which He had created them. This cure is repentance springing from faith and mingled with love, and its steps are:

A. Washing: by saying "Wash you" [16] He does not mean the ceremonial purifications of the Law, because in His accusation of them He asks that they not stop at the outward form of worship; rather, He means the washing of Baptism, in which we put off the old man in order to bear in us the new man who is in the image of our Creator. This is what the Lord meant by saying to the human soul: "Then washed I thee with water" (Ezek 16:9), as it is written in the same book: "Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness... A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you" (Ezek 36:25-26).

In the Old Testament the priests could not enter the temple unless they first washed, or else they would die (Ex 30:19-21), and the Psalmist says: "I will wash mine hands in innocency: so will I compass thine altar, O LORD" (Ps 26:6). It is an inward washing! St. John Chrysostom says: [He does not mean the washing with water that the Jews practiced, but the washing of the conscience.]

"Make you clean" [16]. If by Baptism we received the new man, we received a new capacity to practice the new life in Christ, which is purity of heart, as a condition for seeing God, for the Lord says: "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God" (Mt 5).

* As you enter the good font of great glory, run with reverence in the race of goodness. For the only-begotten Son of God is present here and ready to save you, saying: "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Mt 11:28). You have put on the coarse garment of your transgressions and have been bound with the ropes of your sins; now hear the word of the prophet: "Wash you, make you clean, and your sins shall be blotted out from before mine eyes," that the choir of angels may sing over you, saying: "Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered" (Ps 32:1). You who light the lamps of faith, keep them in your hands unquenched.

St. Cyril of Jerusalem * So if by the washing (in Baptism), as the prophet says, in that mystical font, our will is purified and evil is removed from our souls, then by this we become better people and reach a better state.

St. Gregory of Nyssa B. "Put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes" [16]. When man receives the purity by which he sees God, he is able to distinguish the works of evil from the divine work, and so he rejects everything that is evil, so that he does not halt between the two ways: God and sin.

Our receiving the sacrament of washing and purification gives us a divine capacity for earnest work in discovering ourselves in the Lord, that we may enter into a continual washing (by repentance) and cleansing from everything of evil that belongs to our inner being... We confess our sins to God and so enjoy continual ascents toward Him until we see Him face to face.
* Behold, you see that it is in your power to deposit in your hearts either ascents, that is, thoughts that belong to God, or descents, that is, thoughts debased toward carnal and earthly things.

Abba Serenus We confess our sins and put away our evil, and so we see God in us declaring Himself and His glory within us. As St. Augustine says: [Show yourself to the One who knows you, and He will reveal Himself to you, who do not know Him.]

"Cease to do evil" [16]. If by true repentance we put away evil from the eyes of the Lord, then the sign of our sincerity toward Him is that we cease completely from every evil deed. This is a divine gift, but it is not granted without being asked for with faith and importunity, with striving and perseverance.

* He desires to give an opportunity for repentance to all His beloved, confirming it by His almighty will. Therefore let us obey His great and glorious will; and as we plead, asking for His mercy and the tenderness of His compassion, leaving every vain work and strife and envy that leads to death, let us return to Him and cast ourselves upon His mercies.

St. Clement of Rome C. "Learn to do well" [17]: the negative side is not enough, that is, removing everything that is evil and always ceasing from it; here there is an obligation to positive work, that we bear in us the trait of Christ who is "the Truth." We seek "the Truth," that is, we seek our living Christ dwelling in us and working through us, practicing the work of Christ, the Lover of mankind, who cares for the oppressed, the needy and the weak. Therefore He commands us: "seek the truth, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow." This is positive repentance, through which we return to God not merely to cease from evil and injustice but to stretch out our hands with practical love and mercy, especially toward the helpless and the widows.

* Would that we all, men and women, might stretch out our hands to them, so that we do not fall under the sorrows of widowhood. Let us care for them, and so prepare for ourselves a great storehouse of tenderness, for the tears of widows can open heaven itself. Would that we might not trample on them so that their misfortunes increase, but help them by every means.
St. John Chrysostom * See how everywhere God reckons works of great mercy, for they stand in favor of those who have erred.

St. John Chrysostom D. Practical love toward the suffering and needy is a natural reflection of our experience with God, who has compassion on us, who does not look down on us but asks for dialogue with Him as His friends. He opens the doors of His mercies before us sinners, saying: "Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool" [18].
This is a plain evangelical call, declaring God's longing for the salvation of every person who accepts fellowship with the Holy One through the Cross.

In His love, although God had confirmed the terrible judgment upon the sons of Judah, He quickly seeks reconciliation. He is not like man, who meets stubbornness with stubbornness and anger with anger, but pours soothing oil on the inflamed wounds, to bring every soul back to Him.

God asks man to enter into dialogue with Him, while we sometimes find some Christian emperors who closed the door before those who had sinned, and sometimes we even find shepherds, and even parents, who bear the same spirit that is foreign to the spirit of God, the Lover of mankind.

God wants to wash the blood of our sins (the scarlet and the crimson) with His pure blood, so that we become like snow in whiteness and like wool in purity (Song 8:5); we become His shining garment as at His transfiguration.

Some see that the word "let us reason together Cheyene" here means that we put an end to arguing, for God knows that man no longer has anything to say because of his sins, which have become visible like the scarlet color that cannot be wiped away; therefore He wished to bring him out of the predicament and open to him the door of divine pardon so as not to wound his feelings... a wonderful divine love!

By His call directed to us to reason together with Him, He asks us to judge ourselves by ourselves, for when we perceive our sins and confess them, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins (1 Jn 1:9). We judge ourselves, so that we are not judged.

* Let no one despair of himself, even if he has reached the extreme of evil, even if he has passed into the habit of doing evil, yes, even if he bears the very nature of evil, let him not fear... Great is the power of repentance, for it at least makes us like snow, we become white as wool, even if sin has ruled over us and dyed our souls.
St. John Chrysostom * He does not recall our evil deserts, but still has compassion on us and urges us to repentance.

* It is within God's authority alone to grant the forgiveness of sins and to accuse us of transgressions, since He commands us to forgive our repentant brothers every day, "and He will forgive us" (Mt 6:14).

St. Clement of Rome E. The sanctity of human freedom: God opens the doors of His love before all but compels no one, for He seeks the human heart as a voluntary offering; He presents the way to him and gives him the capacity to work, and at the same time leaves him the freedom to choose, for He says: "If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: but if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it" [19-20].
* Behold, you see that we must first purify ourselves (that is, bear a holy will), and then God purifies us.
* We are masters; it is within our power to make every member in us an instrument of evil or an instrument of righteousness.

* Man can change suddenly and be turned from earthenware to gold. What concerns virtue and vice is not (compulsory) by nature, but can easily be changed... I know that everyone wishes to fly to heaven from now, but there is need to show the wish by action.
St. John Chrysostom * By saying this [19] He proves that acceptance or refusal depends on us.

St. Clement of Alexandria observes here that the steps of repentance mentioned in [16-17] are seven: two negative steps in verse 16 (washing and ceasing from evil) and five positive steps mentioned in verse 17, which must be practiced.

21 How is the faithful city become an harlot! it was full of truth; justice lodged in it; but now murderers. 22 Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water: 23 Thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves: every one loveth gifts, and followeth after rewards: they judge not the fatherless, neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them.

Here he compares what Jerusalem was before with what she became through her deviation and corruption, in a style full of lament and deep sorrow. The prophet Isaiah is entirely frank, yet he is full of love and affection!

A. Jerusalem was the "faithful city" [21], and she became a "harlot." He likens her to the bride who was faithful to her heavenly Bridegroom, keeping His commandments and declaring His splendor and glory through her life, and who ran after another (idol worship) and was defiled by her spiritual adultery with her lovers (Ezek 16:25, 32, 36). She was a virgin (Isa 37) united with her Bridegroom, the Giver of holiness, but she left Him and united herself with abominations.

* You can say that God the Word left the synagogue of the Jews as an adulteress, parted from it, and took for Himself a wife of harlotry from the Gentiles, because those who were "Zion, the faithful city" became adulterers, while the others became like Rahab the harlot, who received the spies of Joshua and was saved, she and all her house (Josh 6:5).

Origen B. She was "full of truth; justice lodged in it; but now murderers" [21]. She was a dwelling for the Holy One, who is "the Truth" and "Justice"; the Lord lodged in her because He found His rest in her, but she became a dwelling for murderers, therefore the Lord says: "The Son of man hath not where to lay his head" (Mt 8:10; Lk 9:58). When she is holy she says: "My beloved is mine; he shall lodge betwixt my breasts" (Song 1:13); but when she is defiled, her heart "between her breasts" becomes a dwelling place of evil.

C. Falsehood crept into her, so her silver became dross, bearing the shine of silver and its appearance but not bearing the substance of silver or its value. Her wine became mixed with water [22], bearing the color of wine but adulterated with water... This is a picture of attention to the formalities of worship and the literal carrying out of the commandments in outward appearances, without attention to the depths. Our Christ turns water into wine, but the evil one turns wine into water.

Silver signifies the word of God (Ps 12:6), and wine signifies the joy of the Spirit. The formalist holds fast to the word of God, and perhaps keeps it by heart, but he does not bear Christ, "the Word of God," in his heart or in his conduct. He has the appearance of spiritual joy while being far removed from the joyful heavenly life and the fellowship of the angels and saints in the Lord.

Silver signifies the treasures of the rich, and wine signifies love and affection; the formalist in his faith resorts to the wisdom of the world as a deceptive treasure that has the appearance of precious silver while it is dross; and he appears full of love and affection while his heart carries water (without warmth).

St. Irenaeus sees that the elders were accustomed to mixing the wine of God's simple commandments with the water of human tradition, which is contrary to the word of truth. And St. Gregory of Nazianzus says: [We are not like the many who are able to corrupt the word of truth and to mix with water the wine that maketh glad the heart of man (Ps 104:15), that is, to mix our teaching with what is trite and cheap and base and worn out and tasteless.]

D. "Thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves" [23], that is, they eat with the thieves and keep their clothes during the theft. It was fitting for the leaders to manage the affairs of the people and shepherd them, but they turned shepherding into authority and toil; they may not steal, but they leave the enemy of good with his soldiers to rob the people and seize their hearts, while they are indifferent because of their love of authority. They love bribes and material or moral gifts, and do not care for the orphans and widows, because temporal glory occupied them from thinking of them. They turned Jerusalem, "the Church of Christ," into a house of injustice, cruelty and violence.

Instead of the leaders being a living example for the people in submission to the word of God and in practicing the godly life, they became a stumbling block to them. St. Irenaeus says: [From the ages of the Law the scribes and Pharisees began to despise God and not to accept His word, that is, they did not believe in Christ.]

entries.section: 9. The Judge comes forward as a Savior:

paragraphs.text: 24 Therefore saith the Lord, the LORD of hosts, the mighty One of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies: 25 And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin: 26 And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city. 27 Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness. 28 And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together, and they that forsake the LORD shall be consumed. 29 For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired, and ye shall be confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen. 30 For ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water. 31 And the strong shall be as tow, and the maker of it as a spark, and they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them.

Before this hideous picture God does not stand with folded hands, but "the LORD of hosts, the mighty One of Israel" [24] rises as the Commander of the heavenly armies, whose hand is strong with might for the salvation of His people from what has befallen them.
The following is observed here:

A. He called God by three titles [the Lord (Yahweh), the LORD of hosts, the mighty One of Israel]. Some scholars see in this a hidden reference to the Holy Trinity. The Father is the incomprehensible and invisible (Yahweh = I Am), the Word who became incarnate to lead the battle against the enemy of good, granting His soldiers every spiritual victory, and the mighty Holy Spirit who works in the believers to form them in the image of Christ, so that they find for themselves a portion in the bosom of the Father.

entries.section: 9. The Judge comes forward as a Savior:

paragraphs.text: And Jerusalem bore 3 titles: the city of righteousness, the faithful city, Zion redeemed by justice [26-27].

entries.section: 9. The Judge comes forward as a Savior:

paragraphs.text: The wicked were also called by three titles: the transgressors, the sinners, those who forsake the LORD [28].

B. God counts the one who destroys His people a heavy burden (Isa 3:14-15), so He does not cease to resist evil until He rests and His people rest with Him: "I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies" [24].
The bowels of the Lord remain yearning over His people until evil is shattered!

C. "He purges Jerusalem of the dross as with borax (perhaps he means the potash of metals)"; for He recreates human nature to restore to the Church her original beauty, as by the purifying fire of the Holy Spirit.
He also purifies us by discipline, though it appear harsh as fire:
* Blessed is the man who is disciplined in this life, for the Lord does not punish twice for one thing (Nah 1:9) LXX.

* A father does not discipline his son if he does not love him, and a teacher does not set right his pupil unless he sees in him signs of obtaining the promise. When a physician withdraws his care from a patient, it is counted a sign that he despairs of his recovery.
St. Jerome * God rebukes in order to correct, and corrects in order to keep us for Himself.
St. Cyprian D. "And I will restore thy judges as at the first" [26]. For He restores man to his dignity and reason as at the beginning of his creation, so that he is like a wise judge.

E. He restores to Jerusalem, or to the human soul, her title: "the city of righteousness, the faithful city" [26]. For the Church, the new Jerusalem, the city of God, the pillar and ground of the truth, the faithful bride of her Bridegroom, is filled with the redeemed penitents who bear the righteousness of Christ in them; but those who forsake the Lord or reject Him have no place in the true Church and no portion in the heavenly Church. These are filled with shame because they desired the world, the terebinth trees, and counted it their garden, and the world was lost and their hopes were lost.
The world is likened here to the terebinth, because the Jews were accustomed to setting up the worship of Baal and Ashtoreth under the terebinth tree.

entries.section: 9. The Judge comes forward as a Savior:

paragraphs.text: Those who forsake the Lord are likened to the terebinth whose leaf has withered, and to the garden that has no water [29]. Why? God created man as a garden in which the Lord finds his fruit sweet within. All the energies, capacities, feelings and instincts that man bears are divine gifts, like trees planted in a garden watered by the water of the Holy Spirit, so that they bear countless blessings. But if the Spirit is withheld from it, it dries up and is burned with fire, and turns into tow (the refuse of flax) [31], that is, what remains of flax after it is combed, to be used as fuel for fire.
"The things that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem:" [1].

Isaiah's heart was occupied with the people of God (Judah) and with the holy city (Jerusalem); he was filled with sorrow at the state to which things had come, seeing a people struck by corruption and a city whose spiritual temple was being torn down, so that his bowels moaned over it.

Before this pure love God gave him insight and presented him with visions and prophecies to comfort him, and to comfort every soul wounded for the sake of mankind; God presented to him His life-giving Word.
* The (Word) came to (Hosea, Isaiah and Jeremiah) and enlightened the prophets with the light of knowledge, and made them see things which they did not understand at that time.
Origen

entries.section: 2. The mountain of the LORD's house:

paragraphs.text: 2 And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD'S house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it. 3 And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. 4 And he shall judge among the nations, and shall do justice for many peoples: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more. 5 O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the LORD.

What did God offer to Isaiah, wounded in soul? He carried him in the Spirit to the fullness of time to see the new Judah, the Lord Christ, and the new Jerusalem, where the temple of the Lord is built and the Kingdom of God is established in the heart... He sees the holy congregation coming from all the nations and peoples to worship the Lord in spirit and in truth in Jesus Christ, the Savior of the world. Therefore he said: "And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD'S house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it" [2].

Some see that this prophecy was taken by Isaiah from the prophet Micah (Mic 4:1-5), or perhaps both took it from an earlier source. But what prevents the Holy Spirit from granting the same gift, prophecy, to the two prophets and to others, when He finds in them a sincere heart, burning for the salvation and building up of man, and so presents it to Isaiah in the days of Ahaz and to Micah in the days of Hezekiah, to confirm that what the inspiration utters will not fall?

The Lord drew Isaiah's heart to the fullness of time to see the Lord Christ, on whom He Himself establishes His Church, being the Rock of ages, the mountain that the prophet Daniel saw, cut out without hands, which filled the earth (Dan 2:34, 45), the true Rock from which the waters of the Spirit flow to His people (1 Cor 10:4), and upon which the serpent cannot crawl to approach His people.
St. Augustine says: [The mountain, as the prophetic testimony teaches us, is the Lord Himself.]

* There are also mountains that are not known because they stand in certain places on the earth... But this mountain is otherwise, for it filled the whole face of the earth; of it it was said, "shall be established in the top of the mountains," it is a mountain standing above the summits of all mountains, "and all nations shall flow unto it."
Who is unable to perceive what this mountain is?!
Who is this who breaks his head by resisting this mountain?!
Who is ignorant of the city that stands upon the mountain?!
Do not wonder if this city is unknown to those who hate the brethren, for they walk in darkness and know not whither they go, because darkness has blinded their eyes. They do not see the mountain.
I want you not to wonder, for they are without eyes; how? Because darkness has blinded them. Prove it? Because they hate the brethren!

St. Augustine The Lord founded His Church when He was lifted up onto the mountain of temptation (Mt 4:8) to give her the spirit of overcoming and victory over the powers of darkness; He went to the mountain Himself, and as St. Jerome says: [He did not go up as one who is compelled or as a captive, but was led with longing for the battle], and St. John Chrysostom also says: [Satan went to man (Adam) to tempt him, but since Satan cannot attack Christ, Christ went to him.]

He also founded His Church on the mountain of teaching (Mt 5:1), where He gave His people His commandment, the secret of life. And also on Mount Tabor, where He declared His glory and entered with His Church into the very heavens (Lk 9:41), and finally on Mount Golgotha, where she delighted in her Bridegroom, the sacrificed one, the Savior of mankind by His precious blood. On this mountain the Lord stretched out His hands on the Cross to draw all men unto Him (Jn 12:32); therefore the prophet continues, saying: "and all nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem" [2-3].
It is known that the Law was given from Mount Sinai to the Jewish people; therefore he speaks of a new law going forth from Jerusalem, addressed to the whole world.

* This Law is not the property of one nation but of all the nations, for the law of the Lord and His word do not remain in Zion and Jerusalem but spread through the whole world. Therefore the Intercessor Himself says to His fearful disciples: "These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me..." (Lk 24:44-47). This is the universal way of the salvation of the soul which was announced before by the angels and the holy prophets...
* There (in Jerusalem) He told the disciples: "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit" (Mt 28:19).

* It was necessary that (the Holy Spirit) be given after the resurrection of Christ in the same city in which the new Law, that is, the New Testament, begins; for the first Law, which is called the Old Testament, was given on Mount Sinai through Moses, but this one was given through Christ, as was foretold of it: "out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem."
St. Augustine It is observed that this Church, founded on Mount Golgotha and going forth from Jerusalem, bears the power of the Holy Spirit, as follows:

A. A steadfast Church, standing on the established mountain of the LORD's house [2]; the Apostle Paul calls it "mount Sion," saying: "But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven" (Heb 12:22-23). The secret of her strength and steadfastness is the Lord Himself, who sanctifies her to Himself and raises her to His heavens so that she bears His traits.

B. High on the top of the mountains [2]; she has become the light of the world, proclaiming the truth openly without fear (Acts 16:26). Her members stand in the body on the earth, but their hearts and thoughts are lifted up as above the high mountains, soaring in the air of heaven. As Origen says: [It is enough that you not remain on the earth, nor dwell in the valleys, nor linger in buried places.]
C. Attractive to the nations and peoples [2-3]: her doors are open to all, bearing a motherhood of love toward all mankind, drawn from the love of her Bridegroom, who gathers all men.

entries.section: 2. The mountain of the LORD's house:

paragraphs.text: D. Her continual work is to lift mankind up [3]. In love she comes down to them without losing her holiness or her heavenly nature, in order to raise all, by the Spirit of the holy God, to the Jerusalem above, that they may practice the new heavenly life in Christ Jesus.
E. Her mission is to declare the way of the Lord [3]; she carries His word to every soul and presents His commandment for every believer to live by, so that he enjoys the law of liberty (Gal 4:26).
F. She proclaims the righteous judgments of Christ, where the believers from all the nations submit to His Kingdom and sovereignty, a spiritual sovereignty unique in its kind.

entries.section: 2. The mountain of the LORD's house:

paragraphs.text: G. She grants peace among the souls sanctified to Him, for they see no human enemies on the whole face of creation. Therefore he says: "and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more" [4]. The Christian's heart is filled with peace even toward his opponents, so that his inner energies are turned from conflict to constructive work, from instruments of war to instruments of production for prosperity.

The word of God turns earth into heaven, so heavenly peace dwells in the life of men, and the kingdom of peace, or the joyful Kingdom of God, is established within them, which neither the enmity of men nor the harshness of events can shake.

* Men went out from Jerusalem into the world, twelve in number; they were unlettered, with no ability to speak, but by the power of God they declared to every race of men that they were sent by Christ to teach all the wisdom of God. And we who formerly fought one another have not only refrained from war against our enemies but have also come to the point that we do not lie or deceive those who examine us (for trial), and we die willingly, confessing Christ.

entries.section: 2. The mountain of the LORD's house:

paragraphs.text: The Martyr Justin H. Enjoying Christ, "the light of the LORD," as Isaiah the prophet heard: "O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the LORD" [5]. The Lord Christ, who dwells in His Church, is the brightness of the Father's glory and the express image of His person, upholding all things by the word of His power (Heb 1:3); He is the Sun of righteousness with healing in its wings (Mal 4:2). He shines upon His Church, and she herself becomes a light to the world, giving light to those who sit in the darkness of sin, presenting her Christ to everyone.

This call addressed to the house of Jacob to walk in the light of the LORD is a call to lift the veil of the letter from the Law, so that the house of Jacob may discover the "Messiah" hidden behind the words, enjoying the word of God not as literal commandments but as fellowship with Christ, the true Light.

Who are the house of Jacob? The Martyr Justin answers: [It is fitting for us here to observe that there are two seeds of Judah, there are two, as there are two houses of Jacob; one born of flesh and blood and the other of faith and the Spirit.]

entries.section: 3. The reason for God's rejection of His people:

paragraphs.text: 6 For thou hast rejected thy people the house of Jacob, because they be replenished from the east, and are diviners like the Philistines, and they clasp hands with the children of strangers. 7 Their land also is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures; their land is also full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots: 8 Their land also is full of idols; they worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made: 9 And the mean man boweth down, and the great man humbleth himself: therefore forgive them not.

The prophet compares the conduct of his contemporary people with the conduct of the nations in the future, when they accept faith in the saving God and enter the Kingdom of peace and enjoy transcendent blessings by dwelling on the mountain of the LORD's house.

The house of Jacob in practice rejected God, in spite of its intense concern for the literalism of worship; therefore God rejected it, and this was a type of the Jews' rejection of the person of the Lord Christ under the cover of their defense of the truth and their zeal for the Law of Moses.

God presented four reasons for rejecting the people, namely: imitating strangers, their love of the wealth of the world, their reliance on their military capabilities, and their acceptance of idol worship.
A. Imitating strangers: "they be replenished from the east" [6].

God had set them apart for Himself to be filled with His Spirit, to bear His heavenly wisdom, and to be witnesses of the truth and a holy leaven for the world; but they opened their doors to strangers, especially the sons of the east, learning from them sorcery, idol worship and abominations, instead of bearing witness before them to God's work in them. For the sake of material gain and indulgence in abominations they encouraged the pagans to settle in their midst, and mixed with them (Hos 7:8), and betrayed the divine covenant.

He also says: "and are diviners like the Philistines" [6]. Instead of returning to God in all their affairs, they imitated the Philistines of that time, resorting to augury and soothsaying, contrary to the divine commandment (Lev 19:26).

B. Their preoccupation with the wealth of the world and material things: "Their land also is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures." Their hearts were filled with the love of money, so they counted it able to satisfy them, and it took the place of God in their thought and feelings.

entries.section: 3. The reason for God's rejection of His people:

paragraphs.text: C. Their reliance on their military capabilities: "their land is also full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots" [7]. They relied on horses and chariots instead of faith and returning to God.

entries.section: 3. The reason for God's rejection of His people:

paragraphs.text: D. Their acceptance of idol worship [8].

entries.section: 3. The reason for God's rejection of His people:

paragraphs.text: These are the reasons for which God rejected His people, and the fruit of that is continual decline instead of growth and ascent [9]. A collapse in every aspect of life instead of complete sanctification by the Lord who ascended into the heavens.

entries.section: 4. The futility of the human arm:

paragraphs.text: 10 Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty. 11 The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day. 12 For the day of the LORD of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and lofty, and upon every one that is lifted up; and he shall be brought low: 13 And upon all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of Bashan, 14 And upon all the high mountains, and upon all the hills that are lifted up, 15 And upon every high tower, and upon every fenced wall, 16 And upon all the ships of Tarshish, and upon all the pleasant banners. 17 And the loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be made low: and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day. 18 And the idols he shall utterly abolish. 19 And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth. 20 In that day a man shall cast his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which they made each one for himself to worship, to the rats and to the bats; 21 To go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged rocks, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth. 22 Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils: for wherein is he to be accounted of?

If God has rejected His people, it is because His people insist on rejecting God by every means, but God remains in His love compassionate toward them and toward all mankind, declaring His salvation to man.

When man grows exceedingly great in his own eyes and the ego swells, the Lord reveals His glory, and man shrinks and seeks salvation. He enters as into a rock and hides in the dust before the fear of the LORD and the glory of His majesty [10]. When God appeared to Abraham, the father of fathers realized that he was dust and ashes, and when Moses saw the glory of the Lord he was afraid and trembled, and so the soul of Job clung to the dust. Nothing shatters man's pride like his meeting with God. The pride is shattered but his soul is not shattered; rather, it is healed and filled with hope in the Lord.

What is the rock in which we hide before the divine majesty but the Lord Christ, for in Him we find a refuge for ourselves before divine justice. Therefore, when the prophet Moses desired to see the divine glory, it was said to him: "Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live... Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock (Christ our Rock): and it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a clift of the rock (union with Christ), and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by" (Ex 33:20-21).

As long as we lean on our Christ, the true Rock, and abide in Him and are found as in a cleft within Him, we see the brightness of the divine glory; but if we trust in ourselves or in the human arm, we perish and are deprived of beholding God.
The prophet likens man's arrogance to the following:

entries.section: 4. The futility of the human arm:

paragraphs.text: A. "All the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, and all the oaks of Bashan" [13] signify reliance on the wealth of nature's resources, and they also signify arrogant kings and leaders such as Rabshakeh.

entries.section: 4. The futility of the human arm:

paragraphs.text: B. "The high mountains and the hills that are lifted up" [14] signify hardness and rigidity, and perhaps they also mean the great kingdoms and the small kingdoms whose rule is pride together with violence.

entries.section: 4. The futility of the human arm:

paragraphs.text: C. "Every high tower and every fenced wall" [15] signify reliance on works of self-righteousness, for man is able to rise up high and fortify himself against every enemy; perhaps they signify the fortified cities.

entries.section: 4. The futility of the human arm:

paragraphs.text: D. "The ships of Tarshish, the ornaments and the pleasant banners" [16] signify absorption in trade and money, with luxury and wealth at the expense of care for the soul.

All these comparisons revolve around man's self-reliance and reliance on the capabilities of nature and its resources, with his continual progress, thinking that he is able by himself to create an atmosphere of satiety, joy and peace, with security and stability in the world, ignoring the divine arm. For this reason he needs the Lord to appear to him, to reveal to him the passing away of all these things, especially in the great day of the Lord.

entries.section: 4. The futility of the human arm:

paragraphs.text: Pride has been linked to idol worship; therefore the prophet affirms that when man discovers the helplessness of the idols, he throws them to the rats and the bats [20], treating them with contempt, instead of taking them with him on his journeys to support him. Instead of honoring them in places of worship he casts them into dark abandoned places where mice and bats play with them.

entries.section: 4. The futility of the human arm:

paragraphs.text: Finally man realizes the error of relying on the human arm, and the prophet says: "Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils: for wherein is he to be accounted of?!" [22]. Let every man be silent, however great his greatness, power or wealth, for the breath of his life goes forth and he is no longer in the world. His spirit goes forth and he returns to the dust (Ps 104:29).

entries.section: 1. The removal of the stay of bread and the stay of water:

paragraphs.text: “For, behold, the Lord, the LORD of hosts, doth take away from Jerusalem and from Judah the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water.” [1].

When God allows Jerusalem and the children of Judah, His people, the bride, to come into want of bread and water, He breaks the stay and the staff, that she may perhaps return and think of leaning upon her Beloved (Song 8:5), so as to find in Him her satisfaction and her quenching of thirst.

God took away from His people the smell of the meat, the leeks and the onions by bringing them out of Egypt, but He gave them the heavenly manna in the wilderness and led them to a land flowing with milk and honey; He deprived them of the waters of the canals in order to present to them the Rock that followed them, flowing with water, and that Rock was Christ (1 Cor 10:4). God deprives us of temporal support so that He Himself may become our support and our heavenly bread and the living fountain who waters our souls with all their powers.
Here the prophet threatens the occurrence of a famine as a fruit of disobedience (Lev 26; Deut 28), and this was fulfilled in history at the destruction of Samaria and Jerusalem.

What is more serious is the occurrence of a hunger for the word of God, as it came in the prophet Amos: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord GOD, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD” (Amos 8:11).
* (The word of God) is food for the soul, its ornament and its safety; so in not listening to it there is famine and deprivation!
St. John Chrysostom

2 The mighty man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the prudent, and the ancient, 3 The captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator. 4 And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them. 5 And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable. 6 When a man shall take hold of his brother of the house of his father, saying, Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand: 7 In that day shall he swear, saying, I will not be an healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing: make me not a ruler of the people. 8 For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen: because their tongue and their doings are against the LORD, to provoke the eyes of his glory. 9 The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves. 10 Say ye to the righteous, that it shall be well with him: for they shall eat the fruit of their doings. 11 Woe unto the wicked! it shall be ill with him: for the reward of his hands shall be given him. 12 As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths. 13 The LORD standeth up to plead, and standeth to judge the people. 14 The LORD will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses. 15 What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith the Lord GOD of hosts.

God raised up for His people mature leaders able to work, such as Moses, great among the prophets, David the righteous king, Deborah the prophetess and judge, and so on. But the people went astray together with their military, judicial, civil and spiritual leaders. They relied on the human arm, with its abilities and thought, and supposed that they were succeeding and advancing in spite of the corruption that had befallen them and their leaders. For this reason God removed from them the mature and wise leaders, leaving them to set up for themselves weak and incapable leaders, that they might realize their need of divine help even for the enjoyment of living and strong leaders.

“(He takes away) the mighty man (the Almighty), and the man of war; the judge, and the prophet, and the prudent (the one who manages affairs), and the ancient, the captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator (skilled in speech)” [2-3].

Perhaps by their removal he did not mean their expulsion or their death, but the stripping of them of the abilities and capacities they had been given: the mighty are weakened, the men of war collapse before the enemy, the judges lose wisdom, the insight of the false prophets is corrupted, and so on. In this way the people reap the fruit of their reliance on the human arm, finding themselves collapsed within and without.

This is what befalls the person who rejects God's work in him: divine grace (the Almighty) is taken away from him; he is deprived of fellowship with the heavenly ones (the spiritual men of war), so that he finds himself without divine help or heavenly support; he loses the gifts of the Spirit, such as wisdom (the judge) and discernment (the prophet), and he cannot make a decision (the removal of the prudent and the ancient); he feels failure even in his temporal work (the removal of the skilled artificer); and he is unable even to speak (the removal of the eloquent orator). In other words, a person loses his life and even his natural abilities, to live in inner emptiness, corruption and failure, in spite of the outward appearances of strength, wisdom, wealth and success that he bears.
Now, when God removes the mature leaders and a person loses the grace of God, what happens?

A. “And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them” [4]. When Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned, he accepted the hasty, violent and extreme counsel of the young men and rejected the wise, balanced counsel of the elders, which was full of love and gentleness (1 Kgs 12); so the people were divided, civil wars came upon the tribes, and enmity prevailed instead of love and unity.

God loves the young; He supports them and seeks their continual growth. But what He meant here by children and babes is spiritual and intellectual immaturity. John the Baptist was a spiritually mature unborn child, who bore witness to the Lord Christ while still in the womb of the Virgin Mary, whereas many of the scribes, Pharisees, Sadducees and priests were mature in years but not in spirit, and so they behaved like children, seeking to kill the Lord Christ and be rid of Him. Thus we see in the history of the people of God, from its beginning until today, many young people who were mature leaders, while we find men and elders who behaved with the spirit of immature childhood. Therefore the Apostle exhorts all believers: “Quit you like men” (1 Cor 16:13), meaning maturity and spiritual strength, for it befits all believers, men, women, children, elders and youths, to be, in the Spirit, mature men.

Origen comments on the numbering of the people mentioned in Num 1, which included the men without the children or the women, saying: [The present text teaches me that if I pass beyond the simplicity of childhood, that is, if I cease to have the thoughts of a child, since “when I became a man, I put away childish things” (1 Cor 13:11), I say, I have become a young man able to overcome the wicked one (1 Jn 2:13), and I appear worthy to be among those of whom it is said that they walk in power... and I am counted fit for the divine numbering. But if any one of us has wavering, carnal thoughts... he is not worthy to be numbered before God in the pure and holy Book of Numbers.]
Perhaps the prophet Isaiah is referring to Manasseh, who took up the rule at the age of twelve when his father Hezekiah died.

B. “And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable” [5]. The sign of the loss of sound, mature leadership is the upsetting of the balances, so that the law of injustice prevails and the spirit of disorder comes upon the life of the community, as within the individual.
