St. Macarius the Great In our study of “The Holy Spirit between the New Birth and Continual Renewal” we saw that the rite of Baptism, which in truth is an enjoyment of dying with the Lord Christ, being buried with Him, and enjoying the power of His resurrection, rests on two main lines: the enjoyment of the new man, who is in the image of his Creator, and the shattering of the works of the old man; that is, the enjoyment of the Lord Christ and the renouncing of the devil and all his powers and works. In the waters of Baptism we are united with our Christ the King, crucified, who shatters Leviathan the deceiving serpent and the dragon that dwells in the waters.

* After you have bent your knees, you are asked to utter these words: “I renounce you, Satan”... What has happened? What is this sudden, strange change? You who trembled with fear, do you rebel against your master? Do you look at his counsel with contempt? What has brought you to this madness? When did this boldness come upon you? You say: We have a sword; a strong sword.
What sword is this? What ally do you have? Tell me.

You answer: We are entering Your service, O Christ, and therefore we are bold and rebellious, because we have a strong refuge. This has set us above Satan. We who before were terrified of him and feared him, not only renounce him alone, but with him all his pomps.
* The priests ask you to say: I renounce you, Satan, and all your pomps and all your service and all your works.
Few words, but of great power!

The angels stand beside you, and the invisible powers rejoice at your change, and they receive the words from your tongues and carry them to the Master of all creation, to be inscribed there in the books of heaven.
St. John Chrysostom

2 In that day sing ye unto the desirable vineyard. 3 I the LORD do keep it; I will water it every moment: lest any hurt it, I will keep it night and day. 4 Fury is not in me: who would set the briers and thorns against me in battle? I would go through them, I would burn them together. 5 Or let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me; and he shall make peace with me. 6 He shall cause them that come of Jacob to take root: Israel shall blossom and bud, and fill the face of the world with fruit. 7 Hath he smitten him, as he smote those that smote him? or is he slain according to the slaughter of them that are slain by him? 8 In measure, when it shooteth forth, thou wilt debate with it: he stayeth his rough wind in the day of the east wind. 9 By this therefore shall the iniquity of Jacob be purged; and this is all the fruit to take away his sin; when he maketh all the stones of the altar as chalkstones that are beaten in sunder, the groves and images shall not stand up.

Since the Lord Himself takes over the leadership of the battle, He becomes personally a party to it, so that the desirable vineyard may enjoy His victory, His keeping of her, and His care and concern for her. Therefore the prophet says on the tongue of the Lord: “In that day sing ye unto the desirable vineyard. I the LORD do keep it; I will water it every moment: lest any hurt it, I will keep it night and day...” [3-5].

God Himself is the owner of the vineyard; He loves her and desires her, and He is the vinedresser and keeper of her; He tends her every moment, watering her with His divine blessings; His eye is upon her night and day; He does not leave her or forsake her; He removes the thorns and briers from her to burn them, and reconciles her with the Father through His cross (Rom 5:1).
If the cross shattered the devil and stripped him of his authority over the believers, it also offered the following blessings:

A. “Sing ye unto the desirable vineyard” [3]. To whom is this said, if not to the heavenly beings who perceived the fruits of the cross in the life of the Church, so that their life exulted and they began to praise God the Savior of mankind for His wondrous work in them, for He made the earthly heavenly, and raised the Church up to the throne to share with heaven its praises and its liturgies. The vineyard desired by God her Savior has become the object of desire of the angels and all the heavenly orders (Rev 5:11-14).

If the remembrance of God is the desire of man's soul, that is a response to God's love for us and His desire for us, since we are His desirable vineyard and His beloved bride and His Church in which He desires to dwell. The psalmist says: “For the LORD hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation. This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it” (Ps 132:13-14); “This is the hill which God desireth to dwell in; yea, the LORD will dwell in it for ever” (Ps 68:16).

B. Divine keeping: “I the LORD do keep it... I will keep it night and day” [3]. If God sends His angels to protect His people from temporal dangers, He Himself undertakes to keep her from the deadly blows of sin. The enemy was shattered by the cross, not as a historical event of the past but as a divine work that is present and active; He fixed His cross in the midst of His Church to embrace her from every blow of the enemy so long as she remains in His embrace and asks for His keeping. Therefore St. Ephrem the Syrian says: [Glory to You who set up Your cross as a bridge over death, on which souls cross from the dwelling of death to the dwelling of life.]

C. Continual care: “I will water it every moment” [3]; for He sends down upon her the rains of His free grace, and turns her wilderness into a divine paradise. Therefore she converses with Him, saying: “Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits” (Song 4:16). What I bear of the fruits of the Spirit is His work in me, the fruit of His unceasing care.
With what does God water His Church, the desirable vineyard?
He gives us His Holy Spirit working in us, gives us His life in us... He gives us Himself!
* Generous is He who gives us the greatest of all gifts, His very life!
St. Clement of Alexandria * Because of the grace of the Spirit that was given to us, we are in Him and He is in us (1 Jn 4:13)...

Apart from the Spirit we are strangers to God and far from Him, but by communion in the Spirit we have become near to the divinity; our being in the Father is not of ourselves but is the work of the Spirit who dwells within us.

Pope Athanasius the Apostolic D. Her not being condemned: “Fury is not in me” [4]. When she receives His free gift and responds practically to His grace, she does not fall under the divine wrath but says with confidence: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death” (Rom 8:1-2).

Some hold that the word “fury” should be read here “hemah,” which means “grapes”; for when He did not find good grapes but thorns and briers, or wild grapes, He burned the thorns and briers to give opportunity for good fruit-bearing.

E. The burning of the thorns and briers: “Would that I had the thorns and briers in battle, that I might go against them and burn them together” [4]. He took upon Himself the resisting of the thorns and briers that choke the desirable vineyard, saying: “Would that I had the thorns...” Indeed He bore the thorns on His head when He was crucified, removing the shame, or the curse, from us to bear it for us. As St. Jacob of Serugh says: [He bore the curse of the earth by the crown they placed on His head, and bore the weight of the whole world like a mighty one...! He became a curse that the returning heirs might be blessed through Him! By His crown He uprooted the cursed seed of the serpent... By the crown of thorns He demolished the crown of Satan, who wanted to be god over creation! From His crown of thorns He wove a crown for the daughter of the Gentiles, the bride whom He betrothed from among the idols and wrote down for His name.]

F. Our reconciliation with God: “Or let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me; and he shall make peace with me” [5]. This is the end of the work of the cross: our reconciliation with God, for when we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of His Son (Rom 5:10).
* The Son of God suffered to make us sons of God, and the son of man (we humans) refuses to suffer so that his sonship to God may continue!!!

St. Cyprian G. The growth of the universal Church or the new Israel: “In the future Jacob shall take root; Israel shall blossom and bud, and they shall fill the face of the world with fruit” [6]. Perhaps God wanted them not to look to His work with them in the near future (their salvation from the Babylonian captivity) but to the distant future, where the new Jacob takes root, and the Church of the New Covenant arises as the new Israel, which included from among the Jews the disciples and Apostles and many believers who brought forth surpassing spiritual fruits that filled the face of the world. St. Irenaeus says: [The seed was cast into all the world... for from this (Jerusalem) Christ and the Apostles were able to bring forth fruits.]

H. His discipline of His children [7-9]: He treats them as sons and not as enemies, so He allows them to be disciplined for their salvation and edification, saying: “Hath he smitten him, as he smote those that smote him?” [7], meaning: has God smitten Jacob Israel as He smote those who smote Jacob? When He strikes His people it is for their edification, but as for the blow to the enemies who smite His people, let it demolish them, because they persist in denial and resistance to God. In the same sense He says: “Or is he slain according to the slaughter of them that are slain by him?” [7].

“With a rebuke (by measure), when thou didst put her away, thou didst contend with her; he removed her with his rough wind in the day of the east wind” [8]. Even in contending, He contends with her as by measure, that is, He allows her affliction as much as she can bear, to discipline her for her sins, even if it seems that He has divorced her and delivered her to the tempestuous wind coming from the east, that is, to Assyria or Babylon in 722 B.C. and 587 B.C.

10 Yet the defenced city shall be desolate, and the habitation forsaken, and left like a wilderness: there shall the calf feed, and there shall he lie down, and consume the branches thereof. 11 When the boughs thereof are withered, they shall be broken off: the women come, and set them on fire: for it is a people of no understanding: therefore he that made them will not have mercy on them, and he that formed them will shew them no favour.

In contrast to His discipline of His children, even if it seemed harsh, using Assyria and Babylon, or as one who had divorced them, He permits the destruction of the evil enemy; He turns Babylon, the fortified city, into a forsaken habitation, left like a wilderness.
Some hold that the talk here is also about Samaria, which became a ruin because of its people's spiritual ignorance and their withdrawal from the worship of God and falling into idolatry [19-11].

12 And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel. 13 And it shall come to pass in that day, that the great trumpet shall be blown, and they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt, and shall worship the LORD in the holy mount at Jerusalem.

Some see in this a prophecy of the gathering of the people of Israel at the end of the ages when they accept faith in the Lord Christ, while others see it as a picture of God's work through the ages when He brought His people out of Egypt and then saved them from the Babylonian captivity.
Perhaps it points here to the new Israel, the Church gathered from among the peoples and nations to enjoy the risen life.

1 Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, whose glorious beauty is a fading flower, which are on the head of the fat valleys of them that are overcome with wine! 2 Behold, the Lord hath a mighty and strong one, which as a tempest of hail and a destroying storm, as a flood of mighty waters overflowing, shall cast down to the earth with the hand. 3 The crown of pride, the drunkards of Ephraim, shall be trodden under feet: 4 And the glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fat valley, shall be a fading flower, and as the hasty fruit before the summer; which when he that looketh upon it seeth, while it is yet in his hand he eateth it up. 5 In that day shall the LORD of hosts be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people, 6 And for a spirit of judgment to him that sitteth in judgment, and for strength to them that turn the battle to the gate.

God brings woe upon Samaria, or Ephraim, permitting Assyria in 722 B.C. to overrun the land, ruin the cities and carry away great numbers into captivity. This was a discipline for Israel and a practical lesson for Judah; the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the capital of Judah, were able to go up on the roofs and see the sky reddened with God's wrath against Israel, for tongues of fire rose from many houses of Samaria and its surroundings. Yet the kingdom of Judah did not take warning, for afterward it walked in the same sins of Samaria and even more, as in the parable of Aholah and Aholibah in Ezekiel 33, which tells this matter in some detail.

Verses [1-6] depict the fall of Samaria, which was built on a high hill with delightful gardens surrounding it on every side, so that it was counted among the most beautiful and beloved cities of Palestine. The valley beneath it reaches to the coast of Jezreel, rich in vineyards and fruitful fields. God had given them an abundance of good things and wealth, but they left the Giver of the gifts and turned aside to the pagan gods worshiped by the surrounding nations; and their worship was bound up with a pampered, luxurious life together with many abominations; therefore God wanted to discipline them. He stirred the heart of the king of Assyria to look upon beautiful, rich Samaria and the cities around it, so he sent a great army to occupy it. But Israel relied on her human arm and forgot her God, and supposed that she was able to shatter the enemy; so her capital and many of her cities were shattered and became a living example for everyone who relies on the human arm, ignoring God's providence.
The prophet presents a wonderful poetic picture of the destruction of Samaria and the glory of the faithful remnant:

A. The rich of Samaria were accustomed to hold constant banquets in which they served wine and strong drink without measure, so they got drunk and made merry, and they used to put wreaths of flowers on their heads as a sign of glory and for adornment.

The prophet sees the city of Samaria, the head of the cities of Israel, surrounded by gardens, like the head of one of these rich men who eats and drinks and makes merry and gets drunk and practices abominations with a wreath of flowers on his head. God brings woe upon these wreaths, so that they become a shame and a disgrace rather than glory and splendor; their appearance fades, and they deserve to go down with the head that bears them to the dust, to be thrown on the dunghill and trodden underfoot [2-3].

B. The Lord sends the army of Assyria as one mighty (strong) and powerful man [2]... It is as though what was accomplished at the hands of the army of the king of Assyria was neither coincidence nor human planning or human resources, but by divine permission that gives them ability and strength and gives them unity to carry out a divine plan, namely the discipline of Samaria!

C. The army of Assyria, which besieges Samaria and humbles her, is likened to one who brings down to the dust the head of a rich man bearing a wreath of flowers, with a snowstorm and sweeping floods of water. The rose cannot bear the snow and so it dies, and it cannot bear the floods of water, so it is swept violently to the ground without settling until it becomes an inseparable part of the dunghill [2].
D. He likens Samaria to a fig tree bearing a few first fruits that are plucked in moments, and no fruit remains on it [4].

E. If God allows this humiliation, removing all glory and splendor for the sake of discipline, He Himself comes forward to be glory and splendor to His believers: “In that day shall the LORD of hosts be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people, and for a spirit of judgment to him that sitteth in judgment, and for strength to them that turn the battle to the gate” [5-6]. God becomes our beauty, and the diadem of our splendor, and also our justice, the defender of the poor and the wronged, and the leader of our battle, giving us spiritual victory against the powers of darkness.

In contrast to the collapse that befell Samaria, which represents the denial of the faith, God offers Himself as splendor of glory, righteousness, justice and victory to the remnant of His people who are faithful to Him [5]; and the following is to be noted here:

First: He says: “In that day” [5]; it is the day of redemption or crucifixion on which the Lord bore our shame on the cross that He Himself might become our crown. He accepted death for us to give us His life and His resurrection and His righteousness; He bore weakness to give us, by His weakness, the power of victory.
St. John Chrysostom speaks of the cross as a sign of glory and power... saying:
[The cross is glory. Look at what the Evangelist says... “for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified” (Jn 7:39).

The cross is that which removed the enmity between God and men, bringing reconciliation, making the earth heaven, joining angels with men, shattering the fortress of death, weakening the might of Satan, quenching the dominion of sin, rescuing the world from error and recovering the truth, driving out demons, demolishing the temples of idols and transforming their altars and abolishing their sacrifices, sowing virtue and founding the Church!

The cross is the will of the Father, the glory of the Son, and the joy of the Holy Spirit. It is the subject of Paul's boasting when he says: “But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ” (Gal 6:14).

The cross is brighter than the sun, and more radiant than its rays, for when the sun was darkened the cross shone forth. The sun was darkened not because it was extinguished but because the brightness of the cross overcame it...
The cross breaks our chains and abolishes the prison of death.
It is the sign of God's love (Jn 3:16)...

The cross is a strong fortress and an impregnable shield, protector of the rich, and a spring for the poor, defender of those fallen into the snares, and armor for those on the attack, and a means of conquering the passions and obtaining the virtues, and a wondrous, astonishing sign!].

Second: Who is the remnant of His chosen people that adorns itself with the LORD of hosts, is justified by Him and overcomes? Some hold that the talk here is of the kingdom of Judah, which for a time remained in a better state than Ephraim; others see that this remnant are those who accepted faith in the crucified Lord Christ, such as the Apostles and disciples and the Marys and Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus, and so on... and others see that it is the remnant that will be saved in the days of the Antichrist, when the spirit of apostasy prevails in the world, but for the sake of the elect God shortens the days (Mt 24:22)...
In any case, this remnant includes every soul that runs to the Savior, the LORD of hosts, to hide in Him and rest at His feet and take shelter under His cross, whatever the time may be!

7 But they also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are out of the way; the priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine, they are out of the way through strong drink; they err in vision, they stumble in judgment. 8 For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean. 9 Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts. 10 For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little: 11 For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people. 12 To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear. 13 But the word of the LORD was unto them precept upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little; that they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken. 14 Wherefore hear the word of the LORD, ye scornful men, that rule this people which is in Jerusalem. 15 Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves:

After speaking of the discipline of Ephraim, it seems that he returned to speak of the sins of Judah, for he says: “But they also” [7]; he exposed and denounced them, depicting the extent of Judah's moral dissolution:

A. Drunkenness: “They also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are out of the way; the priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine, they are out of the way through strong drink” [7]. If the leaders in Samaria, the capital of Israel, had been corrupted by strong drink, the religious leaders in Jerusalem gave in to the same error.

By the prophet here he means the “false prophets” who prophesied out of their own heads to flatter the dissolute priests and the civil leaders. These, as is stated in the Book of Jeremiah, used to speak smooth things, that is, soft, deceptive words, saying that the people were well and at peace and that no disciplines would come upon Jerusalem or the temple... and this is the natural fruit of abandoning the word of God and being entangled in material and moral gain.
If this is the state of the priest and the prophet, what then is the state of the people?!

B. Error and injustice: “They err in vision, they stumble in judgment” [7]. Since the priest and the false prophet reeled with strong drink, they lost their spiritual awareness and offered misleading visions, because their inner sight had been darkened. And for the same reason they lost the ability to judge justly, so they caused unrest and confusion among the people.

In other words, every sin hands man over to another sin; the preoccupation of the priest and the prophet with tables and a life of luxury drew them into absorption in drinking wine until they fell into drunkenness, and this corrupts their inner sight, so they offer misleading visions, and consequently they lose their ability to be just and judge unjustly...
C. False prophecies: “For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean” [8].

The prophet sees the tables filling the city, and everyone absorbed in eating and drinking greedily without limit, until they vomited in order to return and eat, and this was the custom of the Romans. The whole place, indeed the whole city, became full of vomit and filth, so that no place could be found where a man could rest.
This outward picture reveals the spiritual state of Judah, for the false prophets vomited prophecies of their own making and filled the place with what is neither clean nor holy.

This is the picture of the reckless man whose whole being is corrupted by the passions, so that his soul, and likewise his heart, his mind, his feelings and all his energies and talents, are filled with abominations, until he becomes like a city full of corruption; so the holy Savior says: “but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head” (Mt 8:20).
Man corrupted life, so the Holy One found no place or spot to rest among us; yet He came to lay His head on the cross, that we might find a place for ourselves in the bosom of the Father.
When our inner tables are filled with filth, it is said to the Lord “there is no place” [8], instead of saying: “Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits” (Song 4:16).

Yet the Savior longs to prepare a place in Himself for us, saying to us: “Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock: and it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a clift of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by” (Ex 33:21-22).

D. Mockery of the prophet: The priests and false prophets in their drunkenness mocked the prophet Isaiah, saying: “Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts?” [9]. It is as though they were saying that they are people of knowledge and learning, so why does he want to teach them anything?! Let him go to those weaned from milk and present to them his prophecies and commandments, which are fitting only for the simple who have no thought and for infants who are not mature.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little” [10]. It is as though the prophet were talking to small children, repeating to them commands and ordinances and offering them small things... It is like one who holds a child and teaches him to walk, pulling him now to the right and now to the left... a picture of the contempt of the drunken priests and prophets for the prophet Isaiah and his teachings!

What is the punishment of those who mock him and his teachings and prophecies? The prophet says: “For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people” [11]. They mocked the language of the prophet or his prophecies, supposing him to be one who teaches newly weaned children; therefore God sends them an enemy of strange tongue who cries out in their faces, and they do not understand his words, so they become like children without knowledge. They refused to learn from Isaiah and mocked him, so the Lord sent them Assyrian masters to teach them through the language of violence and enslavement together with humiliation.

“To whom he said, This is the rest (my rest) wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear” [12]. They did not wish to listen to the voice of God, who says that His rest is in our giving rest to the weary who are burdened with toils. The priests and false prophets cared for outward formalities, not for the rest of God Himself, who rests in His people.

* It was said by the prophet: “This is my rest: cause the weary to rest” [12]. Accomplish this rest for the Lord, O man, and then you will not need to say: “Forgive me.” Give rest to the weary, visit the sick, give food to the poor, for this in truth is prayer... All the time in which you fulfill the rest of the Lord is a time of prayer...
Beware, beloved, lest an opportunity come to you to give rest to the will of God and you say: Now is the time for prayer, I will pray and then I will work!

Father Aphrahat Let them listen to the voice of the Lord and speak with Him not in the language of formalities but in the language of practical obedience, comforting to God in His children. Let them learn this as children, and let them train in it, ignoring that they are priests and prophets who possess knowledge and learning, lest they fall backward and sink into the snares of the enemy like game or prey [13] whose end is certain death.

He answers these scoffers, saying: “We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves” [15]. They declare that they do not fear death or dread the grave, for they have entered into a covenant with them; they know how to take refuge in lies so that they do not fall under disciplines or afflictions, because their constitution is deceit.

They are a type of the Antichrist and his followers, as he is the tyrant who makes a covenant with the formalists in worship (Dan 9:27) so that they may act without fear of death or the grave; but the work of the Lord Christ is to shatter this covenant in order to establish a covenant with the Father and an eternal reconciliation with His believers.

16 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste. 17 Judgment also will I lay to the line, and righteousness to the plummet: and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters shall overflow the hiding place. 18 And your covenant with death shall be disannulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it. 19 From the time that it goeth forth it shall take you: for morning by morning shall it pass over, by day and by night: and it shall be a vexation only to understand the report. 20 For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it. 21 For the LORD shall rise up as in mount Perazim, he shall be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon, that he may do his work, his strange work; and bring to pass his act, his strange act. 22 Now therefore be ye not mockers, lest your bands be made strong: for I have heard from the Lord GOD of hosts a consumption, even determined upon the whole earth.

If the enemy of good works with all his energies to turn believers away from the truth, working in different forms in every age, especially in the days of the apostasy (the Antichrist), the Lord Himself comes forward to support His children and believers against this satanic work.
“Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste” [16].
Thus, in the midst of the dark picture, the prophet Isaiah prophesies of the Messiah as the cornerstone and the foundation stone on which the Church is built:

A. The foundation stone in Zion: The psalmist says: “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. This is the LORD'S doing; it is marvellous in our eyes” (Ps 118:22-23) (see Mt 21:42; Acts 4:11; Rom 9:33; Eph 2:20; 1 Pet 2:6, 8); He is the foundation stone on which the Church is built, a tried stone, tested by Satan so that by His victory He might give us the victory; a precious stone beyond price. He is the cornerstone who joined the Jews with the Gentiles like two walls knit together in faith in Him. Whoever believes in Him will not flee (be put to shame)... Thus Isaiah gives us a Messianic prophecy that reveals the person of the Lord Christ and His place in relation to the Church, His riches and glory, and trust in Him, and His unchangeableness and rejection.

* The Savior is the chosen stone, rejected by those who should have built the synagogue of the Jews, and He has become the head of the corner. Scripture likens Him to a cornerstone because He joins the two peoples together: Israel and the Gentiles, in one faith and one love (Eph 2:15).
St. Cyril the Great * Who is this of whom we speak?

“The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner” (Ps 118:23); “to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace; and that he might reconcile both unto God in one body” (Eph 2:15-16); that is, the circumcision and the uncircumcision.

St. Augustine B. A spiritual building is raised upon Him [17], whose measuring line is truth and whose plummet is justice. So the building is raised straight, with no crookedness, dwelt in by truth and justice, for God Himself dwells in it with His believers.

If the Church is the living building raised upon the person of the Lord Christ as her foundation, then His Gospel is the truth and His cross is the justice joined to mercy. By the Gospel and the cross the Church of Christ is built in uprightness as a place of safety. But whoever takes refuge in lies, like the false prophets, the hail becomes a refuge for them and the floods sweep away their hidden depths, so all their hope goes in vain and they lose safety. Their covenant with death and the grave is annulled, and the scourge sweeps them away like a flood that brings them down to the ground, so that they are trodden down [18]. With every morning and every evening, new disturbing news reaches them because of the continual attack of the enemies. They find no room enough to stretch out in sleep, nor a covering to wrap themselves in against the cold.
“For the LORD shall rise up as in mount Perazim, he shall be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon, that he may do his work, his strange work; and bring to pass his act, his strange act” [21].

“Perazim” is a Canaanite name meaning “breakings forth,” a place in the valley of Rephaim (2 Sam 5:20; 1 Chr 14:11); it is Mount Perazim near the valley of Gibeon and perhaps its site today is “Ras al-Sanadir.” Isaiah's saying here: “For the LORD shall rise up as in mount Perazim” means that God storms upon His enemies suddenly and shatters them completely, just as He did for the prophet David at Mount Perazim when he said: “The LORD hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me, as the breach of waters” (2 Sam 5:20); and also his saying: “as in the valley of Gibeon” means that He works as in the days of Joshua against the Canaanites in the valley of Gibeon (Josh 10:10).

What is the strange work that God does but the punishing of wrong? For God takes no pleasure in punishing; He does so out of necessity, as a thing strange to Him, for Jeremiah says: “But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies. For he doth not afflict willingly nor grieve the children of men” (Lam 3:32-33), as it is said: “For, behold, the LORD cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity” (Isa 26:21).

Thus the wicked, especially those who mock the word of the Lord and the prophecies and who refuse to believe in the Messiah, the subject of the prophecies and the center of all Scripture, find no mercy or refuge, in spite of God's unwillingness to punish. He says: “Now therefore be ye not mockers, lest your bands be made strong” [22], meaning not the bands with which the people are bound when taken captive to Assyria or Babylon, but the chains of eternal darkness that bind those who deny the faith and reject the prophecies, when the whole earth is judged [22].

23 Give ye ear, and hear my voice; hearken, and hear my speech. 24 Doth the plowman plow all day to sow? doth he open and break the clods of his ground? 25 When he hath made plain the face thereof, doth he not cast abroad the fitches, and scatter the cummin, and cast in the principal wheat and the appointed barley and the rie in their place? 26 For his God doth instruct him to discretion, and doth teach him. 27 For the fitches are not threshed with a threshing instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned about upon the cummin; but the fitches are beaten out with a staff, and the cummin with a rod. 28 Bread corn is bruised; because he will not ever be threshing it, nor break it with the wheel of his cart, nor bruise it with his horsemen. 29 This also cometh forth from the LORD of hosts, which is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in working.

He likens God to a sower who does not stop at plowing and breaking up the ground and preparing it for planting but also scatters the seed. If God permits discipline, it is like the sower who plows the ground and breaks it up and clears it of stones and levels it, and this is the negative work; but He does not stop there but offers a positive work, for He casts the seed of His word into the field of this world. The Lord Himself comes forward as a seed that He Himself casts into our hearts in order to establish His garden in us. He knows how to sow the fitches, Nigella Sativa [a plant of the buttercup family, with umbel-like flowers similar to the anise plant, whose seed is called the seed of blessing, and which is not threshed but beaten with a rod], and the cummin and the wheat and the barley and the rie, each in its place and in the way that suits it.
We are God's husbandry and His field and His vineyard; He cares for us as our own God, who belongs to us as we belong to Him, “For his God doth instruct him to discretion, and doth teach him” [26]...

Like a sower who knows how to deal with each crop: some need threshing with the threshing instrument, and some need to be beaten with the rod to extract the seed from the chaff, and some need neither threshing nor beating [27]; and in all this He does not seek to destroy His crops and crush them but to gather them [28]... He is the compassionate God even in His disciplines, seeking what is for the salvation and edification of His children, working with wonderful wisdom and great understanding [29].

1 Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David dwelt! add ye year to year; let the feasts go round. 2 Yet I will distress Ariel, and there shall be heaviness and sorrow: and it shall be unto me as Ariel. 3 And I will camp against thee round about, and will lay siege against thee with a mount, and I will raise forts against thee. 4 And thou shalt be brought down, and shalt speak out of the ground, and thy speech shall be low out of the dust, and thy voice shall be as a phantom out of the ground, and thy speech shall whisper out of the dust. 5 Moreover the multitude of thine enemies shall be like small dust, and the multitude of the terrible ones shall be as chaff that passeth away: yea, it shall be at an instant suddenly. 6 Thou shalt be visited of the LORD of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire. 7 And the multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel, even all that fight against her and her munition, and that distress her, shall be as a dream of a night vision. 8 It shall even be as when an hungry man dreameth, and, behold, he eateth; but he awaketh, and his soul is empty: or as when a thirsty man dreameth, and, behold, he drinketh; but he awaketh, and, behold, he is faint, and his soul hath appetite: so shall the multitude of all the nations be, that fight against mount Zion.
"Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David dwelt!" [1].

The word "Ariel" means "the fiery hearth of God," or "the lion of God," or "the mighty lion." It is a symbolic name meant for Jerusalem, as the city that contains in the Temple the altar of burnt offering blazing with fire (Ezek 43:15-16), and as the capital of the people of God, like the lion, the king of the beasts.
Ironside sees that Jerusalem was in former times like the lion of God, but she becomes more like a huge hearth for sacrifices, on which her people are offered at the hands of their bitter enemies.

King David, the prophet, used Ariel as his capital for a long time, and built his palace on Mount Zion, where the glory of God was afterwards declared in a wonderful way. His son Solomon built the Temple on Mount Moriah within Jerusalem, so the city became the center of communal worship, in which sacrifices were offered to the Lord, and she was counted as a lion in her spiritual strength. But when she became loosed from the spirit of true worship, was occupied with formalities without spirit, and was immersed in abominations with an insistence on not repenting, woe came upon her.
The people were accustomed to come to Jerusalem to celebrate three annual feasts [1], but God in His discipline turns these feasts into mourning and sorrow [2].

What does He mean by His saying, "and it shall be unto me as Ariel" [2]? Perhaps He wanted to declare that in her sorrow she becomes like a hearth of fire which God allowed to be kindled for the discipline of His wayward people; and perhaps He meant that although He allows her to be defeated and distressed, He makes her like a fiery altar for Himself, burning up the enemy who seized her, as a sacrifice to the Lord.

He expresses the measure of the sorrow that comes upon Jerusalem when she is besieged, saying: "And thou shalt be brought down, and shalt speak out of the ground, and thy speech shall be low out of the dust, and thy voice shall be as a phantom out of the ground, and thy speech shall whisper out of the dust" [4]. Because of her intense sorrow the inhabitants of Jerusalem sit in the dust like those at a "funeral," according to the ancient oriental traditions, and her voice comes out as if from the ground; and since they find none of the living to consult, they resort to the dead, seeking their counsel (Isa 8:19), and the voices come out faint, as if spiritual, and this is a kind of deception of the demons.

Yet in His love God intervenes suddenly with His lofty arm to save His city and His people from the army of Sennacherib (Isa 37:33-36), and the wrath of God falls upon the enemy, who scatters them like fine dust and like chaff in the blowing of the wind. He depicts this deliverance as a type of our salvation by the Cross and of the salvation of the Church at the end of the ages from the Antichrist:

A. The collapse of the enemy despite the greatness of his number and strength: "Moreover the multitude of thine enemies shall be like small dust, and the multitude of the terrible ones shall be as chaff that passeth away" [5]. These point to the devil and his angels, who are without number and fight humanity relentlessly, but before the Cross they become as nothing.

* We do not fear Satan even though he is a spirit without a body, for nothing is weaker than he who came to deal with us while being without a body, and no one is stronger than the brave man, even if he carries a body subject to death!
St. John Chrysostom B. The achievement of a swift victory: "yea, it shall be at an instant suddenly" [5], pointing to the surpassing power of the Cross to overcome enemies.
* With prayer, sign yourself with the Cross on your forehead, and then the demons will not come near you, because you will be armed against them.

St. John Chrysostom C. The Lord's salvation of this stricken city is accompanied by special signs in nature. "Thou shalt be visited of the LORD of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire" [6]. These signs point to what happened during the crucifixion of the Lord Christ, the upheaval of nature, such as the eclipse of the sun, the darkening of the moon, and the occurrence of an earthquake... and they also point to what will happen shortly before the final coming of the Lord Christ for judgment (Isa 28:21; 30:30; Zech 14:1-6; 2 Thess 1:6-8).

Perhaps the purpose of these signs is to rebuke man, whom God appointed lord of nature as the image and likeness of God, for lifeless nature bears witness to the saving works of God and condemns man's ingratitude and his disregard of his Creator and Savior.
D. The complete scattering of the enemies, for they vanish as in a dream of the night: when a man wakes, everything he saw disappears, and it is hard for him even to remember it [7].

The enemy who tried to seize the people of God will be like the hungry man who dreams that he eats, or the thirsty man who dreams that he drinks, only to wake and find himself as he was, hungry and thirsty [8].

entries.section: 2. The spread of ignorance among His people:

paragraphs.text: 9 Be slothful and be astonished. Indulge yourselves and be blind. They are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink. 10 For the LORD hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and hath closed your eyes: the prophets and your rulers, the seers hath he covered. 11 And the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed: 12 And the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I am not learned.

Besides the people's characteristic of covering an evil life with the formalities of worship, there was their ignorance of the word of God and their lack of experience of the power of the commandment in their lives.

If the Holy Spirit makes the soul drunk, giving it a heavenly joy that makes it forget the bitterness of affliction and pain, then spiritual ignorance makes it drunk by its drinking the cup of the wrath of God, and the fruit of this ignorance is:

A. Sloth [9]. The people grew slack and neglected the salvation of their souls, and became as if in a state of deep sleep [10], like sleepers who have lost spiritual feelings and holy sentiments, and watchfulness, and activity, and constant prayer, and the meeting with God in vitality.

St. John Chrysostom says: [The Apostle Paul, when he accused the people of falling into a state of deep sleep and lack of watchfulness (Rom 11:7-8)], resorted to the prophet David and Isaiah, lest this accusation be counted as coming from himself.

B. Being struck by a kind of dazzlement without enjoying the work of God. The truth shines before them like the sun, but their weak eyes deprived them of the enjoyment of its light, so they became dazzled by it without beholding it.
C. Delighting in a life of luxury [9].

entries.section: 2. The spread of ignorance among His people:

paragraphs.text: D. The rejection of good counsel. There were prophets among them [10], as spiritual eyes by which the people, as well as the leaders, could behold the truth and understand the plan of God and His will. The prophets enjoyed visions, therefore they were called seers or beholders [10], but these visions remained a sealed book, either because what came in the book was obscure to them, or because of the people's inability to read it.

13 Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men: 14 Therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.

Perhaps the most dangerous enemy that faces the religious is hypocrisy, or concern for formalities without the substance of the holy life. King Hezekiah began his reforms, but some abandoned the worship of idols outwardly and not from their heart; and they came to draw near to God with their lips and not their hearts, concerned with the praise of men and not of God, having a form of godliness while denying its power.
"Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men" [13].

Origen links the people's drawing near to God with their lips without the heart to the spread of ignorance, that is, the claim of spiritual knowledge while not believing in the Lord Christ, and he says: [When the prophetic words become like the words of a sealed book, not only for those who do not know letters but for those who practice knowledge as a profession, then the Lord says that the people of the Jews draw near to the Lord only with their mouth and honour Him with their lips, because their heart is far from the Lord on account of their unbelief in Jesus].

St. Clement of Alexandria sees that God uncovered this fault not to take vengeance on them nor to expose them, but that they might realize their weaknesses and return to Him seeking their salvation. [Here His pastoral love made Him show their sins as He shows them salvation side by side].
From the comments of the Fathers on honoring God with the mouth without the heart:
* Many have understanding in their lips and not in their hearts.

* They drew near in body but stood far off in their hearts. Who was nearer to Him in body than those who lifted Him up on the Cross?! Who were farther from Him than those who blasphemed Him...? The very same persons who were near Him were also far from Him. They were near with their lips, far with their hearts.
St. Augustine * Let us cling to those who pledge peace by their godliness, not to those who profane the desire for godliness by hypocrisy.

* It is said: "They bless with their mouths, but their hearts curse" (Ps 63:4). And it is also said: "They loved him with their mouth, and lied unto him with their tongue; for their heart was not right with him, neither were they stedfast in his covenant"; "Let the lying lips be put to silence" (Ps 78:36-37; 31:8).
St. Clement of Rome * What does this mean? The true direction of the soul toward the truth is more precious than pleasing words in the sight of God, who hears the groanings which cannot be uttered.

A man can use expressions with an opposite meaning (to what they carry outwardly), for the tongue is ready to accomplish that according to the intention and purpose of the speaker, but the direction of the soul is seen by God, who knows the secrets.
St. Gregory of Nyssa

entries.section: 4. The third woe to him who trusts in his own wisdom:

paragraphs.text: 15 Woe unto them that seek deep to hide their counsel from the LORD, and their works are in the dark, and they say, Who seeth us? and who knoweth us? 16 Surely your turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter's clay: for shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?

One of the signs of hypocrisy is that some of the nobles set in their hearts to carry out their own opinion, which was to resort secretly to Egypt against Assyria, in order to hide this matter not only from the people but even from God Himself, saying: "Who seeth us?! and who knoweth us?!" [15]. They thought, though they were the clay, that they were wiser than their Maker!

God, the Maker of man, in His humility wants to converse with man, the clay creature, while the creature in its pride thinks it is able to have knowledge with wisdom and understanding apart from its Maker, away from conversation with Him.

Father Martyrius the Syrian says: [How great is the grace of God's compassion and His condescension, which knows no limits! God comes down to the level of sinners, men and women; the good God speaks with rebellious servants; the Holy One calls the unclean to receive forgiveness. Humanity, created from clay, speaks with its Creator with boldness; the dust wages war against its Maker. Therefore let us show reverence when we, sinners, stand in the presence of this Great One and speak with Him].

17 Is it not yet a very little while, and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be esteemed as a forest? 18 And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness. 19 The meek also shall increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel. 20 For the terrible one is brought to nought, and the scorner is consumed, and all that watch for iniquity are cut off: 21 That make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate, and turn aside the just for a thing of nought. 22 Therefore thus saith the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob, Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now wax pale. 23 But when he seeth his children, the work of mine hands, in the midst of him, they shall sanctify my name, and sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel. 24 They also that erred in spirit shall come to understanding, and they that murmured shall learn doctrine.
If the hidden, deceitful plans filled with hypocrisy bring distress and sorrow, then on the contrary the open saving work of God brings a succession of joys and countless blessings, among them:

A. A state of fruitfulness: "Is it not yet a very little while, and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be esteemed as a forest?" [17]. The open work of God turns Lebanon into a garden or a paradise; it turns the dry and rugged heart of man into the Kingdom of Christ, which bears the fruits of the Spirit; whereas man's deprivation of grace destroys even his natural fruits (the garden), so that it becomes rugged.

B. The gift of hearing the voice of God and seeing the divine mysteries: "And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness" [18]. Spiritual hearing and inner insight are two gifts from God.
C. Enjoying the increasing inner heavenly joy: "The meek also shall increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel" [19].
D. The crushing of the enemy of good, the devil, and all his works, this tyrant who mocks the believers [20].
E. The nullifying of stumbling blocks and of all snares and evil counsels against the righteous children of God [21].
F. The removal of fear and shame: "Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now wax pale" [22].

G. The sanctification of the name of God: "But when he seeth his children (the children of Abraham), the work of mine hands, in the midst of him, they shall sanctify my name, and sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel" [23]. It is as though the saying "Hallowed be Thy name" is fulfilled in them, since the name of God is sanctified in His people and His believers.

H. The change of human nature, so that they carry understanding and knowledge not in a purely rational manner but as a new life obedient to the Lord, after they had walked for a time in the error of ignorance and a life of rebellion and disobedience [24].

All these are the promises of God, which the Church of the New Testament enjoys, rejoicing in the joy of the Lord: her bearing the fruits of the Holy Spirit as the garden of Christ; her enjoyment of hearing the divine voice and seeing His divine mysteries instead of blindness; the crushing of the devil and all the powers of darkness; the overcoming of obstacles and stumbling blocks without fear or shame; and finally the sanctification of the name of God through spiritual understanding and obedience based on spiritual knowledge.

entries.section: 1. A warning against trusting in Pharaoh:

paragraphs.text: 1 "Woe to the rebellious children," saith the LORD, "that carry out a plan, but not of me; and that pour out a libation, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin: 2 That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt! 3 Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion. 4 For his princes were at Zoan, and his ambassadors came to Hanes. 5 They were all ashamed of a people that could not profit them, nor be an help nor profit, but a shame, and also a reproach." 6 The burden of the beasts of the south: into the land of trouble and anguish, from whence come the young and old lion, the viper and fiery flying serpent, they will carry their riches upon the shoulders of young asses, and their treasures upon the bunches of camels, to a people that shall not profit them. 7 For the Egyptians shall help in vain, and to no purpose: therefore have I called her Rahab who sits still.

"Woe to the rebellious children, saith the LORD, that carry out a plan, but not of me; and that pour out a libation, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin: that walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt" [1-2].
Here, in the fourth woe, the following is observed:

A. He calls them rebellious children, because they rejected the counsel of God their Father and did not trust in Him, but counted Pharaoh as their father who would rescue them. Our sonship to God is not words or mere emotions, but a meeting with Him, a reliance upon Him, and an entering with Him into deep, practical relationships; this sonship condemns us if we do not walk as befits it.
B. They carried out a plan [1], that is, they took counsel among themselves and did not seek the counsel of God, nor did they ask His faithful men.

C. "Pour out a libation," or "cover with a covering, but not of my spirit" [1], meaning that they wanted to cover over their counsel and hide from me what they were doing (Isa 29:15-16), so they deprived themselves of the leading of my Holy Spirit.

D. "That they may add sin to sin" [1]. Thus they were sliding down a chain of sins, which began with rebellion against their heavenly Father, since they counted Him unable to protect them, then they took counsel while ignoring His counsel, then they tried to hide their actions, and so on...

entries.section: 1. A warning against trusting in Pharaoh:

paragraphs.text: E. "That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth" [2]; they sent messengers to Pharaoh to ally with him... They went down to Egypt, and did not accept God, who lifts them up to Himself; they accepted going down instead of going up, or descending instead of ascending toward the heavenly things.

The children of God do not accept descending and going down, as it were, to the love of the world (Egypt), but practice constant growth so as to ascend every day toward the heavenly life, saying: "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD" (Mic 4:2).

entries.section: 1. A warning against trusting in Pharaoh:

paragraphs.text: F. The fortress of Pharaoh is counted as shame to them, and the protection of Egypt as a shameful shadow [3]. Their messengers reached Zoan and Hanes seeking help and counsel, and they received shame and confusion.

Zoan was the capital of Upper Egypt, on the eastern bank of the Delta and on the Tanitic branch of the Nile; the kings fortified it and made it a capital to watch for attacks coming upon Egypt from the east. In this city the negotiations between Moses and Pharaoh took place (Ps 78:12, 43); the Assyrians occupied it afterward, and the Greeks called it "Tanis," and today it is called "San el-Hagar."
Hanes lies about 50 miles south of Memphis on the western bank of the Nile, and it is still known as Ehnasya, that is, Ahnasia, and in the Greco-Roman age it was known as Heracleopolis Magna.

entries.section: 1. A warning against trusting in Pharaoh:

paragraphs.text: The prophet likens the messengers coming from Judah to Egypt to Behemoth (the beasts of the south: [6]), meaning a kind of Egyptian crocodile, the hippopotamus. They came seeking help from a land full of hardships and distresses, unable to save itself, full of lions, vipers, and fiery flying serpents; they came carrying their goods on donkeys and camels as gifts to Pharaoh and his men, who were unable to protect them. They came for safety to a region of troubles and deadly dangers.

entries.section: 1. A warning against trusting in Pharaoh:

paragraphs.text: He calls Egypt by a poetic, symbolic name, "Rahab who sits still" [7]; "Rahab" is meant as "the broad," or "the wide," or "the great," or "the proud," for Egypt became proud and arrogant, making beautiful but unrealistic promises, and instead of rising to help the kingdom of Judah and support it, she "sat" watching Judah as it was carried off captive to Babylon.
Thus the prophet Isaiah warns the kingdom of Judah, which was stricken with stupidity and blindness when it resorted to proud Egypt seeking her protection.

entries.section: 2. Disciplines because of despising the commandment of the Lord:

paragraphs.text: 8 Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever: 9 That this is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of the LORD: 10 Which say to the seers, See not; and to the beholders, Behold not for us right things, speak unto us smooth things, behold deceits: 11 Get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us. 12 Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon: 13 Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant. 14 And he shall break it as the breaking of the potters' vessel that is broken in pieces; he shall not spare: so that there shall not be found in the bursting of it a sherd to take fire from the hearth, or to take water withal out of the pit. 15 For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not. 16 But ye said, No; for we will flee upon horses; therefore shall ye flee: and, We will ride upon the swift; therefore shall they that pursue you be swift. 17 One thousand shall flee at the rebuke of one; at the rebuke of five shall ye flee: till ye be left as a beacon upon the top of a mountain, and as an ensign on an hill.

God asked the prophet Isaiah to write a warning to the people of Judah on a large tablet that all could see in a public place, and also to record it in a book so that it might remain forever [8]. Perhaps he wrote on the tablet "Rahab who sits still" to warn them against trusting in Pharaoh (Egypt), who sits watching, while in the book were written the sins of Judah and the prophecies and visions that God gave him.

entries.section: 2. Disciplines because of despising the commandment of the Lord:

paragraphs.text: The chief sin of Judah is that they are a rebellious people who reject the law of the Lord and accept the words of the false prophets. The Law was bitter and harsh to them, because it exposes their sins and demands of them the narrow divine way; therefore they told the prophets, the seers, not to see and not to behold right things, but sought the deceitful words of the false prophets, which he calls here "smooth things" and "deceits" [10], which give the soul a temporary tranquility through ignoring sin and calming consciences. By this they rejected the prophets' standing in their way, and asked that the Holy One of Israel be removed from before them [11].

entries.section: 2. Disciplines because of despising the commandment of the Lord:

paragraphs.text: As for the fruits of disobedience and of rejecting the true prophets and the Holy One of Israel, they are that they became like a high wall that cracks and falls and is shattered in a moment [13], and are likened to a potter's vessel that falls and is crushed completely without pity, so that no part of it is left fit to be used for taking fire from a hearth or water from a pit... Thus it is good for nothing at all except to be gathered and cast into a dunghill...

entries.section: 2. Disciplines because of despising the commandment of the Lord:

paragraphs.text: The prophet portrays the destruction of the kingdom of Judah because they rejected the counsel of the Lord who says: "In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength" [15]; that is, the secret of your salvation is in your repentance and your return to God with stillness and calm in confidence; this is the true strength. But they refused repentance with faith in God, for they said: "No; for we will flee upon horses... therefore shall they that pursue you be swift" [16], that is, they relied on human resources, especially the horses and chariots of Egypt, and thought that they were able to save them quickly, but the enemy pursues them with greater speed and overtakes them. Even more bitter, they flee before nothing, for one soldier of the enemies terrifies a thousand men of the sons of Judah, and five soldiers terrify the whole army of Judah; they leave their weapons and flee in humiliation, to become like a lone tree or a beacon on a mountain, or a banner or a sign on a hill; they become a lesson for all generations.
When King Hezekiah returned to God (2 Kgs 20) and turned toward the wall while on his deathbed, he lifted his mind to heaven and overcame death victoriously.

entries.section: 3. The mercies of God toward His repentant people:

paragraphs.text: 18 And therefore will the LORD wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he rise up, that he may have mercy upon you: for the LORD is a God of truth: blessed are all they that wait for him. 19 For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem: thou shalt weep no more: he will be very gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear it, he will answer thee. 20 And the Lord shall give you bread in distress and water in affliction; thy teachers shall not hide themselves any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers: 21 And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left. 22 Ye shall defile also the covering of thy graven images of silver, and the ornament of thy molten images of gold: thou shalt cast them away as a menstruous cloth; thou shalt say unto it, Get thee hence. 23 Then shall he give the rain of thy seed, that thou shalt sow the ground withal; and bread of the increase of the earth, and it shall be fat and plenteous: in that day shall thy cattle feed in large pastures. 24 The oxen likewise and the young asses that ear the ground shall eat clean provender, which hath been winnowed with the shovel and with the fan. 25 And there shall be upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill, rivers and streams of waters in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall. 26 Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the LORD bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.

"And therefore will the LORD wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he rise up, that he may have mercy upon you: for the LORD is a God of truth: blessed are all they that wait for him" [8].

The prophet Isaiah expects them to return to God and abandon their reliance on the human arm, waiting for the Lord as their Savior; but strangely it is not Isaiah who waits for this, but the Lord Himself, who takes the initiative in love, waiting for their return, longing for them so that He may be gracious to them and have mercy upon them as a God of truth who loves His creation. In His love He waits to pour out the abundance of His grace upon His prodigal son who returns to Him (Lk 15).
The Lord's waiting also means His coming plan for the salvation of many, which is centered on the following points:

entries.section: 3. The mercies of God toward His repentant people:

paragraphs.text: A. The dwelling of His people in Jerusalem: "For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem" [19]; that is, He brings them into the Church of the New Testament, where is the peace of God which passeth all understanding ("Jerusalem" means "the place of peace").
Jerusalem also points to heaven, Jerusalem which is above, which is the mother of us all (Gal 4:26), as though our salvation lies in God's drawing His people to the heavenly life.

B. The removal of sorrow and weeping: "thou shalt weep no more" [19], since the Church is an image of heaven, in which there is no sorrow nor pain... (Rev 21:4). Here he does not mean outward weeping but the loss of inner joy... for the Church shares with her Bridegroom His sufferings, which are not separated from the joy of His resurrection. In other words, the Church is the Kingdom of Christ, which bears the mark of the Cross that is not separated from the Resurrection.

It is fitting for us here to distinguish between sorrow according to the will of God and despondency, or the loss of comfort and peace. Sorrow according to the will of God is a spiritual virtue accompanied by the comforts of God and His peace which passeth all understanding, while despondency is a vice that reveals a state of despair and lack of hope, which destroys the life and will of man. St. John Chrysostom says: [It attacks not only the body but also the soul itself... It is always deadly, draining the strength of the soul". He encouraged the deaconess Olympias to overcome despondency, as a tyrant that dampens the spirits.

C. A swift answer to prayers: "he will be very gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear it, he will answer thee" [19]; He allows distress and affliction, but He hears the cries, so He gives bread and water and does not leave man in want [20].

entries.section: 3. The mercies of God toward His repentant people:

paragraphs.text: D. If the Lord Himself becomes a teacher (Jn 2:23) and His Holy Spirit a leader and comforter for the Church, then one of the Lord's blessings is that He gives the spirit of sincere teaching and straight spiritual guidance without deviation, and a comforter for the Church, then one of the Lord's blessings is that He gives the spirit of sincere teaching and straight spiritual guidance without deviation; "thy teachers shall not hide themselves any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers: and thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left" [21].

Teaching and knowledge are a gift from God Himself, who sanctifies the ear to hear His words and respond to them, and sanctifies the mind, the heart, and the feelings, so that man in his entirety becomes responsive to the will of God as declared through His word.

In this spirit the early Church lived believing that God alone is able to send laborers to His harvest, giving them His grace to speak the word of truth uprightly, and giving the hearers grace to respond to it and understand it.
This also is what moved the Fathers of the Church to persevere in prayers and through a holy life in order to enjoy the gift of divine knowledge.
* Let us urge God to give us, as the word grows in us, so that we may receive the riches of breadth of mind in Christ Jesus, and thus become able to hear the holy, sacred words.
* Many have sought to interpret the divine Scriptures... but not all have succeeded in that. For rarely is there found one who has this grace from God.

Origen Perhaps by the teachers hiding in the Church he means the company of the prophets, for with the coming of the Lord Christ, the unique Teacher, the prophecies are enlightened and the mysteries of the Old Testament, which points to salvation, are revealed, and it declares the person of the Messiah and His saving works and His divine role in the life of the Church.

entries.section: 3. The mercies of God toward His repentant people:

paragraphs.text: E. The rejection of idolatrous worship with all its luxury: "Ye shall defile also the covering of thy graven images of silver, and the ornament of thy molten images of gold: thou shalt cast them away as a menstruous cloth; thou shalt say unto it, Get thee hence" [22].

Since most of the idols were of wood or pottery overlaid with silver or gold, the work of salvation is the exposure of the inside, for man receives by the Spirit of God the power to say to it "Get thee hence"; so it comes out from the outer covering that hides its reality, that it represents the cloth of the unclean menstruous woman, just as it comes out of the heart of the believer who receives the Lord of glory Jesus as sanctified to Him.

Our Christ bears sufferings outwardly, so that He seems to have "no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him" (Isa 53:2), but He gives us His inward glories that cannot be comprehended. As for the love of the world, it gives outward enticements, and inside them is stench and corruption.

entries.section: 3. The mercies of God toward His repentant people:

paragraphs.text: F. The grace of rain: "Then shall he give the rain of thy seed, that thou shalt sow the ground withal; and bread of the increase of the earth, and it shall be fat and plenteous: in that day shall thy cattle feed in large pastures" [23].

The age of the Messiah in the minds of the prophets was "the age of rain" or "the age of abundant waters." We recall, for example, that this age was described as one in which God gives the rain in its season (Ezek 34:26), and the rain waters the earth so that it brings forth an abundance of grain and crops for man to eat and the beasts find rich pasture [23], and so on..., and there is no hunger or thirst (Isa 31:9; 49:10). Living waters flow out from the Temple and bring forth marvelous fruits and very many trees grow (Ezek 47:1-12); an open fountain comes forth for the house of David that cuts off the idols of the earth and removes the unclean spirit (Zech 13:1-2). The springs of Judah flow with water and a fountain comes forth from the house of the Lord that gives life (Joel 3:18; Zech 14:8), making glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the Most High (Ps 46:4).

In short, the Messianic age is linked with the holy waters, which give quenching of thirst and turn the wilderness into a fruitful land, water the believers like the trees of the paradise of God, remove uncleanness and cleanse the earth of idol worship, and offer life and sanctification... These holy waters are Baptism and the gift of the Holy Spirit.
* The first waters brought forth life; let no one wonder if the waters in Baptism can also give life.

Tertullian * You are outside Paradise, O catechumens; you share with Adam your first father in his exile, and now the door is opened (Baptism as a life in Paradise) and you return to where you came out.

entries.section: 3. The mercies of God toward His repentant people:

paragraphs.text: St. Gregory of Nazianzus Thus souls are watered in the Messianic age just as bodies are satisfied, not through temporal pleasures but through their sanctification by the Lord, so that everything is good, blessed, and pure for them. "The oxen likewise and the young asses (a reference to the body) that ear the ground shall eat clean provender, which hath been winnowed with the shovel and with the fan" [24].

It was the custom to leave for the animals that work the land a fodder that is a mixture of straw with a few remains of grain, but in the Messianic age, when good things overflow, salted and winnowed food is offered to the body, that is, the straw and the dust and so on are removed from it, a sign of our care for the body as a good and sacred element for the sake of the Kingdom of God.

With the coming of the Word of God incarnate, our view of the body was sanctified; therefore the Apostle John forbade those who deny that Jesus came in the flesh (1 Jn 4:2; 2 Jn 7); and the early Church resisted the Gnostic thought which said that the body is an element of darkness that must be destroyed.
* The body is not the source of evil, but freedom of choice (free will).
* The body is the dwelling of the soul.
* The body is the instrument of the spirit... working in the company of the soul.
* The Word became flesh in order to change our body into spirit... and in order to sanctify the whole body with Him, since in Him the firstfruits were sanctified.

entries.section: 3. The mercies of God toward His repentant people:

paragraphs.text: St. Gregory of Nyssa "And there shall be upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill, rivers and streams of waters in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall" [25]. It is as though even the high mountains and hills find sufficient water; perhaps this points to the rich grace of God, which overflows not only upon the simple and the common people but also draws kings, rulers, leaders, and nobles to faith, in the day in which those who deny the faith are slain spiritually, those who fell like towers. It was fitting for the Jewish leaders to be towers for the world, seeing the Kingdom of Christ and preaching it, but they became resisters of the truth and so collapsed, a matter that grieved the Apostle Paul.

entries.section: 3. The mercies of God toward His repentant people:

paragraphs.text: G. Great illumination: "Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the LORD bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound" [26].

As the Lord heals the wounds of the soul and the body, sanctifying man in his entirety, with all his powers of instincts, feelings, emotions, mind, and so on..., he bears the image of his Creator, "the true Light," and so becomes a light to the world, a perfect light in the Lord (sevenfold being a sign of perfection), and hears the voice of the heavenly Bridegroom: "Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee" (Song 4:7).

entries.section: 4. The wrath of God against Assyria:

paragraphs.text: 27 Behold, the name of the LORD cometh from far, his anger kindled, and the burning great: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire: 28 And his breath, as an overflowing stream, shall reach to the midst of the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of vanity: and there shall be a bridle in the jaws of the people, causing them to err. 29 Ye shall have a song, as in the night when a holy solemnity is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goeth with a pipe to come into the mountain of the LORD, to the mighty One of Israel. 30 And the LORD shall cause his glorious voice to be heard, and shall shew the lighting down of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and with the flame of a devouring fire, with scattering, and tempest, and hailstones. 31 For through the voice of the LORD shall the Assyrian be beaten down, which smote with a rod. 32 And in every place where the grounded staff shall pass, which the LORD shall lay upon him, it shall be with tabrets and harps: and in battles of shaking will he fight with it. 33 For Tophet is ordained of old; yea, for the king it is prepared; he hath made it deep and large: the pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it.

Most scholars see that what is mentioned here is a description of the destruction that fell upon the army of Sennacherib, although Assyria with its army and its commander represents the powers of darkness that bear enmity against God under the leadership of the devil himself, who seeks to storm the Church of the Lord, our inner Jerusalem, in order to sit enthroned in the holy temple of our hearts.

A. "Behold, the name of the LORD cometh from far, his anger kindled, and the burning great: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire: and his breath, as an overflowing stream, shall reach to the midst of the neck" [27].
