Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father” (Phil 2:8-11).

In the moments of suffering, when the Lord of glory appeared as in weakness, He said: “I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do. And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was” (Jn 17:4-5).

If the Cross is shame and weakness outwardly, yet it is glory inwardly. Origen says: [We do not hesitate to say that the goodness of Christ appears in a greater way and with the divine light... for “he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross” (Phil 2:6-8)].

The Cross is also glory because it reconciled the Father with mankind, and opened before us the door of Paradise that we may share the Lord’s glory and live with Him praising Him with the heavenly ones.

Some see that what is said here also concerns the Church hidden in the Savior, as the new Israel, which glorifies God through accepting fellowship in the sufferings and crucifixion with her Christ and so enjoys the power of His resurrection and its joy; therefore she deserved to hear the divine voice: “Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” But she, in her sufferings, says: “I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the LORD, and my work with my God” [4].

e. The success of the mission of the Lord Christ in bringing the Gentiles into the faith: if the Lord appeared on the Cross in weakness until all forsook Him, for He came unto His own, and His own received Him not (Jn 1:11), and became wounded in the house of His friends (Zech 13:6), so He said: “I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain” [4]; this is the outward appearance of the Cross, but its inward work is declared by the Father with power, saying to the Crucified One: “It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth” [6]. It is as though He were saying to the crucified Son: Your work of redemption cannot have its fruit confined within the limits of a particular people, but extends to the end of the earth, so that you are a light to the Gentiles and the mystery of divine salvation for all mankind.

When the elder Simeon carried the Child Jesus he said: “For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; a light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel” (Lk 2:30-31). As Paul and Barnabas said: “For so hath the Lord commanded us, saying, I have set thee to be a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldest be for salvation unto the ends of the earth” (Acts 13:46-47). Origen says: [Had He not become a servant He would not have raised up the tribes of Jacob nor changed the heart of scattered Israel, and would not have become a light to the Gentiles for the salvation of the end of the earth].

Our Christ came as a light to the peoples and the Gentiles; the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world (Jn 1:9), calling us out of darkness into light (1 Pet 2:9) that we may walk in the light and become children of light and children of the day (1 Thess 5:5), and even become the light of the world (Mt 5:14). By this the saying of the prophet Isaiah is fulfilled: [The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God oil; thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon be diminished: for the LORD shall be thine everlasting light] (Isa 60:19-20). The Savior, the light of the Gentiles, shines upon the soul as His bride, so she perceives the secrets of wisdom (Job 11:6).
* My Lord and my God... O light of my soul! Never cease to illumine my steps...!
My God... You are my hope... without Your light, by which we behold everything, it is difficult for us to discover the maneuvers of Satan and his wiles.

* You are the Word who said: “Let there be light,” and there was light. Say this word now also, that my eyes may be enlightened by the true light, and I may distinguish it from other light; for without You how can I distinguish light from darkness, and darkness from light?!

entries.section: 1. The humility and glorification of the Savior:

paragraphs.text: St. Augustine The Jews insulted Him and denied Him, seeking His crucifixion, and the pagan peoples received Him, submitted to Him by faith and accepted His work. Therefore the Lord was called “him whom man despiseth,” “him whom the nation abhorreth,” “a servant of rulers,” for the wicked ruled over Him and hated Him and insulted Him; and at the same time it is said, “Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship” [7]. For kings rise from their thrones in His presence, and princes worship Him in adoration.

8 “Thus saith the LORD, In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee: and I will preserve thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages; 9 That thou mayest say to the prisoners, Go forth; to them that are in darkness, Shew yourselves. They shall feed in the ways, and their pastures shall be in all high places. 10 They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun smite them: for he that hath mercy on them shall lead them, even by the springs of water shall he guide them. 11 And I will make all my mountains a way, and my highways shall be exalted. 12 Behold, these shall come from far: and, lo, these from the north and from the west; and these from the land of Sinim. 13 Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into singing, O mountains: for the LORD hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.”
Before us is a wonderful divine address that reveals the mystery of our salvation in Jesus Christ our inexpressible Lord; for in Christ the Savior we receive the following:

a. God’s answering us; the time has come for the Father to hear us through His beloved Son crucified as a sacrifice of obedience to the Father and the object of His pleasure, so that the Father answers us in Him, giving Himself to us as Father, offering us His bosom as a place of eternal rest in which we settle. This is what He meant by His saying, “In an acceptable time have I heard thee” [8]. The time has come in which our acceptance with the Father is declared in His Son, accepted from eternity, so He answers us continually.

b. Through Christ Jesus our Savior, God Himself has become a help and helper to us: “and in a day of salvation have I helped thee” [8]. The Lord Himself took over the leading of the battle against the enemy of good that we may hide in Him and obtain in Him the victory and triumph. As the Apostle says: “Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place” (2 Cor 2:14). St. Augustine says: [This is the day in which the Intercessor became the chief cornerstone; let us rejoice and be glad in it].

It is fitting for us to distinguish between “the day of salvation” [8] or “the day of the Lord” and our own days; the day of the Lord is joyful and gives salvation, but our days in which we walk according to our desire are destructive and ruinous. St. Augustine says: [Rather I call my days (Ps 116:2) the days of my misery, the days of my death, the days according to Adam, full of toil and sweat, the days according to the old corruption. For he cries in another psalm: “I sink in deep mire” (Ps 69:2), “Behold, You have made my days old” (Ps 39:5); in these days of mine I call upon You (Ps 61:2). For my days are different from the days of my Lord].

c. By the Crucified One we have also become preserved in the Lord, for He says: “I will preserve thee” [9]. In the farewell prayer the Savior says: “I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil... Sanctify them in thy truth” (Jn 17:15, 17).

d. The enjoyment of the Crucified One as a covenant with the Father: “and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages” [8]. God gave His new covenant not engraved on stones but recorded in blood in the body of the Son, the incarnate Word; through this covenant the Church does not enjoy the land of promise flowing with milk and honey, but inherits the earth, that is, the peoples who were desolate like the wildernesses, to establish from them a divine paradise and a heavenly kingdom. In the body of His humanity He reconciled the Father with humanity and established in every truly believing heart an inexpressible inheritance.
The characteristics of this new Kingdom, or inner inheritance, or Gospel life, the true Church, are:

First: Freedom; “That thou mayest say to the prisoners, Go forth; to them that are in darkness, Shew yourselves” [9]. He broke the bars of Hades and gave us the freedom of the glory of the children of God, so that we live bearing authority over serpents and scorpions and all the power of the enemy (Lk 10:19), walking in the light, with no authority of darkness over us.

Our Savior gave us inner freedom, so that we are not enslaved to the enemy of good, nor to the lusts of the flesh, nor to the love of the world; but what is more important is that we are not enslaved to the ego, that we no longer shut ourselves up in the ego, but are crucified with our Savior Christ to declare the breadth of our heart, to bear in it the unlimited God, and that it may have room for every human being, even those who oppose us.
Through this inner freedom we accept willingly to submit to God as His servants, so we live free, with no authority of the enemy over our depths.
* Be a servant and free at the same time; be a servant by your submission to God, free, not enslaved to anything, neither to empty praise nor to any passion.

* Free yourself from the chains of sin, live in freedom, for Christ has made you free (Gal 5:1). Seek the freedom of the new world during your temporal life. Do not enslave yourself to the love of money nor to praise that comes from pleasing people.
* Do not set a rule for yourself lest you be enslaved to rules of your own making. Be free, a human being in a position that allows him to do what he wills.
* Free yourself from the yoke of the world by the freedom of the new life.

* Be free, free yourself from every ruinous bondage; for if you do not become free, do not be a worker for Christ, for the kingdom of the heavenly, free Jerusalem does not accept the children of bondage. The children of the free mother are themselves free (Rom 8:5), and are not enslaved to the world in anything.
* Do not bind yourself to an effort beyond your capacity, lest you enslave yourself to the need to please others.

Abba John the Syrian the Solitary Second: The enjoyment of a rich divine pasture, “They shall feed in the ways, and their pastures shall be in all high places” [9]. What is this way but the Savior who called Himself “the Way” (Jn 14:6)? By Him we enter into fruitful high places to find all our needs, so we neither hunger nor thirst, nor does heat or sun smite us; in them are the springs of the Holy Spirit as living waters that water our depths and give us fruit [10].

Third: The enjoyment of a smoothed way that brings us into the divine embraces, “And I will make all my mountains a way, and my highways shall be exalted” [11]. What are these mountains but the commandments of the Lord, which seem like lofty mountains difficult to climb, but by our union with Christ “the Way,” walking over the mountains becomes natural, and the commandment turns into delight and joy, not harsh commands and deprivation.

At the time when He makes the difficult commandment easy, as He turns His lofty mountains into a way in which we rejoice to pass, He says, “and my highways (my paths) shall be exalted,” meaning that the ease of the commandment does not mean our descending to lower things and being lenient with ourselves in accepting bodily pleasures and fulfilling temporal desires, but on the contrary He carries us by His paths upward to practice the heavenly, exalted life with gladness of heart and joy, as a life that is acceptable and joyful in the Lord.

Fourth: The opening of the doors of the Church before all the Gentiles from the east and west and north and south. “Behold, these shall come from far: and, lo, these from the north and from the west; and these from the land of Sinim” [12]. By those coming from afar He means the inhabitants of the Far East, and by the land of Sinim (Aswan) He means the south of Egypt, as representing those coming from the south.

Fifth: The enjoyment of the life of praise and joy as a life lived by the soul (the heavens) and practiced by the body (the earth) and expressed by the salvation of human energies (the mountains). Thus the heavens share with the earth and its mountains in singing to the Lord, “for the LORD hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted” [13].

The secret of our joy is God’s comforts declared by the Holy Spirit in our depths through the merits of the precious Blood, for the Crucified One raised us from our misery and had compassion on us with His practical mercy.

This joy spreads over the whole Church extending here through the generations and also in heaven; therefore St. Pope Athanasius the Apostolic says: [We are not alone in our joy, for in heaven the whole “church of the firstborn” (Heb 12:23) rejoices with us... See, my friends, all creation keeps the feast with us, for the psalmist says: “Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD” (Ps 150:5), and that because of the destruction of the enemies of the Lord and because of our salvation].

Now we have seen how the Lord moved from speaking of Cyrus as the rescuer of the people of God from captivity to what is greater and more lasting, speaking of the Lord Christ as the Savior of all humanity, rescuing them from eternal captivity to grant them the blessings of His salvation by bringing them into His Kingdom, that is, the enjoyment of the new, joyful life of the Church in the Lord, as a paradisal life offered to all peoples and nations.

entries.section: 3. The raising of the forsaken one as an eternal bride:

paragraphs.text: 14 “But Zion said, The LORD hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me. 15 Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee. 16 Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands; thy walls are continually before me. 17 Thy children shall make haste; thy destroyers and they that made thee waste shall go forth of thee. 18 Lift up thine eyes round about, and behold: all these gather themselves together, and come to thee. As I live, saith the LORD, thou shalt surely clothe thee with them all, as with an ornament, and bind them on thee, as a bride doth. 19 For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants, and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away. 20 The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell. 21 Then shalt thou say in thine heart, Who hath begotten me these, seeing I have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro? and who hath brought up these? Behold, I was left alone; these, where had they been?”

The people of God did not expect to be taken captive, and when Israel, the northern kingdom, was taken captive, the kingdom of Judah thought that it would not be taken captive because it embraced the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem, the city of God. But Judah was taken captive and Jerusalem collapsed with the temple, which they had defiled with idolatrous worship and abominations, as is recorded in Ezekiel and Jeremiah. The captives thought that it would perhaps be a few months and God would intervene to free them, but months passed and years upon years, so the people thought that God had forgotten them, and all felt isolation, deprivation and abandonment. This is what the prophet expressed here thus: “But Zion said, The LORD hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me” [14]. This feeling of isolation is a natural fruit suffered by most human beings, if not all of them, at some moments. For man in the time of trial feels himself alone, with no one to share his feelings and sensations and no one to touch his inner bitterness.

Psychologists complain of this disease, “the feeling of isolation,” as a disease that is almost universal, especially among adolescents, when they realize that those closest to them cannot understand the reality of their inner world and their hidden feelings.

The cure for this disease is the meeting with the Savior, who alone can enter into the depths and raise His banner as love, declaring by His Cross a unique personal friendship through which we enjoy a surpassing divine love and a union with God that time cannot and events cannot shatter. By the Cross God gathered humanity to Himself as a holy heavenly bride whom her heavenly Bridegroom does not forsake, instead of the feeling of abandonment.

And, wonderfully, the Savior Himself cried out on the Cross, saying: “Eloi, Eloi... why hast thou forsaken me?!” (Mk 15:34). It is as though, as the representative of humanity and in its stead, He declares our position as forsaken and deprived! By the Cross He became as one forsaken in order to remove from us the feeling of deprivation and abandonment and to return us to the divine embraces as a holy bride!
Now how does the Lord answer Zion’s feeling of deprivation?

entries.section: 3. The raising of the forsaken one as an eternal bride:

paragraphs.text: “Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee” [15]. Without doubt motherhood is considered one of the highest degrees of human love, for the mother who carries her son or daughter as a fetus for months in her womb can hardly forget him after his birth. And yet some mothers have forgotten their sons and daughters, for some of them offered their children as human sacrifices, casting them into the fire amid the beating of drums as a kind of worship to the god Baal. And in some famines we hear of mothers who ate their children. And we still hear now of crimes of killing committed by some mothers against their children. And every day we also see mothers and fathers killing their children through the gloomy family atmosphere or family problems, especially separation and divorce. How many are the victims of divorce?! Fathers and mothers have had no mercy on the new generations, nor have they given them any account in their lives, but in selfishness they wish to achieve what they think is peace at the expense of the lives of their children and their spiritual and psychological peace and sometimes their social and material well-being also.
A mother may forget her infant, but God does not forget us!

* This care of God and His love, which the Lord shows by His goodness... He compares them to the heart of a mother full of tenderness and kindness, as He wants to express it by an example of human affection, for He found in His creation no better feelings of love with which to compare.
Abba Chaeremon * He not only cares for us, but loves us without limit, a holy burning love, an intense true love that cannot be broken or quenched...

* The prophet answers those who were once depressed and groaned, saying, “The LORD hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me,” saying: “Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb?” It is as though he says: It is impossible for a mother to forget her infant, so much the more will the Lord not forget humanity. By this he does not mean to liken God’s love for us to the love of a mother for the fruit of her womb, but because a mother’s love surpasses every love, yet God’s love is surely greater than it. Therefore He says: “yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee, saith the Lord.” Consider how God’s love surpasses a mother’s love...?!

The Lord of the prophets and the Master of all affirms that His love surpasses the love of a father for his children, as light surpasses darkness and good surpasses evil... Listen to what He says: “Or what man of you, if his son ask a fish, will he give him a serpent? If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?” (Mt 7:9-11). As good differs from evil, so the love of God is higher than the affections of parents...
There are other examples, such as the love of a lover for his beloved, yet this love will not equal God’s love (Ps 103:11)..

entries.section: 3. The raising of the forsaken one as an eternal bride:

paragraphs.text: St. John Chrysostom “Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands” [16]. It was among the ancient Eastern customs that a person engraves the name of his beloved on his palm, as a sign that he will not forget her until death, and that all he does with his hands is on behalf of his beloved. The Lord engraved the name of His beloved Church on His palm with the nails, so that the marks of the wounds might remain a sign of eternal love! Indeed, He engraved the name of every member in her on His palm as a sign of His personal love for us by our names.

“Thy walls are continually before me” [16]; as though He says: I know that your walls have been broken down, I will not forget them, I will build them but at the appointed time, I will restore to you your strength and your fortification, and I will return your sons to My land and drive out the destroyers and wasters from it [17].

Who are these sons hastening to Zion but those who accept the faith, who come to the Church of the New Testament and enjoy its walls, which are not made by human hands; as for the destroyers and wasters, they are those who deny the faith, who are driven out of it.

entries.section: 3. The raising of the forsaken one as an eternal bride:

paragraphs.text: “Lift up thine eyes round about, and behold: all these gather themselves together, and come to thee. As I live, saith the LORD, thou shalt surely clothe thee with them all, as with an ornament, and bind them on thee, as a bride doth” [18]. What a splendid picture of the Church of the New Testament! For instead of the city whose walls were broken down, whose people were driven out as captives, and which the destroyers and wasters entered, the Lord establishes the Church of the New Testament not merely as a fortified city to which her children return in haste and from which the wicked wasters are driven out, but she becomes a heavenly bride bearing a unique adornment, which is the gathering of her children in her as children of God, who have the freedom of inner glory. In the East a woman’s beauty was her children; she boasted in them as her glory and as her continual wedding garment; so the Church takes pride in her children glorified in her, like a precious bridal girdle with which she girds herself.

She becomes a fruitful bride, a fertile mother, whose spiritual children multiply until it seems that the earth has become too narrow for them and there is no place for the wasters to dwell with them.

entries.section: 3. The raising of the forsaken one as an eternal bride:

paragraphs.text: The enemy does not stand silent but wants to enter and ruin her children, he who earlier bereaved her by destroying the faith of some, for he says to her: “The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell” [20]. But she sees the wonderful hand of God working in her despite the continual opposition of the enemy, and repeats in her heart, saying: “Who hath begotten me these, seeing I have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro? and who hath brought up these? Behold, I was left alone; these, where had they been?” [21]. It is the surpassing grace of God that brings forth food out of the eater and sweetness out of the strong! It is His rich grace that raises up in us abundant fruit, not of ourselves, but a free gift of God to His believers who walk by the Spirit.

entries.section: 4. The humbled one raised to be a queen:

paragraphs.text: 22 Thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I will lift up mine hand to the Gentiles, and set up my standard to the people: and they shall bring thy sons in their arms, and thy daughters shall be carried upon their shoulders. 23 And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me.

If Zion lived as a humbled captive nation in a foreign land, she now returns to her homeland as a queen, whom all long to lift up on their shoulders, and to whom kings submit and before whom they bow down, licking the dust of her feet.
This is God's work in the life of the soul that sin had previously humbled: the Lord raises her up as a queen, seated at the right hand of the King, and all long to serve her.

“Thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I will lift up mine hand to the Gentiles, and set up my standard to the people” [22]. What is the lifting up of the hand but the coming of the Lord Christ into the world to stretch out His hands on the Cross and so gather the Gentiles to Himself, as He said: “And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me” (Jn 12:32)? And the standard that He sets up is “his banner over me was love” (Song 2:4), that is, the proclamation of redemption on the Cross.

By this work of salvation the Church of Christ is glorified, when it is said to her: “They shall bring thy sons in their arms, and thy daughters shall be carried upon their shoulders. And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me” [22-23].
This has been fulfilled, for kings and queens have become believers working in the Church of the Lord, such as Constantine the Great and Helena, serving the Church as a spiritual queen above all.

entries.section: 5. God the Redeemer of His Church:

paragraphs.text: 24 Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered? 25 But thus saith the LORD, Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered: for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children. 26 And I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.

These promises seemed like a fantasy to Isaiah's contemporaries, and later also to the captives; therefore God affirmed that it is He Himself who accomplishes this salvation, being the only One able to crush the mighty devil and to draw out from him those whom he had previously taken captive.

“Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered? But thus saith the LORD, Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered: for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children. And I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob” [24-26].

So it is fitting for us to trust in God our Savior and not to be troubled before the cruelty and violence of the devil, for the Savior is able to free us from his captivity however fierce and mighty the enemy may be. He brings us back to His Church and contends with those who contend with us, that is, He leads the battle Himself; so the enemy eats his own flesh and drinks and becomes drunk as with his own blood, that is, his work returns upon his own head and he tastes the bitterness of his own violence until he loses consciousness like one who is drunk.

1 Thus saith the LORD, Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement, whom I have put away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities have ye sold yourselves, and for your transgressions is your mother put away. 2 Wherefore, when I came, was there no man? when I called, was there none to answer? Is my hand shortened at all, that it cannot redeem? or have I no power to deliver? behold, at my rebuke I dry up the sea, I make the rivers a wilderness: their fish stinketh, because there is no water, and dieth for thirst. 3 I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering.

When a Jew divorced his wife, even without an acceptable reason, he gave her a bill of divorcement and drove her out of his house; he could also sell her as a maidservant to his creditors (Deut 24:1-3), and he was permitted to sell his children to his creditors. But God did not do so to them. He asks the Jewish nation, which denied Him and refused to believe in Him, for its bill of divorcement, affirming to her that He did not wish to divorce her or to drive her out; rather, she divorced herself and drove herself out of the house of God, her Bridegroom, through her adultery and her abominations, and so broke the holy marriage.

“Thus saith the LORD, Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement, whom I have put away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities have ye sold yourselves, and for your transgressions is your mother put away” [1].

“He came unto his own, and his own received him not” (Jn 1:11). Therefore, in a fatherly reproach, He asks those who refuse faith to show a bill of divorcement or the name of the creditor to whom He delivered His children; as if He were saying to them: I do not wish to divorce your mother, nor to sell you to anyone. She chose the devil, my enemy, as a bridegroom for herself, and you sold yourselves for the pleasures and lusts of sin, just as the Lord Christ said to His opponents: “Ye are of your father the devil” (Jn 8:44).

Abba Abraham says in Cassian's Conferences: [The very pleasures in which we delight (in sin) become a punishment for us, and the delights and enjoyments turn into something like torments for the one who pursues them.]

Origen sees that the Jewish synagogue committed adultery against the Bridegroom and killed Him (Jn 19:6, 15; Lk 23:18): [She (as a bride) rose up against her husband more than he rose up against her, he who drove her out and cast her away, rebuking her for her departure from him.]

If He drove her out, it was only because she left Him and drove herself out, so He gave her the desire of her wicked heart. The Lord Christ came as to His own house and found no one, for she had left it, taking the children with her [2]. He called her, that perhaps she might be softened toward her husband and return to Him, but she did not answer [2]; she did not welcome Him nor respond to His call, but deprived Him of all His rights as husband and father.

St. John Chrysostom says: [He speaks these things to show that we are the ones who began the desertion, and that this causes our destruction. God does not wish to leave us or to punish us; even when He punishes, He does so unwillingly, for He says: “I have no pleasure in the death of the sinner, as that he should turn and live” [(Ezek 18:32) Septuagint]. Jesus weeps over the destruction of Jerusalem as we do over our friends.]

God does not want our destruction, but seeks that we be always fervent in spirit, like a bride rejoicing in her bridegroom, and not like a rebellious wife who leaves her house. As St. John Chrysostom says: [He goes deeper, giving an example that penetrates the deepest matters, saying: “As the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee” (Isa 62:5). For love is at its height at the beginning (between the bride and bridegroom). He used this manner of speaking not to attribute anything human to Himself, but that we might sense the intensity of the burning of His true love...]

For her part, she left Him and refused to live in the joy of the everlasting heavenly wedding; but for His part, He works on their behalf as a Savior who redeems them with His life, mighty and not unable to act for their sake, for He says: “Is my hand shortened at all, that it cannot redeem? or have I no power to deliver? behold, at my rebuke I dry up the sea, I make the rivers a wilderness: their fish stinketh, because there is no water, and dieth for thirst. I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering” [2-3].

The Lord Himself came as to His own house to save, after He had called her through the Law and the Prophets; He came to save, and yet in mockery His maidservant nation and His own said: “He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him” (Mt 27:42).

Thus His maidservant nation mocked Him, though it was He who made for her a way through the Red Sea and the river Jordan; and at His crucifixion nature was stirred, so the sun was darkened and the moon was eclipsed, and darkness came upon the face of the earth.

4 The Lord GOD hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary: he wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as the learned. 5 The Lord GOD hath opened mine ear, and I was not rebellious, neither turned away back. 6 I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting. 7 For the Lord GOD will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed. 8 He is near that justifieth me; who will contend with me? let us stand together: who is mine adversary? let him come near to me. 9 Behold, the Lord GOD will help me; who is he that shall condemn me? lo, they all shall wax old as a garment; the moth shall eat them up.

Some scholars and Fathers see that the speaker here is the prophet Isaiah, who declared that God gave him the tongue of the learned so that he might comfort weary souls with the living word of the Lord; this word has no fixed time but works in him every morning, giving him a spiritual ear able to listen to the divine voice [4].
* “He wakeneth (adds to) mine ear to hear” [4].

It means the addition (of the ear) which is from the Spirit... For after the Spirit gave him the heart of the prophets, he no longer had a human heart but became one with a spiritual heart, as the Apostle said: “We have the mind of Christ” (1 Cor 2:16). It is as though he says: I have received the blessing of the Spirit and have learned the things which a man cannot utter, which none of us, nor of the prophets, could comprehend by his own mind.

St. John Chrysostom * The prophet heard more than many (prophets), and so the faithful also hear more than the catechumens. Here the catechumens, too, must realize that they are not learning these things from men but are taught of God (Isa 54:13).

St. John Chrysostom If the prophet speaks of himself as having enjoyed an additional spiritual ear, perhaps this means more than many prophets enjoyed, for the prophet also speaks of himself as a type of the Lord Christ, just as David the prophet earlier spoke of himself as a type of the Messiah.
Although the Lord Christ came as a Teacher of mankind, He came as unique in this in respect of the following:

a. Being the Word of God, the Giver of wisdom, knowledge and understanding, He took on our humanity and became the Son of Man who submits and obeys. He is the Hebrew servant who of his own will came forward to his master at the Jubilee to have his ear pierced, out of His zeal for His Father's house (Ezek 21:6). Therefore He says: “The Lord GOD hath opened mine ear, and I was not rebellious, neither turned away back” [5]. He offered Himself willingly not only to have His ears pierced but to lay down His life, and so He was obedient unto death, even the death of the Cross.

In His obedience that gives of itself and is full of love, He offered not only His ears to be pierced, but also His back to be beaten, His cheeks to those who plucked out the hair, and His face to shame and spitting... He offered all His life, bearing sufferings, that we the disobedient might be counted obedient in Him, and that we who suffer might find rest in Him.

* Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ is an example for us of how to suffer... By His own will He allowed them to lead Him to death, and so we see in Him the image of all goodness and immortality. In this He is an example for us; if we follow Him we shall be able to tread upon serpents and scorpions and all the power of the enemy.

Pope Athanasius the Apostolic * You may say: The enemy is terrifying and dangerous and cannot be endured. Look at him again and compare him with another picture, and you will learn to despise him. For the accusations, the insults, the rebukes and the reproaches that the enemies pour out together with their plots are like a worn-out garment and wool eaten by the moth [9]... Therefore let nothing of what happens weary you; cease seeking the help of this man or that, and running after shadows, but call with persistence on Jesus whom you serve, for when He bows His head, in a moment of time all evils come to an end.
St. John Chrysostom * He chose to bear all these things only to comfort those who suffer.

St. Augustine In a clear and explicit prophecy, the prophet Isaiah spoke of the events of the Cross, saying in the words of the Savior: “I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting” [6].
* You have shown me the economy of Your compassion.
You bore the injustice of the wicked; You gave Your back to the scourges, and Your cheeks You left to the slaps. For my sake, O my Lord, You did not turn Your face from the shame of spitting.
You came to the slaughter like a lamb, even to the Cross...
The Gregorian Liturgy * That fool, how did he dare to spit in His face?!
How did you dare, O tongue, to pour out spittle...?!
How did you bear, O earth, the mockery of the Son...?!
A fearful sight, full of astonishment, that a man should see wax standing up and spitting in the face of the flame...
And this also happened for the sake of Adam, because he deserved to be spat upon, for he had fallen! And in place of the servant the Master stood up to receive all this!
He offered His face to receive the spitting, because He promised in Isaiah that He would not turn away His face from bearing the shame of spitting...!

Mar Jacob of Sarug The Lord Christ gave Himself up to sufferings to the very depths, bearing all shame and disgrace in order to complete the way of obedience for us and in our name, declaring the inability of pain and disgrace to crush the faithful, and affirming that the way of the Cross is royal and leads us into His righteousness, for He says: “I know that I shall not be ashamed. He is near that justifieth me” [7-8]. The Apostle Paul says: “The redemption that is in Christ Jesus: whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness” (Rom 3:25).
* But what does he mean by saying “to declare his righteousness”...? Not only in that He is righteous, but that He makes those who are full of the foul sores of sin righteous...
Therefore doubt not... Do not reject the righteousness of God, which is not by the works (of the Law) but by (living) faith, and is easy and open to all.
St. John Chrysostom

10 Who is among you that feareth the LORD, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the LORD, and stay upon his God. 11 Behold, all ye that kindle a fire, that compass yourselves about with sparks: walk in the light of your fire, and in the sparks that ye have kindled. This shall ye have of mine hand; ye shall lie down in sorrow.

The Lord obeyed in order to call us to obedience, and so He became an example for us, and also a help in whom we hide so that we may walk the way of obedience... for He says: “Who is among you that feareth the LORD, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the LORD, and stay upon his God” [10].
It is as though whoever wishes to enjoy the light of obedience and to hearken to the voice of the Lord and His Christ should trust in Him to rescue him from the darkness of disobedience.

He likens the disobedient to those who kindle a fire of their own making [11] in order to offer to the Lord strange incense, not the incense of obedience mingled with love, but the incense of selfishness and reliance on the self... Therefore it is fitting for us not to kindle the fire of our own righteousness and human wisdom, but to receive the fire of the Holy Spirit of God, the Giver of righteousness and of obedience to the commandment.

* Let us not walk in the light of our fire [11] and the flame that we ourselves have kindled, for I know a purifying fire which Christ sent on the earth (Lk 12:49), and He Himself in a symbolic way appeared as a fire that scatters what is material in evil habits. This fire He wishes to kindle quickly, for He longs to hasten us to the doing of good.
St. Gregory of Nazianzus

entries.section: 1. A call to enjoy the work of redemption:

paragraphs.text: 1 Hearken to me, ye that follow after righteousness, ye that seek the LORD: look unto the rock whence ye are hewn, and to the hole of the pit whence ye are digged. 2 Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him. 3 For the LORD shall comfort Zion: he will comfort all her waste places; and he will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody. 4 Hearken unto me, my people; and give ear unto me, O my nation: for a law shall proceed from me, and I will make my judgment to rest for a light of the people. 5 My righteousness is near; my salvation is gone forth, and mine arms shall judge the people; the isles shall wait upon me, and on mine arm shall they trust. 6 Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath: for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished. 7 Hearken unto me, ye that know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law; fear ye not the reproach of men, neither be ye afraid of their revilings. 8 For the moth shall eat them up like a garment, and the worm shall eat them like wool: but my righteousness shall be for ever, and my salvation from generation to generation. 9 Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD; awake, as in the ancient days, in the generations of old. Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab, and wounded the dragon? 10 Art thou not it which hath dried the sea, the waters of the great deep; that hath made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over? 11 Therefore the redeemed of the LORD shall return, and come with singing unto Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their head: they shall obtain gladness and joy; and sorrow and mourning shall flee away. 12 I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die, and of the son of man which shall be made as grass; 13 And forgettest the LORD thy maker, that hath stretched forth the heavens, and laid the foundations of the earth; and hast feared continually every day because of the fury of the oppressor, as if he were ready to destroy? and where is the fury of the oppressor? 14 The captive exile hasteneth that he may be loosed, and that he should not die in the pit, nor that his bread should fail. 15 But I am the LORD thy God, that divided the sea, whose waves roared: The LORD of hosts is his name. 16 And I have put my words in thy mouth, and I have covered thee in the shadow of mine hand, that I may plant the heavens, and lay the foundations of the earth, and say unto Zion, Thou art my people.

In this call the word “hearken” or “give ear” is repeated three times [1, 4, 7]. If the “Word of God,” who is the Creator, the Judge and the Lawgiver, heard and obeyed, then all the more should His people be marked by a spirit of obedience... It is as though we cannot enter into the life of the Gospel and enjoy the free salvation unless we hear and give ear, that the Lord may work in us.
What is the content of the call?
a. The repetition of the word “hearken” means that the call is at its core an exhortation to obedience, the obedience of faith, full of trust in God and love.
* [Obedience makes friends of God.] He says: “If ye love me, keep my commandments” (Jn 14:15); He did not say “work miracles,” but what did He say? “Keep my commandments.”
Again: “Ye are my friends” (Jn 15:14) not when you cast out demons but “if ye do whatsoever I command you”... Let us strive to become friends of God and not remain His enemies.

St. John Chrysostom b. “Hearken to me, ye that follow after righteousness, ye that seek the LORD” [1]. Through obedience, hearing is turned into practical conduct, that is, following righteousness or walking in the way of God's righteousness, and the goal of this is seeking the Lord, meeting Him and being united with Him. This is our faith, and this is our Christianity: hearing, obedience, life, union with the Lord!

c. Imitating the faith of Abraham: “Look unto the rock whence ye are hewn, and to the hole of the pit whence ye are digged. Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him” [1-2].

It is as though He says to them: if you find the call difficult, saying, how can we hear the voice of the Lord and follow His righteousness and seek Him in our life? Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah who bore you. Abraham came from a pagan family; indeed the whole world at that time had turned away from the knowledge of God, so Abraham came as though from hard rock and from clay in the hole of a pit. He heard from his parents no word of comfort; no divine law had been delivered, and no priest or prophet supported him; yet when I called him he responded. He was alone in his faith, so I blessed him and increased him... and my people came from his seed!

Truly, if we admit that Adam was created from dust, and that we have been formed from rock, with no spiritual sense, and have wallowed as in the mire of the pit, let us not despair, for our father Abraham was also of the seed of Adam, and he accepted the call and obeyed and received the divine promises in his seed.
Abraham was an old man and Sarah his wife was barren; her womb was like lifeless rock, unable to bear children, yet God raised up children to Abraham from stones.
* God is able to bring forth men from stones... For the child conceived in a petrified womb is like one born of stones...
Now in this prophecy [1-2] you see that He shows them that from the beginning He raised up a father in a miraculous way, as though from stones, and what happened before can be fulfilled now (Mt 3:5).

St. John Chrysostom * God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham (Mt 3:9). He refers here to the Gentiles, for they are stones because of the hardness of their hearts. Let us read: “And I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh” (Ezek 36:26). For stone is an image of hardness, and flesh a symbol of gentleness. He wanted to show the power of God, who is able to create out of hard stones a believing people.

entries.section: 1. A call to enjoy the work of redemption:

paragraphs.text: St. Jerome d. A call of consolation, for God turns her ruins and deserts into a garden of the Lord, or a paradise. This is God's work in His Church: He gives the fruits of His Holy Spirit to His people, so that all become a kingdom bearing fruit in the Spirit. “For the LORD shall comfort Zion: he will comfort all her waste places; and he will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD” [3].

The Book of Isaiah often speaks of God's work of salvation as the establishing of the fruitful Kingdom of God, and the turning of the wilderness into a spiritual orchard (Isa 32:5), in which truth dwells (Isa 32:6), which rejoices and exults in God who dwells in it (Isa 35:1), and so on... He who makes of it a paradise and a heaven.

St. John Chrysostom looked upon the Church, especially when she celebrates the liturgy of the Eucharist (the Divine Liturgy), as heaven, saying: [She is higher than heaven and wider than the whole world. He speaks in the person of the Lord Christ, saying:
“I planted you in paradise, and Satan drove you out!
Behold, I plant you in Myself!
I support you, so that Satan no longer has the power to approach you.
I do not lift you up to heaven, but to here, where the Lord of heaven is.
I carry you within Me, I, the Lord of heaven!”].

St. Clement of Alexandria says: [The earthly Church is the icon of the heavenly Church; therefore we pray that the will of God be done on earth as it is in heaven. And he says: [If you enroll yourself as one of the members of the people of God, heaven becomes your city and God your lawgiver.]

e. A call to joy and gladness: “Joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody” [3]. This line is clear throughout the book, being the book of salvation, which proclaims the rise of the Kingdom of inward joy and of unceasing singing and praise.

When St. John Cassian visited Egypt, he was amazed to find its deserts and villages, from Alexandria to Aswan, filled with monks, from whom nothing was heard but the sound of unceasing praise, so that he thought himself to be in heaven, asking: Are these earthly angels or heavenly men?!
This is the mark of the true Church: an inward joy that never ceases!

This joy is reflected in the whole life of the Church, and Madame Butcher observed that in the poor ancient churches of Egypt there was not one icon bearing the picture of a martyr being tortured or in pain, nor a picture of hell and its torments; rather, every icon radiates a spirit of joy and hope, so that even the martyrs you see rejoicing, looking toward heaven, gazing at the crown of their glory.

Joy is reflected in worship: on almost every day the Church celebrates a feast of the Lord, or a feast of one of the prophets, apostles, heavenly beings, martyrs, and so on... It is as though the Church creates an atmosphere of spiritual joy amid the troubles of this life, so that her children experience the consolations of the Holy Spirit and His heavenly joy; and the believer lives sharing with the heavenly beings their liturgies and their quiet, joyful exultations without interruption.

One of the prominent signs of joy in the Church is that the Holy Bible, especially the Gospels, is not read during the liturgies but chanted with a melody that fills the soul with consolation. Mr. Lieder, the well-known English writer, testified at the beginning of the nineteenth century, on his visit to Egypt, that the mere hearing of the Gospel during the Divine Liturgy in the Coptic Church has an effect on the soul.

entries.section: 1. A call to enjoy the work of redemption:

paragraphs.text: f. A call to preaching, for whoever enjoys the joy of salvation cannot remain silent in bearing witness to the life of the Gospel, but carries the law of the Lord and His Gospel as “a light of the people” [4], assuring all that life in Christ is neither far off nor impossible, for the righteousness of Christ is near to every heart [5], and His arms are stretched out in love on the Cross to the peoples, as the hope of all [5].
Preaching, or bearing witness to the saving work of Christ, belongs to the very core of every Christian's life and is not the work of the priest alone; therefore St. John Chrysostom says:
[Nothing is so worthless as a Christian who does not care about the salvation of others.
Do not say, I am poor, for the widow's two mites put you to shame. And Peter also said: “Silver and gold have I none,” and Paul was so poor that he often suffered hunger.
Do not plead your harsh circumstances, for they too were in harsh circumstances.
Do not plead your ignorance, for they were unlearned.
Perhaps you are a runaway slave; Onesimus was also this!
You may be sick; Timothy was so!
Everyone is able to help his brother, even if only by good will, if he has not the ability to do anything...
Do not say that you cannot influence others, for as long as you are a Christian it is impossible that you should not be influential... for this is the very essence of the Christian.
If you say that you are a Christian and cannot do anything for others, there is a contradiction in your saying this, like saying that the sun cannot give light.]

entries.section: 1. A call to enjoy the work of redemption:

paragraphs.text: g. A call to an eternal salvation that goes beyond heaven and earth: “Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath: for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished” [6].

The passing away of the heavens and the earth while salvation remains for ever signifies the crucifixion of the old man so as to enjoy the new man who is after the image of his Creator. The old heavens and the old earth must pass away in us that we may enjoy the new heavens and the new earth, whose inhabitants do not die like gnats, but in which the eternal righteousness of the Lord dwells.

If the heavens signify the soul and the earth the body, then the vanishing of the heavens and the wearing out of the earth mean the destruction of the works of the old man, for the soul as for the body, for the sanctification of our souls and our bodies, as we are the new creation renewed every day by the work of the Holy Spirit of God.

As for his saying “and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner” [6], it signifies the weakness of the works of the old man: they die like gnats! But the works of the new man are the righteousness of Christ which is not abolished, or the love which never fails.

entries.section: 1. A call to enjoy the work of redemption:

paragraphs.text: h. A serious and courageous call not to be troubled before the opposition of men: “Fear ye not the reproach of men, neither be ye afraid of their revilings. For the moth shall eat them up like a garment, and the worm shall eat them like wool: but my righteousness shall be for ever, and my salvation from generation to generation” [7-8].
Whoever lifts his gaze to the eternal Savior does not fear the actions of men and their opposition, for they come to nothing and end, while our salvation remains eternal.

The living spiritual man looks to his old man, whom he put off in the waters of Baptism like a garment that has worn out, and like a gnat that died in weakness; as for the reproaches of men and their revilings, they are like a garment eaten by the moth and like wool eaten by the worm! They are worn-out temporal things that will not last long; we bear them without being troubled, for in this we share with our Savior, who bore reproaches and insults gladly for our sake. Meet evil with love, bearing the weaknesses of the wicked.
* Do not put out fire with another fire, but with water.
* Nothing restrains evildoers from their evil like the injured person's meeting with gentleness the harm that befalls him.

entries.section: 1. A call to enjoy the work of redemption:

paragraphs.text: St. John Chrysostom i. A call to enjoy the risen life that overcomes death and crushes the murderous dragon. “Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD; awake, as in the ancient days, in the generations of old. Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab, and wounded the dragon?” [9].

The Church is the “arm of the LORD” who puts on the strength of His resurrection and awakes as from the sleep of death. Let the whole Church rise, whether those who came from a Jewish origin or a Gentile one; therefore He repeats the word “awake” twice.

God, the Giver of victory, formerly gave her strength and she overcame Egypt (the poetic name Rahab, as we saw earlier) when He rescued her from the hand of Pharaoh, who drowned in the waters of the Red Sea like a pierced dragon unable to live. It is the Lord Himself who gives His Church in the New Testament the power of His resurrection, not to overcome Pharaoh but the powers of darkness, and not to find a way for herself in the midst of the sea but to pass over into heaven itself.
* Now that death has been abolished (by the resurrection of the Lord Christ), and the kingdom of Satan has been demolished, all are filled with joy and happiness.

Pope Athanasius the Apostolic j. A call to enjoy God Himself as the Comforter: “I, even I, am he that comforteth you” (Isa 59:12), without seeking human consolations or fearing the troubling by men, for their life is but like grass (Isa 59:12).

entries.section: 1. A call to enjoy the work of redemption:

paragraphs.text: In our enjoyment of God's consolations we must not fear man, for he is transient, and his troubling is transient too; if we are disturbed by him we live in dread every day [14], though there is nothing to deserve it.

Despair came upon the captives and they thought that they would die in captivity, but God assured them: “The captive exile hasteneth that he may be loosed, and that he should not die in the pit (in captivity), nor that his bread should fail” [14]. It is fitting for them to wait for God's promise and never despair. If the kingdom of Babylon has drowned them like the sea, the Savior, the LORD of hosts, is able to trouble Babylon: “But I am the LORD thy God, that divided the sea, whose waves roared: The LORD of hosts is his name” (Isa 49:15).

entries.section: 2. The mystery of the fall of Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: 17 Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of the LORD the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out. 18 There is none to guide her among all the sons whom she hath brought forth; neither is there any that taketh her by the hand of all the sons that she hath brought up. 19 These two things are come unto thee; who shall be sorry for thee? desolation, and destruction, and the famine, and the sword: by whom shall I comfort thee? 20 Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the LORD, the rebuke of thy God.

After presenting this joyful call to enjoy the new life in the Lord, He wished to make plain the mystery of Jerusalem's captivity, so that she might realize her weaknesses and rise from her falls. Therefore He began by saying: “Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem” [17]. What He reveals of the weaknesses that struck her is not meant to expose her to shame, but is an uncovering of the wounds in order to treat them, and an explanation of the mystery of the fall so that she may rise and stand. Her weaknesses are summed up in her drinking “at the hand of the LORD the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling” [17].

It was the custom to give those condemned to death a cup of strong wine so that they would stagger before the sentence was carried out; so Jerusalem drank from the hand of the Lord the cup of His fury over her sins, that she might realize that she had fallen under punishment, not by her captivity to Babylon but by her captivity under the sentence of death, because her sins had taken her captive and made her lose her consciousness.

entries.section: 2. The mystery of the fall of Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: She drank of her own will from the cup of disobedience and staggered, and she found none among them to take her by the hand; she became like a mother whom her children despise without being ashamed. Those who sorrow over her state became “desolation, and destruction, and the famine, and the sword” [19].

21 Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine: 22 Thus saith thy Lord the LORD, and thy God that pleadeth the cause of his people, Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again: 23 But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee; which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over: and thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over.

With every uncovering of weakness or evil, the Lord opens the door of hope for salvation. Therefore, after He revealed to her the mystery of her fall, not in the Babylonian captivity but in the captivity of sin, and her drinking of the cup of God's wrath so as to stagger, He went on to assure her that He pardons her, handing the cup to her oppressors, who said to her soul: “Bow down, that we may go over: and thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over.” It was the custom for the conquerors to walk with their feet on the necks of the defeated. Therefore the conquerors commanded her to throw herself on the ground so that the enemy might walk on her back like a narrow street in which they pass. She lived in humiliation because she left God and disobeyed Him... Now He forgives her and sets her free!

“Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean. Shake thyself from the dust; arise, and sit down, O Jerusalem: loose thyself from the bands of thy neck, O captive daughter of Zion” [1-2].

While the prophet affirms the return of the people from captivity with a dignity they had not expected, he is in fact speaking of the return of mankind to its first place, its return to the spiritual city of God and its enjoyment of His surpassing splendor, to live free from all uncleanness as God willed for it...
God loves man and longs to bring him into glory, to live a holy, honored and glorious life; therefore the call comes here to enjoy the following divine blessings:

a. The risen, glorious life: “Awake, awake,” for she had gone down as though into the tomb, to lie in the midst of darkness and be overtaken by corruption. This is the state of Israel in Babylon, where they lost all hope of returning to their land and enjoying freedom, so they counted themselves as dead. This is the state of every man whom sin has captured, so that his inner life collapses and he loses the good will and the ability to enjoy the holy life, becoming like a dead man overtaken by corruption. He needs someone to awaken him from the death of sin and give him the new, risen life.

The Apostle says: “Wherefore he saith, Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light” (Eph 5:14). “And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus” (Eph 2:6).

Now the Savior has come to every fallen and humiliated soul to speak to her, saying: “Now when I passed by thee, and looked upon thee, behold, thy time was the time of love; and I spread my skirt over thee” (Ezek 16:8)... What does the spreading of His skirt over her mean but receiving her as a bride for Himself, united with Him and enjoying His risen life?! He came to her as a Bridegroom so that she might find in Him the “resurrection” and awake as from eternal death. This is what the Apostle Paul meant by saying: “For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ” (Rom 5:17).

Thus the soul is united with the Bridegroom, the Giver of life, and puts off the grave clothes and puts on the wedding garment: “Put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city” [1]. He says to her: “I clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with badgers' skin, and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk. I decked thee also with ornaments... and thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom. And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord GOD” (Ezek 16:10-14). What is this garment that poured out on her the splendor of the Lord, so that she became exceedingly beautiful and fit to be a queen, but the person of Christ Himself, in whom we are hidden, as the Apostle says: “have put on Christ” (Gal 3:27).

* It is fitting for the whole Church to exult, praising the Lord Christ, after the example of the holy women when they realized the resurrection of the Lord, who awakened mankind from sleep, giving it life and filling it with the light of faith.
St. Jerome * Today is the “feast of the Resurrection,” and it is for me a new beginning.

* The divine mystery has anointed me... which brings me to this great, radiant day, giving help to my weakness; so that He who rose from the dead on a day like this may give life to my soul also, and clothe me with the new man (Eph 4:23-24), and make me of the new creation, of those who were born of God... so that I may be ready to die with Him and rise also with Him...

Yesterday (Good Friday) the Lamb was slain and the doorposts were sprinkled with His blood... and the destroying angel passed by with his destroying sword, terrified and afraid... because we are kept safe by the precious Blood.
Yesterday I was crucified with Christ, and today I am glorified in Him!
Yesterday I died with Him, and today I am given life with Him!
Yesterday I was buried with Him, and today I rise with Him...!
Whoever was able to understand this great mystery in Christ and what He has done for us, and has not given himself to Christ, has given Him nothing!

St. Gregory of Nazianzus b. She becomes a holy city into which no uncircumcised or unclean shall come any more, that is, strangers shall no longer trample her. As the city of God she is sanctified from all uncleanness to bear the nature of the heavenly life that befits the heavenly King.
* Now, my beloved... Satan has been slain, that tyrant who is against the whole world, so we are not approaching a temporal feast but a perpetual, heavenly one...
Now death is abolished and the kingdom of Satan is destroyed; therefore everything is filled with joy and happiness...
We must approach the feast in this way, not in a defiled garment, but with our souls wrapped in clean garments. We must put on our Lord Jesus (Rom 13:4), so that we may celebrate the feast with Him.

Now we put Him on when we love virtue and hate evil; when we train ourselves in chastity and put our lusts to death; when we love righteousness and not iniquity; when we honor contentment and have a settled mind; when we do not forget the poor but open our doors to all men; when we help the weak and cast off pride.

Pope Athanasius the Apostolic c. She shakes herself from the dust, for the soul no longer clings to temporal things but seeks first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things are added to her. She lives set free toward eternity, released from the bonds of the world.

d. She arises as a queen to sit on the throne of the kingdom [2], after having been a maidservant and a captive slave sitting in the dust, serving her masters in humiliation and shame; she rises to the right hand of the heavenly King. As the Psalmist says: “Upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir” (Ps 45:9).

e. Enjoying freedom: “Loose thyself from the bands of thy neck, O captive daughter of Zion” [2]. After having been bound by the neck to be dragged like one of the animals in captivity, these bands are loosed and the dignity of freedom returns to her, so that she lives as mistress of herself, with an inward authority. If sin humiliates man and drags him as it wishes, toying with him like a plaything in the hands of the evil enemy, then in Christ Jesus man lives as a king (Rev 1:6), holding authority over his heart, his thought, his feelings and his body.

In short, man rises from the death of sin, puts off his grave clothes and puts on the Lord Christ Himself as an everlasting garment; he refuses all uncleanness to bear within himself the righteousness of Christ; he shakes himself from the dust of the love of earthly things so that his soul may soar in the heavenly places; he rises from humiliation to sit at the right hand of God and enjoy fellowship in glory. His inner chains are loosed that he may enjoy the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

3 For thus saith the LORD, Ye have sold yourselves for nought; and ye shall be redeemed without money. 4 For thus saith the Lord GOD, My people went down aforetime into Egypt to sojourn there; and the Assyrian oppressed them without cause. 5 Now therefore, what have I here, saith the LORD, that my people is taken away for nought? they that rule over them make them to howl, saith the LORD; and my name continually every day is blasphemed. 6 Therefore my people shall know my name: therefore they shall know in that day that I am he that doth speak: behold, it is I.

“For thus saith the LORD, Ye have sold yourselves for nought; and ye shall be redeemed without money” [3]. God did not sell His people to Babylon; rather, they sold themselves by forsaking God and disobeying Him, so He delivered them over to them. They received nothing in return, and God received nothing, because Babylon did not thank God who delivered this people to them as captives, but blasphemed Him. It is as though God did not wish to deliver them to Babylon, but they compelled Him by selling themselves to sin and to the abominations of idolatry.

God's people had earlier gone down to Egypt and sojourned there, and Pharaoh humiliated them; yet they did not learn, and sold themselves to Assyria, which oppressed them without cause, or without any provocation on the people's part against Assyria... Therefore God intervenes to save His people and to glorify His holy name.

We too delivered ourselves to the authority of sin and enslaved ourselves to the evil enemy for nothing... Now the Savior has come forward to free us without cost, not with gold or silver but with His precious Blood (Rev 5:9).

7 How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth! 8 Thy watchmen shall lift up the voice; with the voice together shall they sing: for they shall see eye to eye, when the LORD shall bring again Zion. 9 Break forth into joy, sing together, ye waste places of Jerusalem: for the LORD hath comforted his people, he hath redeemed Jerusalem. 10 The LORD hath made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.

The good tidings of the people's return from captivity came from the Lord Himself, who reigned over His people [7], and voices of praise and singing rose up, not because of their return to their land but because of “the LORD's return to Zion” [8]. He came Himself to comfort His people, and made bare His holy arm to work to repair the ruin that had befallen His people and His city, to proclaim openly “in the eyes of all the nations” [10], that all the ends of the earth might glorify Him.
The speech here is chiefly about the joyful good tidings of the Gospel of salvation:

“How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth” [7]. What are these two beautiful feet but the Church of the New Testament, which speaks through the word of God (the mountains) to preach the Gospel and to proclaim that our Lord Jesus reigned from the wood and that He raised us up with Him?!

* He (Isaiah) sees how beautiful and fitting is the preaching of the Apostles who walk in (the Lord) who said “I am the way,” praising the feet of those who walk in the rational way of Jesus Christ, for through this door they enter to God (the Father). They bring good tidings, these whose feet are beautiful because Jesus has become for them (a way for their feet and the secret of their beauty).

Origen * When they preach to us the Gospel of this peace, of which he had prophesied: “How beautiful are the feet of them that publish peace, that bring good tidings of good” [7], each one of us begins to be a son of peace by his obedience and his faith in this Gospel, for he is justified by faith and receives peace with God.
* What are the feet of the Lord? They are the holy Evangelists!
* Through the beautiful feet of men who announce good things, the hearts of mankind have become an open way for the Lord.
St. Augustine

11 Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the LORD. 12 For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight: for the LORD will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your rereward.

In the spirit of prophecy Isaiah saw the priests bearing the vessels of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken and which Belshazzar had used at the feast with contempt (Ezra 1:7-11), in a majestic procession that lasted about four months.
The prophet disclosed the secret of the majesty of this procession, namely:

a. On the negative side: departing from evil and continually going out from the captivity of sin: “Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the LORD” [11]. It is a call to a continual going out, as the Apostle says: “Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you, and will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters” (2 Cor 6:17-18).

* Paul counsels, saying: “Put away from among yourselves that wicked person,” “that he that hath done this deed might be taken away from among you” (1 Cor 5:13, 2). It is a terrible thing, truly terrible, the assembly of the wicked, for their plague spreads quickly and affects those who deal with them as though they were sick... “Evil communications corrupt good manners” (1 Cor 15:33)... May no one have a wicked friend.

St. John Chrysostom b. On the positive side: accepting God Himself as the leader of the procession; therefore we go out in calm and assurance, confident of the power of our Leader and of His protection of us all the way: “For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight: for the LORD will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your rereward” [12].

entries.section: 5. The glory of the servant of the Lord:

paragraphs.text: 13 Behold, my servant shall deal prudently, he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high. 14 As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men: 15 So shall he sprinkle many nations; the kings shall shut their mouths at him: for that which had not been told them shall they see; and that which they had not heard shall they consider.

Since He commanded that the Lord, the Savior, lead the procession, He presented to us a picture of the glory of the Savior, who became a servant in order to be glorified on our behalf and in our name; and the ancient Jews interpreted this text as referring to the Messiah.
a. “Behold, my servant”: the Word became flesh and was counted a servant of the Father as a representative of mankind, the Servant who obeys, so that in Him we are counted obedient to God.

b. “He shall deal prudently, he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high” [13]: He is the wisdom of God; for our sake He received the Spirit of wisdom and understanding resting upon Him (Isa 11:2), although the Holy Spirit is His own Spirit, inseparable from Him.

entries.section: 5. The glory of the servant of the Lord:

paragraphs.text: c. His appearance on the Cross astonished those in heaven and on earth: “As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men” [14]. This is what he will declare more clearly in the next chapter: “He hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him...” (Isa 53:2-3).

d. Through this painful sight, as a sacrifice lifted up on the Cross, He sprinkled the Gentiles with His blood and so sanctified them to Himself, and shut the mouths of kings (perhaps meaning the powers of darkness), since they saw a salvation they had not understood before.

entries.section: 1. The Cross is a transcendent mystery:

paragraphs.text: 1 Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed?
The prophet opens his discourse on the Cross, saying: “Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed?” [1].

If the contemporaries of the prophet Isaiah were unable to accept the prophecies concerning the appearing of Cyrus to bring the people back from the Babylonian captivity, how could they believe the matter of the Cross?! Truly it is a wondrous mystery before which the heavenly and the earthly stand in amazement, as they see the arm of the Lord revealed through the Incarnation, so that the Lord might stretch out His hands on the Cross to embrace the Gentiles, granting them the power of His resurrection and its joy through their fellowship in His sufferings and His crucifixion.
* That God, the Son of God, the arm of the Lord, should endure such sufferings!

St. Cyril of Jerusalem The subject of the revealing of the arm of the Lord, or the incarnation of the Word of God, remains a subject of amazement for the heavenly and earthly creation: how does the Word become flesh?!
* With what words shall we bless God, and what thanks can we offer Him...?!
He loved us so much that, though He is the Eternal One, older than the whole world itself, He became in age younger than many of His servants in the world!
