Perhaps by hiding here he meant that He cannot bear to see His children under pain and distress, so He is like one who strikes and hides for a moment, in order to draw His children to Himself through hardship. Therefore He affirms that even if He seems to have hidden, His eyes are on the ways of those being chastened by Him, so that He may heal them and lead them Himself and compensate their mourning with divine comforts. What a surpassing, fatherly divine love!
* If you suffer evil and bear it with gentleness, all evils will be removed from you.

* Such is the compassionate love of God. He will not turn His face away from sincere repentance, for even if a man has rushed into evil to the very end, when he chooses to return to the virtuous life God receives him and welcomes him and does all that is for his restoration, and brings him back to his first state.

entries.section: 3. The blessings of returning to God:

paragraphs.text: St. John Chrysostom e. He pours out upon them double peace while the wicked are filled with turmoil, as He says: "I create the fruit of the lips; Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith the LORD; and I will heal him. But the wicked are like the troubled sea, when it cannot rest, whose waters cast up mire and dirt. There is no peace (joy), saith my God, to the wicked" [19-21].

He calls those who are far off (unbelievers) and those who are near (fallen believers) to come to Him in repentance and receive double peace. As St. Augustine says: [The Lord promised true consolation in the words of Isaiah: "I will give him true comfort, peace upon peace" [17] (LXX). Without this consolation men find themselves amid earthly gladness that is dissolution more than rest]. And also: [What the wicked man calls joy is not joy].

1 "Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins. 2 Yet they seek me daily, and delight to know my ways, as a nation that did righteousness, and forsook not the ordinance of their God: they ask of me the ordinances of justice; they take delight in approaching to God.

If clinging to idolaters stirred up the spirit of corruption and rebellion in the life of the people, so that they set up the worship of idols under every green tree, in every valley, and on the mountains and hills in the open, committed adultery, practiced abominations, and offered their children as human sacrifices, yet what is more serious is that they mixed this great evil with the worship of the living God in order to satisfy their consciences. This is the most serious enemy facing the religious and causing men to stumble in the knowledge of God: hypocrisy, or covering evil and corruption with the outward forms of worship without sincere repentance.

Now God asks the prophet to speak openly and with a loud voice like a trumpet, exposing their weaknesses and declaring their transgressions and sins, that is, uncovering their wounds so that their consciences may not be quieted by a worship full of hypocrisy. He is like the physician who uncovers hidden wounds or diseases in order to treat them in their depths.
The Lord says: "Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins" [1].

In the New Testament our Lord Jesus sent us His Holy Spirit, who "will reprove the world of sin" (Jn 16:8), that is, He reveals to the soul in its depths its hidden wounds and stirs it to repentance, instead of concealing the wounds so that they corrupt the body and destroy it.

The exposing or revealing of sin does not mean God's rejection of His people or His abandoning them, but on the contrary a sign of love for them. Therefore He says: "shew my people... the house of Jacob" [1], without any flattery on your part toward them, but cry aloud and do not stop.

When He spoke of idolatry, adultery, or making their children pass through the fire as human sacrifices, God did not ask the prophet to cry out loudly as with a trumpet, because these are plain sins; but when He speaks of hypocrisy He asks this, because it is a hidden sin that creeps into the souls of the worshipers and is hard for a man to discover. Therefore, when the Lord rebuked adulterers or tax collectors, He often spoke with them individually without wounding their feelings; but with the hypocritical leaders His words were firm and His discourses public.
The people covered themselves with outward appearances such as:
a. Visible and continual prayer: "Yet they seek me daily" [2].

b. Delight in rational spiritual knowledge: "and delight to know my ways, as a nation that did righteousness, and forsook not the ordinance of their God" [2]; that is, they persist in studying the Scripture and attending meetings as a people's custom, or as Herod delighted in hearing John the Baptist.
c. They show zeal for the practice of justice and godliness [2].
d. "They take delight in approaching to God" [2], that is, pretending to be near to God, worshiping Him and knowing His ordinances and judgment.

3 "Wherefore have we fasted, say they, and thou seest not? wherefore have we afflicted our soul, and thou takest no knowledge? Behold, in the day of your fast ye find pleasure, and exact all your labours. 4 Behold, ye fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: ye shall not fast as ye do this day, to make your voice to be heard on high. 5 Is it such a fast that I have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the LORD?"
"Wherefore have we fasted, say they, and thou seest not? wherefore have we afflicted our soul, and thou takest no knowledge?" [3]. He answers this as follows:

a. "Behold, in the day of your fast ye find pleasure, and exact all your labours" [3]. The Pharisee thought that God was pleased with him because he fasted twice in the week (Lk 18:12), and these also practice fasting but do everything that pleases themselves, not what pleases God. The sign of this is that, contrary to the Law, they give those who work for them no opportunity to rest and share in their fasts and worship, but drive them for the sake of greed and the love of acquisition and wealth.

God does not want our fasting from food alone, but that the soul fast along with it from the love of the world and from greed, which appears clearly in our dealings with others. In other words, it is fitting for us to control our souls along with controlling our bellies.
Perhaps by "pleasure" he meant here not only material gain but the satisfaction of bodily pleasures instead of chastity.

b. "Behold, ye fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: ye shall not fast as ye do this day, to make your voice to be heard on high" [4]. Instead of a man judging himself and blaming himself on the day of his fast, he enters into strife with others and condemns them; therefore God does not accept his fast nor hear his voice on high. This is what happened when Ahab king of Israel and Jezebel wanted to rob us of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite, for Jezebel planned to kill him unjustly and asked the elders and nobles to proclaim a fast (1 Kgs 21:9, 12).

At the very time when they practice fasting, a man clenches his hand to strike his brother unjustly, instead of offering works of love. Therefore Abba Yusab al-Abah says: [Do not fast with bread and salt while you eat the flesh of men by condemnation and slander. Do not say, I am fasting a "clean" fast, while you are soiled with every offense].

c. "Is it such a fast that I have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the LORD?" [5].

It is good for a man to join fasting with self-humbling and asceticism, but if he stops at the outward appearance he loses its essence. It was fitting for the one who fasts to humble himself, repenting of his sins and feeling his weaknesses, and to practice humility in his heart side by side with his self-humbling, not to bear the Pharisaic image, as the Lord says: "Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward" (Mt 6:16).

6 "Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke? 7 Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?"

a. Offering works of love instead of seeking self-pleasure [3] and driving others for our own benefit. Fasting is the giving up of the "I" and its crucifixion, so that Christ, who is "Love", may live in us, and we bear the marks of His love and practice His work as members of His body. This is fasting in its positive meaning. "Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke? Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?" [6-7].

How beautiful is the saying "hide not thyself from thine own flesh", as though the one who fasts, being crucified with Christ, realizes that the flesh of others is his own flesh. When he loosens the bands he is loosening the bands of his own soul, counting himself bound with those who are bound (Heb 13:3), imprisoned with every prisoner, hungry and poor and wandering and naked with those who suffer these things. By fasting he loves others as himself, since they are members one of another, or members working together in one body under the one Head, our Lord Jesus.

* Fasting is not counted good by its own nature, but becomes good and pleasing to the Lord through the other works. Again, fasting -according to the surrounding circumstances- can be regarded as not only vain but truly hateful, as the Lord says: "When you fast, I do not hear your prayers."

Abba Theonas * He taught them to break their bread to the hungry, and to take in the poor who have no shelter, and to clothe the naked, and not to ignore those who are of their own blood. And now they in particular receive more benefit from our need (through their giving) than their benefit from our goods.
St. Gregory of Nazianzus * You have heard from Isaiah: "Break your bread to the hungry" (Isa 57:5); so do not think that fasting is sufficient in itself.

Fasting controls yourself but does not refresh others. Your distress for yourself profits you if there is comfort in it for others. Behold, you deny yourself; look to whom you have given what you have deprived yourself of...! How many poor have been filled by the breakfast you deprived yourself of?!
St. Augustine

8 "Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thine health shall spring forth speedily: and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the LORD shall be thy rereward. 9 Then shalt thou call, and the LORD shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity; 10 And if thou draw out thy soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul; then shall thy light rise in obscurity, and thy darkness be as the noonday: 11 And the LORD shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not. 12 And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in."

a. Enjoying the divine light: "Then shall thy light break forth as the morning" [8]. When a man practices fasting in its positive form, he enjoys union with the Father through His only-begotten Son by His Holy Spirit, and God, "the true Light", shines in him as his own light. "Then shall thy light rise in obscurity, and thy darkness be as the noonday" [10].

A wonderful picture of fasting joined to giving and self-sacrifice for the sake of others through our union with God, the Lover of mankind. If the poor and suffering feel in the midst of their bitterness as though they were in darkness, then the work of love that flows from an enlarged heart is like the rising of the sun that scatters the darkness. This light does not spring from the outward appearance of giving, but from the transfiguration of the Lord of glory in the loving heart. As the Lord of glory says: "Ye are the light of the world... Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven" (Mt 5:14, 16).

The fast joined to love that flows from the heart, where the Kingdom of Christ is established, and translated into practical conduct, is united with the fast of the Lord Christ, and so is sanctified and accepted before the Father.

b. Enjoying the health of spirit, soul and body: "and thine health shall spring forth speedily" [8]; "and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not" [8, 11]. What are the bones that are made fat if not the health of the soul, which enjoys the bones of faith that support the whole life of man?!

Holy fasting also helps the body, and it has been proven scientifically that fasting with a period of abstinence and refraining from fatty foods is beneficial for health; as it is beneficial for the soul, which by fasting submits in humility to God, that He may establish it and make it grow in faith, so that He may make of it His paradise, whose rivers and springs never dry up.

c. Enjoying God as the leader of the soul and the source of its inner glory and righteousness: "and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the LORD shall be thy rereward" [8]; "the LORD shall guide thee continually" [11].

d. The answering of prayer: "Then shalt thou call, and the LORD shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am" [9]. So long as in our fasts we look not at the outward form but at the opening of the heart to God through the holiness of life and its enlargement with love toward men, God rejoices in such a fast, declaring this through His answering of prayer.
* Do you want to raise your prayer to God? Let giving and fasting be its two wings!

St. Augustine * God hears me quickly because I do not seek earthly happiness, but have learned holy endurance from the New Testament; so I do not seek the earth or its goods, nor temporal health, nor victory over enemies, nor riches, nor temporal positions...

St. Augustine e. A state of inner satisfaction: "and satisfy thy soul in drought (the wilderness)" [11]. In ourselves we are wildernesses and droughts, but when by love we satisfy the hungry, God satisfies us from His own, despite the complete inability of our resources.

f. The building of others: "And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in" [12]. When our hands are stretched out to work with God in small matters, such as material giving or comforting the sorrowful, etc..., He grants us what is greater, that we become a cause of building the inner life of others as a holy dwelling for the Lord.

13 "If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: 14 Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it."
After presenting a living picture of the accepted fast, He disclosed to us the keeping of the Sabbath in its true spiritual meaning as a spiritual rest in the Lord, requiring of us the following:

a. "If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day" [13]. If the Sabbath is the holy day of the Lord, it is fitting on it to cease from satisfying bodily pleasures or delights, so that we may practice the holy life.

b. Enjoying delight and joy in the Lord honors the Lord of the Sabbath and glorifies Him [13]... as though the Sabbath were not a deprivation but an inner satisfaction and joy, through which the Lord carries us as on the high places of the earth to soar in the heavenly things, and feeds us from the manna of the eternal inheritance [14].

entries.section: 1. The sins that hide the Lord's face:

paragraphs.text: 1 "Behold, the LORD's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: 2 But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear. 3 For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken lies, your tongue hath muttered perverseness. 4 None calleth for justice, nor any pleadeth for truth: they trust in vanity, and speak lies; they conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity. 5 They hatch cockatrice' eggs, and weave the spider's web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper. 6 Their webs shall not become garments, neither shall they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands. 7 Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; wasting and destruction are in their paths. 8 The way of peace they know not; and there is no judgment in their goings: they have made them crooked paths: whosoever goeth therein shall not know peace."

"Behold, the LORD's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear" [1-2].

As for the Lord, He is Almighty, His hand is not shortened that it cannot save, and He is the loving Father whose ear is not heavy to hear the voice of His children. The fault lies wholly in man, whose iniquities -his disobedience to the Lord- have become a veil separating God and man; they have corrupted the eyes of man so that he no longer sees the face of God, and corrupted his voice so that it is no longer fit for the Lord to hear. God wants to save and is able to, but He does not compel us by force, so our transgressions and evils stand as an obstacle to enjoying Him and His salvation.
* Since this is the cause that keeps us far from God, let us remove this hateful barrier that deprives us of drawing near to Him.
St. John Chrysostom * Every sin is serious because it grieves God.

Fr. Theophan the Recluse What do the iniquities and sins that separate us from God and hide His face from us mean? They are a rejection of the law of God and a desire for man to go outside the circle of His Kingdom, as the Apostle says: "sin is the transgression" (1 Jn 3:5). It is a rejection of God Himself, of His Kingdom, His law, and the image in which we were created... This is what grieves the heart of God.

In other words, our sins and iniquities are not merely certain actions, but an indicator of the inner state of the soul and its position toward God... when it thinks that clinging to Him is a kind of bondage and deprivation, so it wants to be rid of Him and freed from His commandments, expressing this by one means or another. Therefore Holy Scripture sometimes portrays sin to us as a being that opposes God, as the Apostle says: "sin entered into the world" (Rom 5:12).

The work of sin -the constitution of the kingdom of the devil- is to tear humanity away from the Kingdom of God and deprive them of meeting their Father and enjoying the reflection of His image upon them and fellowship in the divine nature; but the work of the righteousness of Christ is to draw the deceived souls into the Kingdom of God so that they may conceal their goodness and take on the likeness of the Son of God and share His attributes and glory.
Sin is the "state of the soul" and its position, but it is translated into inner actions in the heart, thought and feelings, as well as outward actions in words and deeds.
St. Cyprian says:

[The truth of the matter has been presented through the mouth of the prophet by a divine Spirit... that God is able to prevent opposing things, but the wicked deserts of sinners hinder the giving of His help...

Let your sins and transgressions be counted, let the wounds of your consciences be taken into account, let each one of you cease to murmur against God and against us, if he counts himself deserving of what he suffers].
The prophet here enumerates a group of sins that the people had already committed, and into which many men still fall:

entries.section: 1. The sins that hide the Lord's face:

paragraphs.text: a. Murder or violence: "For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity" [3]. If "God is love", whose law is tenderness, compassion and mercy, then the law of sin is hatred, violence and unjust killing. Therefore, when the Lord wanted to uproot the kingdom of sin from its roots, He said: "Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill... But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire" (Mt 5:21-22).

b. Lying: "your lips have spoken lies, your tongue hath muttered perverseness" [3]. Since they rejected God and belonged to the kingdom of the devil, they bore its marks, which are violence together with lying and deception, for the enemy of good was called "a liar, and the father of it" (Jn 8:44), "the deceiver". If the Lord Christ is "the Truth", then the enemy of good is "the liar" and "falsehood".
Lying is the law of the kingdom of the devil, therefore Holy Scripture warns us against it:
"Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight" (Prov 12:22).
"no lie is of the truth" (1 Jn 2:21).
"The mouth that lies kills the soul" (Wis 1:11).
* Every proud man is deceitful, and every deceitful man is a liar. Men suffer from speaking deceit, though they could speak the truth with perfect ease.

St. Augustine c. Partiality: "None calleth for justice, nor any pleadeth for truth" [3]. They practice the law of their king, namely injustice and respect of persons. The fruit of their unjust works is the destruction of others without profit to themselves. They are like a woman who conceives not a human child that gladdens her heart at its birth, but suffers bitterly the pains of pregnancy and labor, conceiving great toil in order to bring forth iniquity that destroys her and those around her. "They conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity" [4], and as the Psalmist says: "Behold, he travaileth with iniquity, and hath conceived mischief, and brought forth falsehood" (Ps 7:14).

entries.section: 1. The sins that hide the Lord's face:

paragraphs.text: The second simile is that they became like a viper that offers eggs, but they hatch what kills, not what satisfies and sustains [5].
The third simile is that they are like the spider, which weaves threads that do not cover but catch insects [5-6].

In the three preceding similes there is a common element, "deception": in the first, the woman appears pregnant and is expected to bear a child, but she gives birth to iniquity; in the second, the eggs appear for a man to eat and be satisfied, but a deadly viper hatches; in the third, a man sees a fine, wonderful web, but it is the spider's work, not covering nakedness but catching insects in order to kill them. These are the similes he presents of those who rule unjustly under the name of justice.

entries.section: 1. The sins that hide the Lord's face:

paragraphs.text: d. What is more serious is that the iniquities they commit, whether mentioned here or not, they do not fall into involuntarily out of weakness, but run to them of themselves and hasten to commit them like one who delights in them [7].

9 "Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us: we wait for light, but behold obscurity; for brightness, but we walk in darkness. 10 We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noon day as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men. 11 We roar all like bears, and mourn sore like doves: we look for judgment, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far off from us. 12 For our transgressions are multiplied before thee, and our sins testify against us: for our transgressions are with us; and as for our iniquities, we know them; 13 In transgressing and lying against the LORD, and departing away from our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood. 14 And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. 15 Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey: and the LORD saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment."
a. Deprivation of drawing near to God, the "Truth": "Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us" [5].
Accepting sin is accepting falsehood and rejecting the truth, that is, entering the kingdom of the devil and transgressing against the Kingdom of God.
* O my wretchedness... Many follies have assailed me, and although You are the Truth, I did not seek counsel from You.
* When I was separated from You, O my God, I no longer existed, I became as nothing....
St. Augustine b. "Immersion in darkness: " We wait for light, but behold obscurity; for brightness, but we walk in darkness" [9].
* O my wretchedness... Darkness has trodden upon me, and although You are the Light, I hid my face from You!.

* You are the Light for the children of light! Your day knows no sunset! Your day shines for Your children so that they may not stumble! But those who are outside You walk in darkness and live in it...?
Everyone who departs from You, O true Light, goes deeper into the darkness of sin, and when darkness surrounds him he cannot discern the snares set for him all along the way!.

St. Augustine c. Loss of insight, without conscious spiritual guidance: "We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noon day as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men" [10]. The Lord Christ has shone, the Sun of Righteousness, and we have become as those in the noonday, but because of loss of insight some stumbled as those who are in darkness; He veiled His divinity as in the mist of the flesh, and in unbelief the unbelievers fell like the dead.

d. Crying out without profit; the great pray with a loud voice and roar, and the small moan like doves, yet there is no salvation for them [11]; for no other reason than their clinging to continual and increasing disobedience, which has become the companion of man, committed with knowledge [12].

In other words, they do not cease to pray, but without benefit, because their prayer does not flow from a heart sincere in its longing for God, in its faith in the work of God in its life, and in its spiritual conduct. Although God in His love longs to answer the prayers and requests of man before man expresses them with his tongue, man by his evil and unbelief loses the enjoyment of this divine gift.
* He is fully assured that his prayer will not be answered! Who is this wretched man? The one who prays and does not believe that he will receive an answer.
St. John Cassian e. Deviation, or turning aside from God, by our clinging to lying and the loss of the spirit of truthfulness and uprightness [14-15].

entries.section: 3. The need for God the Savior:

paragraphs.text: 16 "And he saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor: therefore his arm brought salvation unto him; and his righteousness, it sustained him. 17 For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke. 18 According to their deeds, accordingly he will repay, fury to his adversaries, recompence to his enemies; to the islands he will repay recompence. 19 So shall they fear the name of the LORD from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun. When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD shall lift up a standard against him. 20 And the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith the LORD. 21 As for me, this is my covenant with them, saith the LORD; My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the LORD, from henceforth and for ever."

The matter became very bad, but God, the Creator of man, who cares for him and loves him, does not stand by as a spectator. "And the LORD saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment. And he saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor: therefore his arm brought salvation unto him; and his righteousness, it sustained him" [15-16].

* Because of this separation the Intercessor was sent to take away the sin of the world by which we were separated from Him as enemies, in order that we might be reconciled with Him and be changed from enemies into sons.

St. Augustine Since there is no intercessor able to reconcile us with God, the Lord Himself came down, and as St. Gregory the Theologian says: [You entrusted our salvation neither to an angel nor to an archangel nor to a prophet, but You alone became incarnate and became man and were made like us in everything except sin alone...].
What did the propitiatory Intercessor do for us?

entries.section: 3. The need for God the Savior:

paragraphs.text: a. He went forward into the battle as our leader and as a representative of humanity, giving it victory and triumph by His righteousness and authority: "For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke. According to their deeds, accordingly he will repay..." [17-18]. Instead of the sin to which we were bound and which crushed us, He put on His divine righteousness as a breastplate for us; instead of the destruction that came upon us, He put on salvation as a helmet upon His head; and instead of the weakness or collapse into which we fell, He arose to take vengeance on the devil and all his angels, repaying them their evil, so that they lose their authority over the nations in the west or the east. The Savior is glorified among the peoples and nations as He grants them victory even over the enemy who comes in like a rushing flood, but the Lord, as with the breath of His Holy Spirit, stops his overflowing [19].

entries.section: 3. The need for God the Savior:

paragraphs.text: b. He established His Church, the new Zion, as a center of repentance [20]; He established it as a hospital for the sick and not a court for judgment and condemnation, as He says: "And the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith the LORD" [20].
* Gentleness (toward the weak and sinners) is the only virtue that works for the growth of the Church, which the Lord demands as the price of His blood.
Gentleness is an imitation of the tenderness of heaven toward men, aiming at the salvation of all.

* Let us not laugh at anyone's sin but grieve, for it is written: "Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me..." (Mic 7:8-9). He did not say this in vain, for whoever gloats over the fallen rejoices in the victory of Satan. Therefore we ought rather to grieve when we hear of the destruction of a person for whom Christ died.

entries.section: 3. The need for God the Savior:

paragraphs.text: The martyr Cyprian c. The establishing of a new covenant with mankind [21], with an assurance of the fulfillment of the divine promises.

1 "Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee. 2 For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the LORD shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.

The Lord had already affirmed that He Himself accomplishes the salvation and redeems Zion, establishing His new covenant with her (Isa 59:15-21). Now that the Lord Christ has offered His salvation on the Cross, and the Father has declared His acceptance through the Resurrection -which is not a gift external to the Lord Christ, since He Himself is the Resurrection (Jn 11:25), and He has power to lay down His life and power to take it again (Jn 10:18)- He asks the Church of the New Testament to enjoy the life of her Redeemer as a risen life in which there is no place for darkness.

"Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee. For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the LORD shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee" [2].

When the Jews returned from captivity they counted themselves as those who had risen from the dead, and they enjoyed the light of life and freedom after seventy years of humiliation as in the darkness of the tomb. But the Church of the New Testament has enjoyed something greater: her union with the true Light as an eternal Bridegroom, who makes of her a bride bearing His light, His splendor and His glory. As the Lord said of Himself, "I am the light of the world" (Jn 8:12), He called His disciples the light of the world (Mt 5:14), since they bear Him within them.
What is the secret of the Church's illumination?

The Lord's Resurrection, which gave us the new life that death will not overcome, that darkness cannot seize, and that the tomb cannot destroy. Therefore the Apostle says: "Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light" (Eph 5:14).
Since Baptism is the enjoyment of Christ's Resurrection in us, this sacrament was called "illumination".
* When we are baptized we are enlightened, when we are enlightened we are adopted as sons, when we are adopted we are made perfect...
This act is called by many names, I mean grace, illumination, perfection, washing... It is illumination because by it we see the holy light of salvation, I mean that by it we gaze upon God clearly.
St. Clement of Alexandria * Illumination, which is Baptism... is the helper of the weak... a sharing in light... a shaking off of darkness.
Illumination is a vessel sailing toward God; a keeping company with Christ, the foundation of religion, the perfection of the mind!
Illumination is the key of the Kingdom and the restoration of life.
St. Gregory of Nazianzus * Baptism is the daughter of the day; it opened its doors and the night, into which all creation had entered, fled!

Mar Jacob of Serugh Thus, when we accept union with our Lord Jesus Christ the Crucified, we are buried with Him in Baptism and rise bearing the possibility of new life, to live as is fitting, as children of light and members of the body of the holy Christ. It is not fitting for us to descend again into the darkness of sin, nor to excuse ourselves by our human weakness, for we bear within us the light of the Lord and His glory shines upon us. We no longer become a dark earth but a heaven that embraces the glory and splendor of God.

This is the mark of the Church as a new life in Christ, who dwells in her and shines upon her with His divine righteousness, so that it is said of us: "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven" (Mt 5:16).

* When they practice divine things and speak of them, and live the divine life, overcoming hardness of heart and enjoying the peace of righteousness, a great glory pursues them in the Church of Christ.

St. Augustine Since the Lord Christ came into the world to win humanity as a bride for Himself, He pours His glory and splendor within her; He gives her His Holy Spirit to adorn her and beautify her, so that she may be prepared with inner glory for the eternal heavenly wedding. So it is said to her: "Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father's house; so shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he is thy Lord; and worship thou him... The king's daughter is all glorious within" (Ps 45:10-13).

3 "And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising. 4 Lift up thine eyes round about, and see: all they gather themselves together, they come to thee: thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall be nursed at thy side. 5 Then thou shalt see, and flow together, and thine heart shall fear, and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee. 6 The multitude of camels shall cover thee, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall shew forth the praises of the LORD. 7 All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered together unto thee, the rams of Nebaioth shall minister unto thee: they shall come up with acceptance on mine altar, and I will glorify the house of my glory. 8 Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows? 9 Surely the isles shall wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring thy sons from far, their silver and their gold with them, unto the name of the LORD thy God, and to the Holy One of Israel, because he hath glorified thee.

The inner glory of God in the soul is attractive; it wins souls for His spiritual kingdom. For the Church of the New Testament becomes an illuminated city that attracts the Gentiles, as the Lord Himself says: "Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid. Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven" (Mt 5:14-16). This is the fulfillment of what is written in the prophet Isaiah: "And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising" [3].
The Church, like her Bridegroom, becomes a pillar of the light of truth that leads the Gentiles in the way of the Lord and sets up among them spiritual kings who have inner authority.

The Church looks around her to see on every side the wonderful work of God, who draws from all nations sons and daughters for her, coming from far to become the honored household of the Lord, carried in arms [14].

The power of Christ risen from the dead appears in the life of His Church by converting powers (the wealth of the Gentiles) for the sake of His Kingdom, for it is said to His bride: "Then thou shalt see, and flow together, and thine heart shall fear, and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee" [5]...
What is the wealth or riches of the Gentiles that are sanctified for the sake of the Church of Christ?

a. The abundance of the sea [5], that is, fish and pearls. The Fathers of the early Church counted the Lord Christ as "the Fish" (Ichthys, ἰχθύς), and the believers as the fish that live with the Lord Christ and in Him (Ezek 47:9). Tertullian says: [We little fish, after the example of our Fish, Jesus Christ, are born in water, and we are not safe in any other way than by remaining in the water continually].

b. Gold and incense carried by camels from Midian and Sheba, not for trade but offered as a gift to Zion. As the Magi offered gold, frankincense and myrrh to the Lord Christ as a sign of His kingship, that He is God to whom incense is offered, and that He suffers; so the members of His body become kings who offer incense as a sweet fragrance to the Savior.

c. The offering of acceptable sacrifices for the service of the house of the Lord and its adornment [7-8]; these sacrifices are our lives, our bodies and all our powers, which are united with the unique Sacrifice, and so become burnt offerings of love lifted up through the Cross. The Apostle says: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service" (Rom 12:1). Our offerings to the Lord are our very "souls", as St. Jerome says.

d. Perhaps the most beautiful thing we offer to Zion is our enjoyment of the ability to fly like a cloud, carried by the Spirit of the Lord toward the heavenly things, so that we live with our Christ in His glories as in our own home. "Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?!" [8].

The Lord will come on the last day in the clouds (Mt 24:30); He comes carried upon His saints, the light and luminous cloud (Isa 19:1)... Our likeness to a cloud means that we have become a throne bearing our Christ; and our likeness to doves means that we have become spiritual, because the Holy Spirit appeared at the Lord's baptism as a dove. In other words, our attachment to the Church of God makes us a throne for the Lord, bearing the fruits of His Holy Spirit.

In the Septuagint it says: "Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as doves with their young?" St. Gregory of Nyssa sees that this prophetic phrase announces from afar the Church coming with her children, full of beauty and very many.

St. Gregory of Nyssa compares the true children of the Church, who in lightness of spirit fly like doves and clouds, with the wicked, who because of the weight of sin sink as in deep waters. [One walks lightly enough while the other sinks in deep waters. For virtue is light and floats, and all who live in its way fly like a cloud and like doves with their young, as Isaiah says; but sin is heavy; and as another prophet says, it sits upon a talent of lead (Zech 5:7)].

e. Silver with gold [9]. If silver points to the word of God (Ps 12:6), then gold points to the pure heavenly life; so the wealth of the Church coming from the Gentiles lies in her clinging to the word of God and her enjoyment of the heavenly mind.

10 "And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee. 11 Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought. 12 For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted. 13 The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious. 14 The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the LORD, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel. 15 Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, so that no man went through thee, I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations. 16 Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles, and shalt suck the breast of kings: and thou shalt know that I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob. 17 For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron: I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness. 18 Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise. 19 The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory. 20 Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the LORD shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended. 21 Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified. 22 A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the LORD will hasten it in his time."

a. "And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee" [10]. Here he points to Cyrus, the stranger by race, who ordered the return of the captives, and to the facilities given to Nehemiah to build the wall.
God in His love uses all foreign powers for the building of His Kingdom, offering every good for the sake of His Church; and this is the true glory of the Church: the sanctifying of every work!

b. The beauty of the Church is poured out in the opening of her gates continually, "they shall not be shut day nor night" [11]. She does not turn away a sinner nor wound his feelings; she bears a heart enlarged with love, like her Bridegroom, toward all.

She is like Noah's ark, whose doors were wide, receiving Noah and his family and the animals and birds, etc... Whoever was inside was saved, but whoever refused perished. "For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted" [12]. As the martyr Cyprian says: [There is no salvation outside the Church].

c. "The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious" [13]. Lebanon was known for its excellent trees, so its wealth of timber is turned to the adornment of the temple of the Lord. A wonderful picture of converting idle powers, or those that have been misused, for the sake of the temple of the Lord.

d. Enjoying spiritual authority, where the powers of darkness are subjected under the feet of the believers. "The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the LORD, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel" [14]. Even the enemy of good, with all his powers, bears witness to the believers that they are the holy city of God. The wicked cannot but testify to the children of God of the holiness of their lives, even in the moments of their persecuting them.

e. Her enjoyment of everlasting joy: "Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, so that no man went through thee, I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations" [15]. This is her eternal pride, that she is no longer forsaken and no longer suffers a state of emptiness or isolation or the hatred of others toward her, but is filled with joy and becomes glorious forever.

f. God gives her more than she asks and above what she requests: if she asks for brass He gives her gold, and if she asks for iron He gives her silver, and instead of wood He offers her brass, and in place of stones iron... Thus she finds in God her inner satisfaction, and also the secret of her spiritual wealth and the satisfaction of all her needs.

g. Justice dwells in her, therefore "Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise" [18]. Every man finds in her his salvation and the secret of his praise and joy, because the just God in her grants justice and righteousness, and does not permit injustice or destruction or oppression to be practiced within her.
h. As the icon of heaven she needs no sun or moon to light her, "but the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory" [19].
i. Enjoying the righteous life [21].

j. Enjoying the surpassing power of God: "A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation" [22]. Man in himself is counted small, but as a member of the body of Christ he is counted a thousand, that is, heavenly, because the number 1000 points to heaven. Outside Christ he is counted despised, played with by the enemy of good and crushed by sin, but in Christ Jesus he becomes a strong nation. He becomes a "nation" when he bears holy powers of spirit and body working together in harmony and unity, bearing within them the power of the Spirit of the Lord.

Thus this chapter presents to us a living picture of the Church of the Lord Christ as the illuminated city bearing within her the radiance of the Lord Christ, attracting the Gentiles and peoples through her inner glory, and sanctifying all their powers and abilities that they had misused. She opens her gates before all with love, and the Lord opens His gates before her to give her more than she asks and above what she requests; He gives her His righteousness, His justice, His power, His beauty and His light, so that nothing is lacking to her!

1 The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the poor; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; 2 To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn; 3 To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.

Through the words of the prophet Isaiah, the Lord Christ presents to us a living program of His saving work, which He sets forth briefly yet with depth. It is this: 1. Humanity's enjoyment of the Holy Spirit, who renews human nature and enriches it, removes its corruption and grants it the new life that is in Christ Jesus, so that it delights in fellowship in the divine life... This gift was offered to us in the person of the Lord Christ, who says: “The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me” [1]. As we said before in the interpretation of the eleventh chapter, the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of the Son, not a stranger to Christ; but through the Incarnation He received His descent upon Him in the name of the Church and on behalf of those who believe in Him:

* The Holy Spirit departed from man because He could not dwell in corruption; but now a new man has appeared among mankind, and he alone makes the return of the Spirit possible, for this man is without sin.

* God promised to give the Spirit a second time to mankind... and there was no other way by which this grace could be restored to humanity without departing again, except in Jesus Christ... It is an eternal return, caused by a state of stability and steadfastness.
* Christ gave the Holy Spirit to His humanity, and thereby made the Spirit become familiar once more with our nature.

* The return of the Holy Spirit to man in Christ, God incarnate, the second Adam, is an eternal return. For the Holy Spirit descended upon the second Adam because of His righteousness. And righteousness in Christ is steadfast righteousness, because the union of divinity with humanity in the person of Christ is steadfast... and this is a sure guarantee for humanity and its stability in the new life.

St. Cyril the Great * The name “Christ” implies the One who anoints, the One who is anointed, and the anointing itself. The Father is the One who anoints, the Son is anointed, and the Spirit is the anointing.

St. Irenaeus * The Holy Spirit shone in the fullness of His being upon Him, for like rests upon like. As for you, after you came up from the font of holy water, the anointing was given to you, which is a symbol of that with which Christ was anointed; this is the Holy Spirit.

St. Cyril of Jerusalem When the book of Isaiah was handed to the Lord Christ, He read this passage, “and he closed the book, and he gave it again to the minister, and sat down... And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears” (Lk 4:17-21). 2. The Lord Christ came to gladden the hearts of the poor with the gospel of His salvation, to bind up the brokenhearted and to grant freedom to the captives... counting His coming a true jubilee year, acceptable to the Lord and granting comfort to those who mourn (Isa 61:2; Lev 25:9, 40). 3. His coming is “the day of vengeance of our God” [2], in which He shattered the authority of the powers of darkness, the devil and his angels and his evil works. 4. The Lord establishes the believers as trees of righteousness, or the planting of the Lord in the divine Paradise [3], bearing beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, and the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that is, He pours out upon us His beauty, His joy and His praise in place of humiliation, mourning and despair!

entries.section: 2. The new life of the Church:

paragraphs.text: 4 And they shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations, and they shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations. 5 And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers. 6 But ye shall be named the Priests of the LORD: men shall call you the Ministers of our God: ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles, and in their glory shall ye boast yourselves.

The mission of the Lord Christ, whom the Father anointed to preach good tidings to the poor, is “to repair the waste cities” that have become desolate through the generations. In every generation human nature has become like waste cities, needing to be torn down and rebuilt. This is the work of God the Creator, who establishes His Kingdom within us, and by His Holy Spirit transforms us from a dwelling of sin and evil into a sanctuary for the Lord. As for the strangers who feed our flocks, and the sons of the alien who keep watch over our land and work as vinedressers in our garden, they are the inner faculties of the soul and its impulses, which had become as though foreign and alien to the Lord and His Kingdom. They are brought into subjection anew, so that they are no longer a stumbling block in the way of our salvation but, on the contrary, a help to the soul, supporting it in its striving. This is as the Hebrew people did of old, when they carried gold, silver and fine garments out of Egypt and used them in setting up the tabernacle of meeting, instead of using them in the worship of idols in Egypt.

entries.section: 2. The new life of the Church:

paragraphs.text: He says: “Ye shall be named the Priests of the LORD” [6], because when we put on the new nature through Baptism we become priests spiritually, lifting up our hands in prayer and offering our bodies as a sacrifice of love acceptable to the Father. St. Jerome calls this priesthood “the lay priesthood (Laic Priesthood).”

entries.section: 3. The glorious life of the Church:

paragraphs.text: 7 For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them. 8 “For I the LORD love judgment, I hate him who seizes by wrong. And I will make their reward faithful, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them. 9 And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the LORD hath blessed.”
God grants His Church an abundance of inner glory, heavenly consolations and perpetual joy.

a. A double reward in place of the old afflictions: “For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double” [7].

What is the double reward that we enjoy in place of our shame? It is the enjoyment of the forgiveness of our sins and the attainment of the righteousness of Christ; in other words, the removal of the shame of sin and the enjoyment of the glory of Christ in us; pardon for us as rebellious slaves and our acceptance as children of God in Jesus Christ, the Only-Begotten Son.

The atoning work of Christ did not stop at paying the debt that weighed us down, but He gave us His righteousness that we might share His glory. The Apostle says: “For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God. When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory” (Col 3:3-4).

Perhaps by the double inheritance He also means the two resurrections: the first resurrection, which we receive here in our temporal life as we enjoy the risen life, and the second resurrection, when the Lord of glory comes on the clouds, that we may rise with Him and be found with Him in glory. As St. Augustine says: [We who have died a twofold death (the death of the soul and of the body) rise with a twofold resurrection. Until now we have risen one resurrection, which is the resurrection from sin, for we were buried with Him in Baptism, and we rose with Him through Baptism in the resurrection. This resurrection is salvation from our sins; the other resurrection is the resurrection of the body. He has given us the greater resurrection, and behold, we await the lesser! The first resurrection is greater than the second, for our salvation from our sins is greater than the resurrection of the body.]

If the mark of the kingdom of the devil is the selfishness that brings hatred, then the shame into which we fell is that we were marked by deadly selfishness. In place of this shame we have received the double inheritance, that is, love in its two complementary aspects, love of God and love of neighbor. It is as though the work of Christ in us is to shatter the ego, in order to give us a surpassing love for God and for His creation.

b. “Everlasting joy shall be unto them” [7]; since the life of the Church here is a pledge of the heavenly life, it is marked by a double glory in place of shame, and by love in place of selfishness... and so it bears the nature of joy and gladness! The secret of our joy is that we bear our Christ within us, that He may establish His joyful heavenly Kingdom in our depths.

entries.section: 3. The glorious life of the Church:

paragraphs.text: c. “And I will make an everlasting covenant with them” [8]... The book of Isaiah often repeats the discussion of this covenant between God and His Church, declared in the body of the crucified Christ as the mystery of an eternal reconciliation.

entries.section: 3. The glorious life of the Church:

paragraphs.text: d. A blessing in their spiritual fruits as in their seed: “And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the LORD hath blessed” [9]...
What is this blessed seed that the Gentiles recognize?

He does not mean our children according to the flesh, but rather those who become disciples of the Lord through us, who come to know salvation and receive the new birth through our living witness to the gospel of our salvation.
Perhaps by the seed and the offspring He meant the holy works that are the fruits of the Spirit of the Holy God in us, and the gift of His free grace in our life.

10 I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with a turban, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels. 11 For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations.

The true life of the Church is a life of perpetual wedding, filled with joy and gladness without interruption, in which we put on the garment of salvation as the garment of the eternal wedding, or as a general priestly garment...

“I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with a turban (crown), and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels” [10].

In some traditional churches the priest repeats the preceding verse when he puts on the priestly vestments to take part in the Liturgy of the Eucharist, regarding himself as approaching the sacrament of the Eucharist as one approaches a joyful wedding, needing to put on the invisible garments of salvation, the robe of righteousness and the adornment of the Spirit... What is this garment but the Lord Christ Himself?! The believers put Him on when they enjoy the waters of Baptism (Gal 3:27).
* Truly Christ is the adornment of the bride, He who is, and who was, and who is to come, blessed now and forever, Amen.

St. Gregory of Nyssa * Now (after Baptism), since you have taken off your old garments and put on the white garments spiritually, it is fitting for you to continue wearing what is white. Of course we do not mean by this that you should wear a white garment at all times, but that you should wrap yourselves in white garments in truth, shining spiritually, and say with the blessed Isaiah: “My soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation...”.
* Keep the holy day, clothed in the garment of salvation, Jesus Christ.

St. Cyril of Jerusalem The prophet explained what he means by the garments of salvation, saying: “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” [11]; as though the garments of salvation were the righteousness of Christ and His praise, which He gives us as a free gift from His own.

entries.section: 1. A new name and a glorious life:

paragraphs.text: 1 For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth. 2 And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name. 3 Thou shalt also be a crown of beauty in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God.

“For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth. And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all the nations thy glory: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name” [1-2].

The speaker here is the Word of God, in whose heart the Church holds the central place; for He came into the world to betroth her to Himself as an eternal bride. If Boaz did not rest until he had completed the matter of his marriage to Ruth the Gentile (Ruth 3:18), then the Lord Christ does not cease His constant work until He has joined to Himself, as His bride, the Church that He acquired with His precious blood. He is the Sun of righteousness who shines upon her, so that she bears His righteousness as her own righteousness. She enjoys splendor and becomes a spiritual lamp that all the winds of the world cannot extinguish. He speaks to her, saying: “And thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom. And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord Christ” (Ezek 16:13-14).

The Lord Christ gives her His splendor within her and His glory as glory for her, so that she enjoys the renewal that reaches even the name, the sign of complete renewal: “And thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name.” For when the Lord Christ came and by His Holy Spirit gave us renewal, we took His name as a new name and became “Christians.” For this reason the early apologists, such as the philosopher Athenagoras, said: [The true accusation that was brought against the Christians was the accusation of “the Name.” The persecution against them was fierce not because of a crime they had committed, but because of the name they bore.

entries.section: 1. A new name and a glorious life:

paragraphs.text: The Church of the New Testament enjoyed being attributed to the name of the Savior as a living source for enjoying His surpassing righteousness as the secret of her beauty: “Thou shalt also be a crown of beauty in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God” [3]. The Lord calls her a “crown of beauty” and a “royal diadem,” not that she may be placed on the head of the Lord, for He needs no additional honor, but that she is in His hand; she is the work of His hands, her glory is of His own making. He cherishes her, and He remains the Head while she is His glorious body.

4 Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married. 5 For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee.

One of the new names that the Church has enjoyed is “the bride of Christ.” “Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married. For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee” [4-5].

Outside Christ the Savior she was called “Forsaken” and “Desolate,” like a barren land without life or fruit, and like a girl whom everyone has abandoned, so that she became a ruined soul crushed by the feeling of isolation and desertion. Now, in Christ, she has become an eternal heavenly bride; therefore she has taken two honored titles in place of the two former names: “Hephzibah,” which means “my delight is in her,” and “Beulah,” that is, “the one who has a husband” or “married.” She has become the object of God's delight, living in the bosom of her heavenly Bridegroom.

Her sons love her land and work with joy and gladness as though they were married to the Church, working on her behalf not as slaves nor as hired servants awaiting their reward, but as a husband who delights in his bride, seeking her rest and her comfort... This is the mark of the children of God, who with joy dedicate their hearts, their thoughts and their energies to work in the Church of Christ.
It is noted that this bride is unique and wonderful in the following respects:

a. She is a virgin and at the same time a mother who has sons, a thing that will not be realized in the life of any girl, but it was realized in the holy Virgin Mary, the Theotokos. She bore Jesus, the Lord of glory, and remained ever-virgin, because her Son is the Giver of virginity, and so she became the most perfect member of the Church.
Our Church is a chaste virgin (2 Cor 11:2), and she is at the same time the mother of the believers.
We also, when we receive membership in the Church, have our souls become chaste virgins within, and through love they bear a kind of motherhood toward human beings.
* Your virginity must be spiritual...
Truly, many cannot be virgins according to the flesh, but every believer is bound to be a virgin according to the spirit.
Therefore awake, O my soul, and take care of your virginity.
* The mother of the Lord Christ is a virgin, and His bride, “the Church,” is also a virgin.
St. Ambrose * Grace made the Virgin a mother and did not dissolve her virginity.

Father Theodotus, Bishop of Ancyra b. By saying: “As a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee” [5], he reveals the unity of the Church, for he regarded all her children as one young man, because all live with one aim and one goal, which is union with the Father in His Son Jesus Christ by the Holy Spirit. On the other hand, he makes clear that he does not mean marriage in the bodily sense, for it is not fitting for sons to marry their mother, but he means the attachment of the children of God to His bride the Church and their union with her. Finally, the likening of the children of the Church to a young man means that they are marked by perpetual youthfulness, in which old age does not overtake them and weakness does not afflict them.

c. By saying: “And as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee” [5], he reveals that the Church is marked by perpetual joy, and that she remains in a state of perpetual wedding in which each of the two parties longs for the other. In other words, the wedding does not grow old and is not subject to time, but remains an eternal, perpetual wedding.

It is wonderful that in the rite of the Coptic Church, during the Marriage service, attention is directed toward the Church as the bride of Christ, and also toward St. Mary as a living example of enjoying an inner wedding with the Lord Christ. At the end of the service of this Liturgy the deacons chant this hymn:

“Hail to the shining bride, the mother of Him who shines; hail to her who received into herself the Word who is in her womb; hail to her who is more honorable than the Cherubim; hail to her who bore for us the Savior of our souls...”.

6 I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the LORD, keep not silence, 7 and let him not keep silence, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth. 8 The LORD hath sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, “Surely I will no more give thy corn to be meat for thine enemies; and the sons of the stranger shall not drink thy wine, for the which thou hast laboured: 9 But they that have gathered it shall eat it, and praise the LORD; and they that have brought it together shall drink it in the courts of my holiness.”

The Jews suffered the captivity and regarded themselves as a wife forsaken by her husband, or as a land that had become desolate; and behold, the Lord brings them back to be sons working in their land (their country). But perhaps some feared being exposed to captivity once more; therefore the Lord affirms His watching over His people who have returned to Him.

If the enemy of good took us captive in his land, and deprived us of the promised land and of the enjoyment of the heavenly holy things, now through the Cross we have become the bride of the Lord, and we have returned, as it were, to Paradise as a house of our own, or as a holy city in which we dwell with our God, who sets a strict and vigilant guard at our walls, watching the enemy night and day without ceasing [6].

Who are these watchmen whom the Lord sets over His Church but His faithful and vigilant servants, especially in the spirit of constant prayer together with pastoral work filled with love? This is what we perceive in the ministry of the Apostle Paul, who says: “Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears” (Acts 20:31). And also in the ministry of the prophet Samuel, who says: “Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the LORD in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way” (1 Sam 12:23). Thus constant prayer is joined with love and with continual teaching, all of them being the work of watching over the city of the Lord.

In the life of the true Christian who has practical spiritual knowledge—the Gnostic—it is necessary to set up a constant inner watch, which St. Clement of Alexandria expressed by saying: [It is fitting for the Gnostic to contemplate God as far as possible].

How wonderful is the statement: “Ye that make mention of the LORD, keep not silence, and let him not keep silence” [6-7]. Thus the Lord calls us to remember Him continually and not to be silent, and then He too answers and is not silent; we remember Him and He remembers us, for He longs to bring us into strong and continuous dealings with Him, asking that we be established like His glorious Jerusalem, and that He make of us “a praise in the earth” [7]. Everyone who looks at us or comes into contact with us enjoys an icon of heaven, true inner joy.

God grants us to enjoy the fruit of His Holy Spirit, wheat and wine, without the enemy seizing it from us. What is the wheat but the enjoyment of fellowship with Christ, the unique ear of grain?! And what is the wine but the gift of the Holy Spirit, the Giver of joy?! It is as though our watchfulness in the Lord preserves our fellowship with God in Jesus Christ, our heavenly wheat, by means of His Holy Spirit, the unique wine.

10 Go through, go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a standard for the people. 11 Behold, the LORD hath proclaimed unto the end of the world, Say ye to the daughter of Zion, “Behold, thy Saviour cometh; behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.” 12 And they shall call them, The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD: and thou shalt be called, Sought out, A city not forsaken.

Preparing the way for the Lord in our life is a preparing of our own way into His heavens. He passes through to the gates of our hearts to carry us to His everlasting gates. He set up His Cross as a banner of love for us, that by it we may pass through the spiritual battle and receive the heavenly reward. Therefore it was said: “Go through, go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a standard for the people. Behold, the LORD hath proclaimed unto the end of the world; say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy Saviour cometh; behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him” [10-11].
St. John the Baptist came to prepare the way for the Lord (Mt 3:3), but the One who truly works and who rewards is the Savior of the Church.

1 Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? “I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.” 2 Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat? 3 “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I have trodden them in mine anger, and trampled them in my fury; and their juice was sprinkled upon my garments, and I have stained all my raiment. 4 For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come. 5 And I looked, and there was none to help; and I wondered that there was none to uphold: therefore mine own arm brought salvation unto me; and my fury, it upheld me. 6 And I have trodden down the people in mine anger, and made them drunk in my fury, and poured out their juice upon the earth.”

In the day of the destruction of Jerusalem at the hands of Babylon, the sons of Edom stood gloating, and even played a positive role against Jerusalem by seizing the fugitives to hand them over as captives, and by entering with their spoils to pasture in Jerusalem, and so on... Therefore the psalmist cries out, saying: “Remember, O LORD, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof” (Ps 137:7); and as the prophet Obadiah says: “For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever. In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them” (Obad 1:10-11).

Edom (meaning earth, and a lover of shedding blood) points to the enemy of good, the devil. Therefore the Savior appears as one coming from Edom in red garments, in His majesty and greatness; He overcame the enemy and trod him down as in a winepress, to give His people victory and salvation.

“Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?! this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength?! I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save” [1].
The prophet looked upon the Savior as He was lifted up on the Cross, shattering the true Edom and giving victory and splendor to His believers, and so he began to ask Him:
Who art Thou?
From where dost Thou come?
What is Thy condition?
What is Thy work? And what is Thy purpose?

As to His person, He says: “I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save” [1]. Many speak of righteousness and are skilled in discoursing about it; even some of the religious leaders of that time were able to teach concerning righteousness. But the Savior, our Lord Jesus, is the only One able to speak of righteousness that is “mighty to save,” that is, practical righteousness that grants deliverance from enemies and the enjoyment of eternity. He alone is the Righteous One who knew no sin (2 Cor 5:21), who bore our sins in His body to atone for them by His shed blood, giving us His righteousness as our righteousness. He is unique in His righteousness: on the one hand, He alone is absolutely without blemish, and on the other hand, He is able to justify others. He is the Righteous One in whom the Father is well pleased, and He carries us in Himself that we too may be counted objects of His good pleasure.

The Lord Christ speaks of righteousness not with His mouth only, but with His whole being and His life, which He gave by His holy will through His divine love for the sake of our justification, to restore our corrupt nature and give it fellowship in the divine nature (2 Pet 1:4).

As to the place, he saw Him coming from “Edom,” which means “earth” or “blood.” It is as though the Lord came to where we had fallen, to Edom, where we returned to our dust, in order to turn our dust into heaven. It was said to us, “for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return” (Gen 3:19); now that our heavenly Savior has come down to our earth that we may be united with Him, we hear the divine voice: “For heaven thou art, and unto heaven shalt thou return.” This is the righteousness of Christ that lifts us as from the dunghill to set us in His heavens.
