From another side, since we became “Edom” (= blood), lovers of fighting or haters of others, our Christ came to the field of battle to wrest us from the enemy of good, the lover of shedding blood, that our hearts might be enlarged with love and self-giving!

As to His work, He says: “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me” [3]. He entered the battle, the battle of the Cross, alone, as He said to His disciples: “and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me” (Jn 16:32).

His apparel is red and His garments like him that treadeth in the winefat [2], since they put a scarlet robe on Him (Mk 15:17) to mock Him. It also indicates that His whole body poured out blood from the wounds that bring healing (Isa 53:5). This self-giving is the secret of a surpassing beauty, which is perceived by one who has experienced the Cross as the power of God unto salvation; therefore it was said, “glorious in his apparel” [1].
* He wrought a wonderful dispensation for the suffering body, for it was adorned with sufferings and glorified with divinity, and there is nothing more sweet and beautiful than that.

St. Gregory of Nazianzus What He did was inspired by His great love and His zeal for His bride, since He wanted to free her from the enemy, the devil, and to give her the enjoyment of the perpetual year of jubilee, or unbroken liberation [4].

entries.section: 2. A hymn about the Lord's lovingkindnesses:

paragraphs.text: 7 I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the LORD, and the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD hath bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he hath bestowed on them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his lovingkindnesses. 8 For he said, Surely they are my people, children that will not betray: so he was their Saviour. 9 In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.

The prophet found nothing that the Church, the bride redeemed by blood, could offer in return for God's constant lovingkindnesses, which were revealed in their deepest form on the Cross, except praise to Him.

entries.section: 2. A hymn about the Lord's lovingkindnesses:

paragraphs.text: God did not bestow His lovingkindnesses for the sake of some return, but because of His mercies and the multitude of His lovingkindnesses, looking upon us as His people and His sons; He shares with us our affliction and our sufferings. “In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence (the Savior) saved them” [9]. It is a wonderful love!

10 But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them. 11 Then he remembered the days of old, Moses, and his people, saying, “Where is he that brought them up out of the sea with the shepherd of his flock? where is he that put his holy Spirit in the midst of them, 12 That led them by the right hand of Moses with his glorious arm, dividing the water before them, to make himself an everlasting name, 13 That led them through the deep, as an horse in the wilderness, that they should not stumble? 14 As a beast goeth down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD caused him to rest.” So didst thou lead thy people, to make thyself a glorious name.

If man in his foolishness takes a stand against his Creator and Redeemer, God in His love remembers His former works with them, how He shepherded them through Moses, and how He dwelt in their midst by His Holy Spirit. He divided the waters before them that His name might be glorified in them... God is still the same, in a love that wants to lead His people Himself!

Truly He disciplines them for their hostile stand, but He remains waiting for their return. This is what He meant by saying: “But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them. Then he remembered the days of old,” and so on... [10-11].

* If we pray and chant the Psalms before Him in pride, in a critical manner, in arrogance, if we perform the service with a scattered mind, He not only does not listen to us but even delivers us to the evil one... He turns to become an adversary who fights us; in other words, He withdraws us from His presence and delivers us to Satan for our discipline, until we cease from blaspheming (1 Tim 1:20).
Father Martyrius the Syrian

15 Look down from heaven, and behold from the habitation of thy holiness and of thy glory: where is thy zeal and thy strength, the sounding of thy bowels and of thy mercies toward me? are they restrained? 16 Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O LORD, art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting. 17 O LORD, why hast thou made us to err from thy ways, and hardened our heart from thy fear? Return for thy servants' sake, the tribes of thine inheritance. 18 The people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while: our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary. 19 We have been of old as they over whom thou never barest rule; upon whom thy name was not called.

When we fall into evil and stand as enemies of God, God remains waiting for our repentance. So we do not justify our faults, but we move His love and His zeal toward us, since He is our Father, who knows us more than Abraham, the father of the believers, and Israel himself [16].

“Look down from heaven, and behold from the habitation of thy holiness and of thy glory” [15]. Thus the sinner feels as though he had defiled the earth with his sin and his abomination, and as though God had left the earth to remain in heaven, where His sanctuary and His glory are; therefore he moves God's mercies, asking Him to look down from His pure heavens upon the fallen soul that longs to return to Him and to enjoy His presence.

Perhaps this feeling came as a result of what had befallen the temple of the Lord in destruction, for the prophet Ezekiel saw the glory of the Lord leaving the temple and the city of Jerusalem, indeed the whole earth, when he says: “Then the glory of the LORD departed from off the threshold of the house, and stood over the cherubims. And the cherubims lifted up their wings, and mounted up from the earth in my sight” (Ezek 10:18-19).

“Where is thy zeal...? and thy mercies toward me are restrained” [15]. Repentance is built on the discovery of the Lord's zeal toward His children and His surpassing, deep love, “the sounding of thy bowels,” and His mercies toward man, whatever his weaknesses. It is also built on man's awareness of his sonship to Him (Deut 32:6; Isa 63:16).

“O LORD, why hast thou made us to err from thy ways? and hardened our heart from thy fear? Return for thy servants' sake, the tribes of thine inheritance” [17]. It is clear here that the penitent does not mean to cast blame on God; rather, having at once discovered God's fatherhood, he reproaches Him, because he had expected that His grace would support him. Truly he sinned and persisted in sin, so God gave him over to a reprobate mind and left him to the hardness of his heart (Rom 1:28); now he asks for His grace, that he may not err from the way of the Lord nor remain in hardness of heart. This is what the psalmist meant by saying: “With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments” (Ps 119:10).

When a person comes under discipline he feels bitterness, and so he stands reproaching God by every means: at one time he asks Him not to allow it any longer, leaving him in the corruption of his mind and the hardness of his heart; at another he asks for His mercy for the sake of His blessed saints who intercede for humanity [17]; and finally he asks Him to hasten to help, since the period of discipline has been long. This is what the prophet expressed by saying: “The people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while: our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary. We have been of old as they over whom thou never barest rule; upon whom thy name was not called” [18-19]. They counted the time in which the people possessed the temple, “the sanctuary of the Lord,” to be short, although it amounts to about 400 years from the building of the temple until the captivity; but the period of the captivity (70 years) they counted as exceedingly long because of its bitterness, for they say, “We have been of old...” They became under the captivity like the rest of the nations, as though God were not ruling over them to rescue them from this bitterness, and as though His name had not been called upon them...
Having tasted the bitterness of the captivity, they longed for the Lord to reign over them and to call His name upon them, that He might save them.

entries.section: 1. The descent of the Messiah from heaven:

paragraphs.text: 1 Oh that thou wouldest rend the heavens, that thou wouldest come down, that the mountains might quake at thy presence, 2 As when the fire kindleth the stubble, and the fire causeth the waters to boil, to make thy name known to thine adversaries, that the nations may tremble at thy presence! 3 When thou didst terrible things which we looked not for, thou camest down, the mountains quaked at thy presence.

“Oh that thou wouldest rend the heavens, that thou wouldest come down, that the mountains might quake at thy presence, as when the fire kindleth the stubble, and the fire causeth the waters to boil, to make thy name known to thine adversaries, that the nations may tremble at thy presence” [1-2].

Some interpreters see that the discourse here concerns the Lord Christ when He descends from heaven openly to establish His kingdom on earth for a thousand years, reigning and defeating His opponents and enemies and all the nations, and so on... in contrast to His first coming, which was hidden in the womb of the Virgin, when He does not cry out nor does anyone hear His voice, and so on...

I do not want to speak here about the millennial kingdom, since I dealt with it in the interpretation of chapter 19 of the Book of Revelation; what I want to affirm is that the texts of the prophet Isaiah are not understood in a literal way, because our Christ is a spiritual King, who refused to reign materially, counting His divine Incarnation a descent as from heaven to meet us. We were like mountains in the hardness of our life, and so our depths were shaken; He kindled the stubble of evil within us, and made the cold waters within us boil with love, granting us victory over the enemies of His name, not through visible wars but through faith working by love.

For deliverance from captivity or afflictions, it is enough for man to ask God to look down from heaven and behold from the habitation of His holiness and His glory (Isa 63:15), although God fills heaven and earth with His divinity... But for our salvation from our sins and our return to the Father's embrace, the matter requires the rending of the heavens and the descent of the Word of God to our earth [1]. As the Lord Christ said of Himself.

* “For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me... that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day” (Jn 6:38-40). He came down from heaven to accomplish obedience in place of the fallen Adam in disobedience, offering the will of the Father, which is one with His will. And the will of the Father is the accomplishment of salvation and resurrection by seeing the Son in faith and abiding in Him.
* “No man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven” (Jn 3:13).
And St. John the Baptist said of Him: “He that cometh from heaven is above all” (Jn 3:31).
St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian praises the Word of God who rent the heavens and came down, saying:
[Blessed is He who by His Incarnation bought life for our human nature!
Blessed is He who sealed our souls and adorned them and betrothed them to Himself as a bride!
Blessed is He who made our body a tent for His invisible nature...!
Glory to Him who looked upon us, how we accepted to resemble the beasts in our rage and our greed, and came down to us and became one of us, that we might become heavenly...!].
The prophet David looked to the divine Incarnation and said: “He bowed the heavens also, and came down” (Ps 18:9).

Some see that by saying “Oh that thou wouldest rend the heavens, that thou wouldest come down, that the mountains might quake at thy presence” [1] he means that the people in the midst of their affliction felt as though God had hidden His face from them with a cloud: “The LORD dwelleth in the thick darkness” (2 Chr 6:1); “Thick clouds are a covering to him, that he is not seen” (Job 22:14). It is as though they were crying out that if our sins have hidden Thee behind the clouds, and have veiled from us the perception of the mysteries of Thy purposes, there is none who can set the matter right but Thyself. We cannot ascend to Thee, but Thou canst rend the veil and come down to us. It is not enough that Thou lookest upon us from Thy heavens; we need Thy dwelling in our midst.

“The mountains quake” [1]. If the solid mountains trembled at Sinai when God met with Moses (Ex 19:17-18), and the mountains were rent and the rocks broken in pieces before the Lord when He spoke to Elijah (1 Kgs 19:11), who can stand before Him?! God alone is able to solve all our problems, shaking our old man and shattering the might of our evil in order to establish His kingdom within us. If the devil and all his soldiers and angels, with their evil works and deceits, are like mountains, then the Lord shakes their kingdom by the Cross; and if they are like stubble (like brittle dry straw that is good for nothing but fuel), then God destroys them with fire.

We need the Lord to come down to us because our enemies who are like mountains are the enemies of His name; they oppose us to tear us away from His Kingdom or to tear His name and His Kingdom out of us.

entries.section: 1. The descent of the Messiah from heaven:

paragraphs.text: The opposition of the enemies, the devil and his soldiers, however violent it may be, becomes like stubble that God burns with fire, not only to scatter the opposition but to turn it to good, since He uses these fires to heat the cold waters of our hearts so that they boil with love and holy zeal [2]. St. John Chrysostom says: [Even the devil can be a cause of benefit to us if we understand him... This is clear in the case of Job. We can also learn this from Paul, who writes concerning the fornicator: “To deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved” (1 Cor 5:5). See how even Satan has become a cause of salvation, not by his nature, but by the skill of the Apostle, like a physician who takes a viper to extract a medicine from it].

entries.section: 2. The blessings of waiting for the Messiah:

paragraphs.text: 4 For from eternity they have not heard nor given ear, neither hath the eye seen a God beside thee, which worketh for him that waiteth for him. 5 Thou meetest him that rejoiceth and worketh righteousness, those that remember thee in thy ways. Behold, thou art wroth; for we have sinned: it is for ever, and we shall be saved.

As the prophets lived awaiting the coming of the Messiah for salvation, we remain always waiting for Him to reign, not on earth, but in our hearts, over our inner life, that He may carry us into the fellowship of His glory; we see what God has prepared for us, and we are filled with joy by His righteousness working in us. The prophet says: “For from eternity they have not heard nor given ear, neither hath the eye seen a God beside thee, which worketh for him that waiteth for him. Thou meetest him that rejoiceth and worketh righteousness...” [4-5].

Though God's works have been wonderful from of old, nothing has ever been heard or seen like what the Lord did with mankind through His saving works; for He went forth as from heaven to meet sinners with joy, working righteousness in their lives, granting them inner glories as a pledge of the eternal glory.

St. Hippolytus comments on this prophetic statement, speaking in the person of the Lord Christ: [Enter into the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. Enjoy forever what is given to you by My Father who is in the heavens and the life-giving Holy Spirit. What mouth can tell of these blessings which eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him (Isa 64:4; 1 Cor 2:9)? You have heard of the unbroken joy! You have heard of the unchanging Kingdom! You have now learned of the banquet of blessings that has no end!].

6 But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away. 7 And there is none that calleth upon thy name, that stirreth up himself to take hold of thee: for thou hast hid thy face from us, and hast consumed us, because of our iniquities. 8 But now, O LORD, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand. 9 Be not wroth very sore, O LORD, neither remember iniquity for ever: behold, see, we beseech thee, we are all thy people. 10 Thy holy cities are a wilderness, Zion is a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation. 11 Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised thee, is burned up with fire: and all our pleasant things are laid waste. 12 Wilt thou refrain thyself for these things, O LORD? wilt thou hold thy peace, and afflict us very sore?

Our souls remain always rejoicing for God's surpassing saving works, always awaiting a continual meeting with Him, that He may remove the shame of our sins and declare the glory of His righteousness in us. The way of this meeting is:

a. Confession of sins: “Behold, thou art wroth; for we have sinned” [5]. St. Cyprian says: [Good is repentance! If it has no place in your heart, you will lose the grace of the washing that you received in Baptism long ago, for it is better for us to have a garment to mend than to have no garment to wear; but once the garment has been prepared for us, it must be renewed...]. And St. John Climacus says: [Repentance renews Baptism, a covenant made with God for a second life]. And St. John Chrysostom says: [Have you sinned? Say to God: “I have sinned.” What toil is there in this...?].

b. Our realization of the inability of self-righteousness to save us: “But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away” [6]. As Father Martyrius the Syrian Martyrius: Sahdona of Halmon says: [Our whole inner being is swallowed up when we see Him (Dan 10:8); because of His majesty our mouths fall silent. When we receive a little strength to speak with Him, our consciences blame us, and we see that we have sinned and done iniquity in His presence (Ps 106:6). If we imagine that we have come to the place of the righteous, all our righteousness is as a menstrual rag (Ex 36:17); to Him belongs victory, but to us confusion of face and shame (Bar 1:15)].
Father Theonas shows us how our good works turn to wickedness if we rely on our own righteousness, for our righteousness is counted as a menstrual rag when compared with the divine righteousness.

c. Awareness of God's tender fatherhood, which forgives sins: “But now, O LORD, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand. Be not wroth very sore...” [8-9].

God presents Himself to us as Father, Bridegroom, Friend and self-giving Shepherd... in order to draw every soul to Himself by repentance. And His Church bears the same mark so as to embrace all with love, that they may enjoy God's wonderful salvation. In a letter to a fallen monk, St. Basil the Great says:
[I grieve for you, for what priest does not weep when he hears this...?!
What minister of the altar does not beat his breast?!
What “layman” is not broken in heart?!
What ascetic does not grieve...?!
You have shattered all at once, all at once you have despised everyone...
Remember the good Shepherd who follows you and calls to you...

I beg you not to hesitate to come to me because of any earthly consideration, for I lament when I find my dead one, I stay by him and weep for him because of “the spoiling of the daughter of my people” (Isa 22:4).
Behold, all are ready to welcome you! All join with you in your striving, so do not draw back...
It is a time for salvation, it is a season for amendment!
Be cheerful and do not despair, for she (the Church) is not a law that condemns the sinner without mercy, but (she has) a law of mercy that removes the penalty and awaits amendment.
Behold, the doors have not yet been shut, the Bridegroom hears...
Have pity on yourself and on all of us in our Lord Jesus Christ].
d. It reminds us that we are His people who belong to Him [9].
e. Our confession of the ruin that has befallen us: we have become a barren wilderness, fires have been kindled within us, and all the inner sanctuaries have been disfigured.
1 “I gave ear to them that asked not for me; I was found of them that sought me not: I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name.

“I gave ear to them that asked not for me; I was found of them that sought me not: I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name” [1]. It is clear here that the discourse concerns the acceptance of the Gentiles, who had not known God nor sought Him before nor borne His name, but who believed in the Savior and so enjoyed what the people of God had deprived themselves of.

St. Paul spoke of the calling of the Gentiles and the rejection of the unbelieving Jews in his Epistle to the Romans (Rom 9:11), citing the prophetic statement found here (Rom 10:20-21). For God gave ear to the Gentiles who had not asked Him, and those who had not sought Him found Him, because while we were enemies He reconciled us to the Father. He loved all mankind before they loved Him, and chose us before we knew Him or sought Him. He inclined our hearts to Himself, taking the initiative of love before His name was called upon us.

St. John Chrysostom says: [Did Israel hear and not understand? If the pagan Gentiles have heard and grasped the faith, how much more should the Jews have done, to whom God gave from of old all the signs aimed at removing the veil from their eyes].

* Who are those who did not seek Him? Who are those who did not ask for Him? Certainly not the Jews, but those who are of the Gentiles who did not know Him, whom Moses described in the words: “not a people,” “a foolish nation”; and on the same basis he refers to them here because of their extreme ignorance.
It is a very great shame that those who did not seek Him found Him, and those who searched for Him lost Him (through their unbelief).
St. John Chrysostom * Who is this who was revealed (and whom the Gentiles found) but the Word of the Father, when the Father sent Him, and in Him is the power for men that proceeds from Him?!
St. Hippolytus

2 I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts; 3 A people that provoketh me to anger continually to my face; that sacrificeth in gardens, and burneth incense upon altars of brick; 4 Which remain among the graves, and lodge in the monuments, which eat swine's flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels; 5 Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou. These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day. 6 Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will recompense, even recompense into their bosom, 7 Your iniquities, and the iniquities of your fathers together, saith the LORD, which have burned incense upon the mountains, and blasphemed me upon the hills: therefore will I measure their former work into their bosom.”

“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts.” The Lord spread out His hands on the Cross with love to embrace all and give them the life of victory, as the prophet Moses spread out his hands during the battle against Amalek, as a symbol of the saving work of Christ.
The Lord spread out His hands from His side, waiting for us to respond to this work by seeking Him every day, as St. Paphnutius says.
As for the secret of God's rejection of His people, it is:
a. Their rebellion [2], seeking to walk according to their own desires and not according to the mind of God.
b. Their breaking of the Law, and their turning aside to idolatrous worship [3-4].
c. Their reliance on self-righteousness [5].
St. Augustine sees that the denial of faith in the Lord is death, for they saw the miracles of the Savior with their own eyes and did not live through them, but remained as in a state of death.

8 Thus saith the LORD, “As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it: so will I do for my servants' sakes, that I may not destroy them all. 9 And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob, and out of Judah an inheritor of my mountains: and mine elect shall inherit it, and my servants shall dwell there. 10 And Sharon shall be a fold of flocks, and the valley of Achor a place for the herds to lie down in, for my people that have sought me.”

Although the people as a whole took a stand of ingratitude, there is a holy remnant for the Lord, such as the disciples, the Apostles, the Marys, Zacchaeus the tax collector, Levi, and so on... This holy few does not perish but is a blessing. “Thus saith the LORD, As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it: so will I do for my servants' sakes, that I may not destroy them all” [8].
Among the opponents there were found those chosen by the Lord, His servants, who seek Him [10].

entries.section: 4. A comparison between the believers and the unbelievers:

paragraphs.text: 11 “But ye are they that forsake the LORD, that forget my holy mountain, that prepare a table for the Greater Fortune, and that fill mixed wine for the Lesser Fortune. 12 Therefore will I number you to the sword, and ye shall all bow down to the slaughter: because when I called, ye did not answer; when I spake, ye did not hear; but did evil before mine eyes, and did choose that wherein I delighted not. 13 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, my servants shall eat, but ye shall be hungry: behold, my servants shall drink, but ye shall be thirsty: behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed: 14 Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart, but ye shall cry for sorrow of heart, and shall howl for vexation of spirit. 15 And ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen: for the Lord GOD shall slay thee, and call his servants by another name: 16 That he who blesseth himself in the earth shall bless himself in the God of truth; and he that sweareth in the earth shall swear by the God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hid from mine eyes.”

a. Some of those who forsook the Lord thought that they would be saved by holding idolatrous feasts marked by luxury and drunkenness, and they did not realize that they had become like sheep for the slaughter [11-12].

entries.section: 4. A comparison between the believers and the unbelievers:

paragraphs.text: b. The unbelievers often think that they live in luxury without deprivation, but soon the believers are satisfied and the unbelievers hunger, the former rejoice and the latter grieve. The believers enjoy a life of praise and inner rejoicing while the hearts of the unbelievers are broken [13-15].

entries.section: 4. A comparison between the believers and the unbelievers:

paragraphs.text: c. The believers are exposed to afflictions, but they receive the blessing of the true God even while on earth, and so they forget their troubles amid God's consolations and His blessing [16].

entries.section: 5. The new heavens and the new earth:

paragraphs.text: 17 “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind. 18 But be ye glad and rejoice for ever in that which I create: for, behold, I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people a joy. 19 And I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people: and the voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her, nor the voice of crying. 20 There shall be no more thence an infant of days, nor an old man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred years old; but the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed. 21 And they shall build houses, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them. 22 They shall not build, and another inhabit; they shall not plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands. 23 They shall not labour in vain, nor bring forth for terror; for they are the seed of the blessed of the LORD, and their offspring with them. 24 And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear. 25 The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpent's meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the LORD.”

The prophet Isaiah presents to us a wonderful picture of the work of the Lord Christ the Creator in establishing the Church of the New Testament. He created new heavens and a new earth [17]; He established a true renewal of the soul (the heavens) and of the body (the earth), so that soul and body together came into harmony, since both submitted to His Holy Spirit. The old conflict between the desires of the soul and the desires of the body has ended, and by the Holy Spirit we have entered into a life of spiritual joy and heavenly gladness, as our life is filled with the fruit of the Holy Spirit, love, joy and peace (Gal 5:22). We rejoice, as a holy bride renewed by her Bridegroom, and He rejoices in us, for He says: “And I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people” [19]. It is the joy of mutual love!

In this new life that became ours in Baptism, wolves are turned into lambs, so the wolf feeds with the lamb, and the nature of predation and ferocity is shattered, so the lion eats with the ox. As for the serpents, they do not hurt nor destroy the one who knows his sonship to God and lives by the possibilities of the life that has become his].
The marks of this new life are:
a. We no longer remember the former life, nor does it come into our mind, because the overflow of the Lord's blessing absorbs all our energies [17].

entries.section: 5. The new heavens and the new earth:

paragraphs.text: b. A life of perpetual, everlasting joy and gladness [18-19], in which the voice of weeping or crying is not heard.

entries.section: 5. The new heavens and the new earth:

paragraphs.text: c. In it there is no one who bears the weakness of childhood or old age, but all enjoy spiritual maturity [20].

entries.section: 5. The new heavens and the new earth:

paragraphs.text: d. It is full of blessings: they build spiritual houses in which they dwell with God, and plant vineyards to be satisfied with the fruits of the Spirit [21].

entries.section: 5. The new heavens and the new earth:

paragraphs.text: e. The enemy (the devil) does not seize any place in them [23].
f. They are filled with peace, no terror comes upon them [13].

entries.section: 5. The new heavens and the new earth:

paragraphs.text: g. The Lord answers their prayers before they utter them: “And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear” [24].

h. A change of nature by the removal of the spirit of enmity and the enjoyment of the spirit of love and unity, even between the wolf and the lamb, the lion and the ox, the serpent and man! People come from diverse nations, some of them marked by ferocity, and all become one people under the leadership of the Spirit of the Holy God.

1 Thus saith the LORD, “The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: where is the house that ye build unto me? and where is the place of my rest? 2 For all those things hath mine hand made, and all those things have been, saith the LORD: but to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word. 3 He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog's neck; he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swine's blood; he that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol. Yea, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations. 4 I also will choose their calamities, and will bring their fears upon them; because when I called, none did answer; when I spake, they did not hear: but they did evil before mine eyes, and chose that in which I delighted not.”

The Jews often relied on the presence of the temple in Jerusalem as a source of security for them, whatever their life or their relationship with the Lord might be. Therefore the Lord rebukes them, saying: “The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: where is the house that ye build unto me? and where is the place of my rest?” [1].

If God in His love for man permitted a house to be built for Him, it was only as a condescension of God to declare His dwelling in our midst. God is not concerned with stones and massive buildings; He dwells in “him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word” [see 2]. Solomon the wise realized this truth, and so he prayed on the day of the dedication of the temple, saying: “But will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?” (1 Kgs 8:27).

* He truly accepted the temple that was called “the temple of Jerusalem” as a house for Himself or a dwelling place, not out of need of it but so that, as you look at it, you may offer your souls to Him.

St. Justin * What is this dwelling that David remembers and pours out his soul upon it (Ps 42:2), longing for this house in a love strong unto death? Is it the tabernacle made of skins and reeds and blue and purple?! Without doubt David's vision is quite different from that...

Put away from you every earthly thought, and come, walk in the way that the prophets and Apostles open for you, and above all walk in the Word of God with all your heart and with all your understanding, that you may ascend to heaven and contemplate the splendor of the eternal dwelling, of which Moses showed you only a shadow.
Origen * The Church of God is heaven!
* “The soul of the righteous is the seat of wisdom”... The righteous are the thrones.
* You have become a heaven; will you then fear the earth...?

Therefore when you have attained perfect knowledge and have love, you become the throne of God and a heaven. For this heaven that we look at with these eyes is not very precious before God. Our holy souls are God's heaven; the minds of the angels and of all the ministers are God's heaven.

St. Augustine The Church is entering into the rock, as the prophet Moses did in order to see the glory of God; this rock is Christ. We are established in Him in a spirit of humility with contrition, and so we enjoy the divine indwelling; therefore it was said: “But to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word” [2].
* Do you wish to be a place for the Lord? Be poor in spirit, contrite and trembling at the Word of God, and what you ask will be fulfilled for you.
* Let our hearts tremble when God looks upon us, and so He rests in them.
St. Augustine * Let us tremble at His words, that He may build us up always.

St. John Chrysostom * It is fitting for us to take care to be in the narrow, straight way, the way of praise and glory, where it is fitting for all Christians to practice peace, humility and the quietness of a good life according to the word of the Lord, who looks only to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at His word [2].

St. Cyprian Thus by humility, contrition of heart and fear of His words the Lord looks upon us, and dwells in us, and transforms us into His holy heavens. But whoever is occupied with formalities in worship in a spirit of hypocrisy and pride, God finds no rest in him, and his worship becomes an abomination before Him. God smells in the sacrifices the odor of murder, uncleanness and idol worship, for He says: “He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog's neck; he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swine's blood; he that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol” [3]. And as the wise man says: “The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD: but the prayer of the upright is his delight” (Prov 15:8).

* (Animal) sacrifices do not sanctify man, for God has no need of a sacrifice, but it is the conscience of the one who offers it that sanctifies the sacrifice when it is pure, and by this he moves God to accept the offering.

St. Irenaeus The fruit of being occupied with formalities without spirit is to enter into troubles without consolation; and instead of the Lord reassuring them by saying to each one of them: “Fear not: for I am with thee; I have called thee by thy name, thou art mine” (Isa 43:1), He says to them: “They have chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations. I also will choose their calamities, and will bring their fears upon them; because when I called, none did answer; when I spake, they did not hear: but they did evil before mine eyes, and chose that in which I delighted not” [3-4].

They choose the evil way and delight in the abominations hated by the Lord; therefore God leaves them to their choice, and they fall under calamities that He brings upon them... which are the natural fruit of their conduct. They reject His call and do not listen to His voice; therefore He does not listen to their prayers nor answer their requests. They drink from the very cup that they filled.

entries.section: 2. The distinction between the formalists and the earnest in worship:

paragraphs.text: 5 Hear the word of the LORD, ye that tremble at his word: “Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my name's sake, said, Let the LORD be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed. 6 A voice of noise from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of the LORD that rendereth recompence to his enemies. 7 Before she travailed, she brought forth; before her pain came, she was delivered of a man child. 8 Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things? Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day? or shall a nation be born at once? for as soon as Zion travailed, she brought forth her children. 9 Shall I bring to the birth, and not cause to bring forth? saith the LORD: shall I cause to bring forth, and shut the womb? saith thy God.”

If the formalists in worship suffer troubles without consolation, then, on the contrary, those who are earnest in their lives, who tremble at the word of the Lord, are exposed to persecution even to expulsion, yet they enjoy true joy.

“Hear the word of the LORD, ye that tremble at his word: Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my name's sake, said, Let the LORD be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed” [5]. This is what happened when the Jews hated the disciples of the Lord and His Apostles and cast them out under the cover of zeal for the glory of God and the Law of Moses, but the disciples rejoiced and their persecutors were put to shame. The Lord Christ pointed to this by saying: “They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service” (Jn 16:2).

entries.section: 2. The distinction between the formalists and the earnest in worship:

paragraphs.text: As for the fruit of the affliction that came upon the men of the Church of the New Testament from their brethren, it is the destruction of the temple at the hands of Titus, for it was said here: “A voice of noise from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of the LORD that rendereth recompence to his enemies” [6].

entries.section: 2. The distinction between the formalists and the earnest in worship:

paragraphs.text: The opposition ended with the destruction of the temple, but the temple of the Church of the New Testament was established in every heart that bears fruit, which is the manifestation of the Lord of glory Jesus in the inner life of every believer. The prophet speaks to us here of the rise of this Church in a surpassing way, saying: “Before she travailed, she brought forth; before her pain came, she was delivered of a man child. Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things?” [7-8]. What is this birth but the manifestation of the Lord Christ in the lives of the believers.
The Fathers of the Church look at the spiritual life of the Christian after his baptism as a state of growth of Christ Himself within their hearts, which are marked by motherhood toward Him.

* As the child is formed in the womb, so it seems to me that the Word of God is formed in the heart of the soul that has received the grace of Baptism, so that it perceives within it the word of faith more glorious and more clear.

* It seems wrong to speak of the Incarnation of the Son of God from the holy Virgin and not to point also to His incarnation in the Church... for it is fitting for each one of us to know the coming of the Son of God in the flesh by means of the pure Virgin, and at the same time to realize His coming in the Spirit in each one of us.

Origen * What happened to Mary, who was without blemish, when the fullness of the divinity that is in Christ shone in her, is realized in every soul that practices virginity as its rule. Truly the Lord no longer comes to dwell in a bodily dwelling, “yet now henceforth know we him no more” according to the flesh (2 Cor 5:6), but He dwells in us spiritually, and brings with Him His Father, as He told us in the Gospel...

* By this every Christian can become a mother of Him who is in essence everything, for our Lord Himself says: “Whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my mother” (Mk 3:25; Mt 12:5).
St. Gregory of Nyssa * (Every Christian) conceives God in his heart.

St. Augustine * He calls the soul that begins to move toward the Lord Christ thus: “Mary,” that is, it receives the name of the woman who bore Him in her womb, since the soul bears Him in a spiritual sense.
* Take care to fulfill the will of the Father so that you may be a mother of Christ (Mk 3:25).

entries.section: 2. The distinction between the formalists and the earnest in worship:

paragraphs.text: St. Ambrose The catholic Church was born with power as in one day, for it was said: “Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day? or shall a nation be born at once?” [8], since she was born on the day of Pentecost and grew with wonderful speed.

10 Rejoice ye with Jerusalem, and be glad with her, all ye that love her: rejoice for joy with her, all ye that mourn for her: 11 That ye may suck, and be satisfied with the breasts of her consolations; that ye may milk out, and be delighted with the abundance of her glory. 12 For thus saith the LORD, “Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the Gentiles like a flowing stream: then shall ye suck, ye shall be borne upon her sides, and be dandled upon her knees. 13 As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem. 14 And when ye see this, your heart shall rejoice, and your bones shall flourish like an herb: and the hand of the LORD shall be known toward his servants, and his indignation toward his enemies. 15 For, behold, the LORD will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. 16 For by fire and by his sword will the LORD plead with all flesh: and the slain of the LORD shall be many. 17 They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the gardens behind one tree in the midst, eating swine's flesh, and the abomination, and the mouse, shall be consumed together, saith the LORD. 18 And I will recompense their works and their thoughts: it shall come, that I will gather all nations and tongues; and they shall come, and see my glory. 19 And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, that draw the bow, to Tubal, and Javan, to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory; and they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles. 20 And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the LORD out of all nations upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and upon mules, and upon swift beasts, to my holy mountain Jerusalem, saith the LORD, as the children of Israel bring an offering in a clean vessel into the house of the LORD. 21 And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the LORD. 22 For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the LORD, so shall your seed and your name remain. 23 And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD. 24 And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.”
The prophet concludes his discourse by revealing the new Jerusalem:

a. She overflows with joy and gladness upon those who love her and mourn for her because of the afflictions she suffers [10]. Outwardly there are pains and troubles, and inwardly an overflow of joy even upon others.
b. She overflows with satisfaction for all; she gives the little ones consolations as from the milk of her breasts, while she gives the grown the juice and delight of the abundance of her glory.

c. An overflow of peace like a river, and great glory like a flowing stream. “For thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the Gentiles like a flowing stream: then shall ye suck, ye shall be borne upon her sides, and be dandled upon her knees” [12].
God Himself directs peace upon His Church as the farmer waters his field, irrigating it from the springs of His peace as from an unfailing river, and pours glory out upon her.

* In His promise to the righteous He says that He will pour out upon them a river of peace, meaning that He will pour out upon them the greatest possibility. By this peace we are refreshed... and all are satisfied by it, for it will overflow even upon earthly bodies with the peace of incorruption and immortality... as though God pours (Himself) from the things above into the things below, and makes men equal to the angels.

St. Augustine d. A source of divine comfort: “As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem” [13]. God, as Father, grants the Church a motherhood not only toward the believers, her children, but toward every human being; she bears a heart as wide as her Bridegroom's, to overflow with love upon all.

As a mother she offers comfort to her children, especially those who suffer and bear the cross; this comfort is not from her own resources, but is the gift of the Holy Spirit who dwells in her... therefore the Lord says, “so will I comfort you” [3].

As for the men of the Old Testament, they found their comfort in Jerusalem in two respects: that they had returned from captivity, and that God dwells in their midst. But in the New Testament the Holy Spirit gives us His consolations in victory over the enemy who shatters our freedom, and in our being accepted as a dwelling for the Holy Trinity.

“And when ye see this, your heart shall rejoice, and your bones shall flourish like an herb: and the hand of the LORD shall be known toward his servants, and his indignation toward his enemies” [14]. We see the Cross, for in it life appeared, and the hand of the Lord is known, that is, the person of the Lord Christ is revealed as the hand of the Father... for by Him the love of God the Father was practically accomplished through the sacrifice of the Cross. In the Church we enjoy this, so our hearts rejoice with gladness, and the bones of our faith flourish. This is our comfort in the Lord through His Church: He gives us the joy of the heavenly heart and its enlargement with love, and He causes our faith to grow (the bones being the center of the body).

e. A source of purity: “They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the gardens behind one tree in the midst, eating swine's flesh, and the abomination, and the mouse, shall be consumed together, saith the LORD” [17]; “as the children of Israel bring an offering in a clean vessel into the house of the LORD” [20].
f. She declares the glory of God among the Gentiles [18-20].
g. A priestly city: “And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the LORD” [21].
h. An eternal city: “so shall your seed and your name remain” [22].
i. A people perpetually in worship: “And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD” [23].

j. Among them there is no one perishing... rather, perdition is accomplished outside the true Jerusalem. “And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh” [24].
